children.translated_text: Dawn, indeed, is the head of the sacrificial horse.

children.text: sūryaś cakṣur vātaḥ prāṇo vyāttam agnir vaiśvānaraḥ saṃvatsara ātmāśvasya medhyasya
children.translated_text: The sun is its eye, wind its breath, its opened mouth is <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>, and the year is the self of the sacrificial horse.

children.text: dyauḥ pṛṣṭham antarikṣam udaraṃ pṛthivī pājasyaṃ diśaḥ pārśve avāntaradiśaḥ parśava ṛtavo 'ṅgāni māsāś cārdhamāsāś ca parvāṇy ahorātrāṇi pratiṣṭhā nakṣatrāṇy asthīni nabho māṃsāni
children.translated_text: Heaven is its back, the midspace its belly, earth its lower part; the directions are its sides, the intermediate directions its ribs, the seasons its limbs, the months and half-months its joints, days and nights its footing, the stars its bones, and the clouds its flesh.

children.text: ūvadhyaṃ sikatāḥ sindhavo gudā yakṛcca klomānaś ca parvatā oṣadhayaś ca vanaspatayaś ca lomāni
children.translated_text: The sand is the food in its belly, the rivers its bowels, the mountains its liver and lungs, and herbs and trees its hairs.
The rising sun is its forepart; the setting sun is its hindpart.
When it yawns, then lightning flashes.
When it shakes itself, then thunder sounds.
When it urinates, then it rains.
Speech itself is its speech.
Day, as a <s>mahiman</s> (greatness), was born before the horse.
Its womb is in the eastern ocean.
Night, as a <s>mahiman</s>, was born behind it.
Its womb is in the western ocean.

children.text: etau vā aśvaṃ mahimānāv abhitaḥ saṃbabhūvatuḥ
children.translated_text: These two <s>mahimans</s> came into being on both sides of the horse.

children.text: hayo bhūtvā devān avahad vājī gandharvān arvāsurān aśvo manuṣyān
children.translated_text: Becoming <s>haya</s>, it carried the gods; as <s>vājī</s>, the gandharvas; as <s>arvā</s>, the asuras; as <s>aśva</s>, human beings.
The ocean indeed is its kinsman; the ocean is its womb.
In the beginning there was nothing whatsoever here.
This was covered by death, by hunger.
For hunger is death.
It made mind for itself, thinking, "May I become possessed of a self."
Worshipping, it moved about.
As it worshipped, waters were born.

children.text: arcate vai me kam abhūd iti
children.translated_text: It thought, "While I worship, refreshment has arisen for me."
That indeed is the <s>arka</s>-nature of <s>arka</s>.

children.text: kaṃ ha vā asmai bhavati ya evam etad arkasyārkatvaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Refreshment comes to the one who knows this <s>arka</s>-nature of <s>arka</s> in this way.
The waters, indeed, are <s>arka</s>.

children.text: tad yad apāṃ śara āsīt tat samahanyata
children.translated_text: What was the foam of the waters became solid.
That became the earth.
Upon it he wearied himself.
From him, wearied and heated, the essence of heat came forth as fire.

children.text: sa tredhātmānaṃ vyakurutādityaṃ tṛtīyaṃ vāyuṃ tṛtīyam
children.translated_text: He divided himself threefold: one third as the sun, one third as wind.
This <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) is arranged in three ways.

children.text: tasya prācī dik śiro 'sau cāsau cermau
children.translated_text: Its eastern direction is the head; those two quarters are its two foreparts.

children.text: athāsya pratīcī dik puccham asau cāsau ca sakthyau
children.translated_text: Then its western direction is the tail; those two quarters are its two hind parts.
The southern and northern directions are its two sides.

children.text: dyauḥ pṛṣṭham antarikṣam udaram iyam uraḥ
children.translated_text: Heaven is its back, the midspace its belly, and this earth its breast.
This one is established upon the waters.

children.text: yatra kvacaiti tad eva pratitiṣṭhaty evaṃ vidvān ||
children.translated_text: Wherever he goes, there he becomes firmly established, the one who knows thus.
He desired, "Let a second self be born from me."

children.text: sa manasā vācaṃ mithunaṃ samabhavad aśanāyāṃ mṛtyuḥ
children.translated_text: With mind he brought speech into union as a pair; he was hunger, death.

children.text: tad yad reta āsīt sa saṃvatsaro 'bhavat
children.translated_text: What was his seed became the year.

children.text: na ha purā tataḥ saṃvatsara āsa
children.translated_text: Before that there had not been a year.

children.text: tam etāvantaṃ kālam abibhar yāvān saṃvatsaraḥ
children.translated_text: He bore it for as much time as a year lasts.
After that span of time he emitted it.
When it was born, he opened his mouth over it.
It made the sound "bhāṇ."
That itself became speech.

children.text: sa aikṣata yadi vā imam abhimaṃsye kanīyo 'nnaṃ kariṣya iti
children.translated_text: He considered, "If I kill this one, I shall make only scant food."

children.text: sa tayā vācā tenātmanedaṃ sarvam asṛjata yad idaṃ kiñca ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni chandāṃsi yajñān prajāṃ paśūn
children.translated_text: With that speech and with that self he created all this, whatever there is: Ṛg verses, Yajus formulas, Sāman chants, metres, sacrifices, offspring, and cattle.

children.text: sa yadyad evāsṛjata tattad attum adhriyata
children.translated_text: Whatever he created, he set himself to eat that very thing.

children.text: sarvaṃ vā attīti tad aditer adititvam
children.translated_text: Because he eats everything, that is the <s>Aditi</s>-nature of <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text: sarvasyāttā bhavati sarvam asyānnaṃ bhavati ya evam etad aditer adititvaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: One becomes the eater of all, and everything becomes food for him, who knows this <s>Aditi</s>-nature of <s>Aditi</s> in this way.
He desired, "May I sacrifice again with a greater sacrifice."
He wearied himself.
He performed austerity.

children.text: tasya śrāntasya taptasya yaśo vīryam udakrāmat
children.translated_text: From him, wearied and heated, fame and vigor departed.
The <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) are fame and vigor.
When the <s>prāṇas</s> had departed, the body began to swell.
His mind was in the body itself.

children.text: so 'kāmayata medhyaṃ ma idaṃ syād ātmanvy anena syām iti
children.translated_text: He desired, "May this be fit for sacrifice for me; may I become possessed of self through it."
Then it became a horse.

children.text: yad aśvat tan medhyam abhūd iti tad evāśvamedhasyāśvamedhatvam
children.translated_text: Because it swelled, it became fit for sacrifice; that indeed is the <s>aśvamedha</s>-nature of the <s>aśvamedha</s>.

children.text: eṣa ha vā aśvamedhaṃ veda ya enam evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He knows the <s>aśvamedha</s> who knows it in this way.
He regarded it as something to be left unconfined.
After a year he sacrificed it for himself.
He assigned the animals to the deities.
Therefore they sacrifice the consecrated <s>Prājāpatya</s> animal, belonging to all the deities.

children.text: eṣa vā aśvamedho ya eṣa tapati
children.translated_text: This indeed is the <s>aśvamedha</s>: this one that burns.
The year is its self.
This fire is <s>arka</s>.
These worlds are its selves.
These two, then, are <s>arka</s> and <s>aśvamedha</s>.

children.text: so punar ekaiva devatā bhavati mṛtyur eva
children.translated_text: Again it becomes one deity alone: death itself.
He conquers repeated death.
Death does not reach him.
Death becomes his self.
He attains the full span of life.
He becomes one among these deities.

children.text: dvayā ha prājāpatyā devāś cāsurāś ca tataḥ kānīyasā eva devā jyāyasā asurāḥ
children.translated_text: There were two kinds of descendants of <s>Prajāpati</s>: the gods and the asuras. Of these, the gods were the younger and the asuras the older.
They contended with one another in these worlds.

children.text: te ha devā ūcur hantāsurān yajña udgīthenātyayāmeti ||
children.translated_text: The gods said, "Come, let us overcome the asuras in the sacrifice by means of the <s>udgītha</s>."

children.text: te ha vācam ūcus tvaṃ na udgāyeti
children.translated_text: They said to speech, "Sing the <s>udgītha</s> for us."
"So be it," speech replied, and sang the <s>udgītha</s> for them.

children.text: yo vāci bhogas taṃ devebhya āgāyat
children.translated_text: Whatever enjoyment there is in speech, that it sang for the gods.
Whatever fine thing it speaks, that was for itself.
They knew, "By this singer they will overcome us."
Having rushed upon it, they pierced it with evil.

children.text: sa yaḥ sa pāpmā yad evedam apratirūpaṃ vadati
children.translated_text: That evil is this very thing: when one speaks what is improper.
That indeed is that evil.

children.text: atha ha prāṇam ūcus tvaṃ na udgāyeti
children.translated_text: Then they said to <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), "Sing the <s>udgītha</s> for us."
"So be it," <s>prāṇa</s> replied, and sang the <s>udgītha</s> for them.

children.text: yaḥ prāṇe bhogas taṃ devebhya āgāyat
children.translated_text: Whatever enjoyment there is in <s>prāṇa</s>, that it sang for the gods.
Whatever good thing one smells, that was for itself.
They knew, "By this singer they will overcome us."
They rushed upon it and pierced it with evil.

children.text: sa yaḥ sa pāpmā yad evedam apratirūpaṃ jighrati
children.translated_text: That evil is just this: that one smells what is improper.
That indeed is that evil.

children.text: atha ha cakṣur ūcus tvaṃ na udgāyeti
children.translated_text: Then they said to the eye, "Sing for us."
"So be it," and the eye sang for them.

children.text: yaś cakṣuṣi bhogas taṃ devebhya āgāyat
children.translated_text: Whatever enjoyment is in the eye, that it sang for the gods.
Whatever good it sees, that was for itself.
They realized, "Surely with this singer they will get beyond us."
They rushed upon it and pierced it with evil.

children.text: sa yaḥ sa pāpmā yad evedam apratirūpaṃ paśyati
children.translated_text: That evil is just this: that one sees what is improper.
That indeed is that evil.

children.text: atha ha śrotram ūcus tvaṃ na udgāyeti
children.translated_text: Then they said to hearing, "Sing for us."
"So be it," and hearing sang for them.

children.text: yaḥ śrotre bhogas taṃ devebhya āgāyat
children.translated_text: Whatever enjoyment is in hearing, that it sang for the gods.
Whatever good it hears, that was for itself.
They realized, "Surely with this singer they will get beyond us."
They rushed upon it and pierced it with evil.
That evil is this:
that one hears what is improper.
That indeed is that evil.

children.text: atha ha mana ūcus tvaṃ na udgāyeti
children.translated_text: Then they said to the mind, "Sing for us."
"So be it," and the mind sang for them.

children.text: yo manasi bhogas taṃ devebhya āgāyat
children.translated_text: Whatever enjoyment is in the mind, that it sang for the gods.
Whatever good it intends, that was for itself.
They realized, "Surely with this singer they will get beyond us."
They rushed upon it and pierced it with evil.
That evil is this:
that one intends what is improper.
That indeed is that evil.

children.text: evam u khalv etā devatāḥ pāpmabhir upāsṛjan
children.translated_text: In just this way, then, they assailed these deities with evils.
In just this way they pierced them with evil.

children.text: atha hemam āsanyaṃ prāṇam ūcus tvaṃ na udgāyeti
children.translated_text: Then they said to this <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) in the mouth, "Sing for us."
"So be it," and this <s>prāṇa</s> sang for them.
They realized, "Surely with this singer they will get beyond us."
They rushed upon it, wishing to pierce it with evil.

children.text: sa yathāśmānam ṛtvā loṣṭo vidhvaṃsetaivaṃ haiva vidhvaṃsamānā viṣvañco vineśuḥ
children.translated_text: Just as a clod, striking a stone, would be shattered, so indeed they, being shattered, perished in every direction.
Then the gods prevailed, and the asuras were defeated.

children.text: bhavaty ātmanā parāsya dviṣan bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: One becomes oneself, and one's hateful rival is defeated, whoever knows thus.

children.text: te hocuḥ kva nu so 'bhūd yo na ittham asakteti
children.translated_text: They said, "Where, then, was he who attached himself to us in this way?"
"Here, inside the mouth," they said.
He is <s>Ayāsya Āṅgirasa</s>, for he is the essence of the limbs.

children.text: sā vā eṣā devatā dūr nāma
children.translated_text: This deity indeed is named <s>Dūr</s>.
For death is far from it.

children.text: dūraṃ ha vā asmān mṛtyur bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Death indeed becomes far from one who knows thus.

children.text: sā vā eṣā devataitāsāṃ devatānāṃ pāpmānaṃ mṛtyum apahatya yatrāsāṃ diśām antas tad gamayāṃcakāra
children.translated_text: This deity, having struck away the evil, death, from these deities, caused it to go to the ends of the directions.
There it deposited their evil.

children.text: tasmān na janam iyān nāntam iyān net pāpmānaṃ mṛtyum anvavāyānīti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should not go to a person, nor should one go to the end, lest one come upon evil, death.

children.text: sā vā eṣā devataitāsāṃ devatānāṃ pāpmānaṃ mṛtyum apahatyāthainā mṛtyum atyavahat ||
children.translated_text: This deity indeed, having struck away the evil, death, from these deities, then carried them beyond death.

children.text: sā vai vācam eva prathamām atyavahat
children.translated_text: It first carried speech beyond.

children.text: sā yadā mṛtyum atyamucyata so 'gnir abhavat
children.translated_text: When speech was released beyond death, it became <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: so 'yam agniḥ pareṇa mṛtyum atikrānto dīpyate ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Agni</s>, having crossed beyond death, shines.
Then it carried <s>prāṇa</s> beyond.

children.text: sa yadā mṛtyum atyamucyata sa vāyur abhavat
children.translated_text: When it was released beyond death, it became <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: so 'yaṃ vāyuḥ pareṇa mṛtyum atikrāntaḥ pavate ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Vāyu</s>, having crossed beyond death, blows.
Then it carried the eye beyond.

children.text: tad yadā mṛtyum atyamucyata sa ādityo 'bhavat
children.translated_text: When it was released beyond death, it became <s>Āditya</s>.

children.text: so 'sāv ādityaḥ pareṇa mṛtyum atikrāntas tapati ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Āditya</s>, having crossed beyond death, gives heat.
Then it carried hearing beyond.

children.text: tad yadā mṛtyum atyamucyata tā diśo 'bhavan
children.translated_text: When it was released beyond death, it became the directions.

children.text: tā imā diśaḥ pareṇa mṛtyum atikrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These directions, having crossed beyond death, remain.
Then it carried the mind beyond.

children.text: tad yadā mṛtyum atyamucyata sa candramā abhavat
children.translated_text: When it was released beyond death, it became <s>Candra</s>.

children.text: so 'sau candraḥ pareṇa mṛtyum atikrānto bhāti
children.translated_text: That <s>Candra</s>, having crossed beyond death, shines.

children.text: evaṃ ha vā enam eṣā devatā mṛtyum ativahati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed this deity carries beyond death the one who knows thus.
Then it sang food to be eaten for itself.
For whatever food is eaten is eaten through this alone.
It is established here.
The gods said:

children.text: etāvad vā idaṃ sarvaṃ yad annam
children.translated_text: "All this, surely, is only so much as food.
You have sung that for yourself.
Share us in this food."
"Then enter into me," it said.
"So be it," and they entered around it on every side.

children.text: tasmād yad anenānnam atti tenaitās tṛpyanti
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever food one eats through this, by that these are satisfied.

children.text: evaṃ ha vā enaṃ svā abhisaṃviśanti bhartā svānāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ puraetā bhavaty annādo 'dhipatir ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: Thus one's own people enter around him; he becomes the supporter of his own, the best, the leader, an eater of food and an overlord, whoever knows thus.

children.text: ya u haivaṃvidaṃ sveṣu pratipatir bubhūṣati na haivālaṃ bhāryebhyo bhavati
children.translated_text: If someone among his own wishes to become a rival of one who knows thus, he is not able to support his dependents.

children.text: atha ya evaitam anubhavati yo vaitam anu bhāryān bubhūrṣati sa haivālaṃ bhāryebhyo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: But whoever follows him, or whoever after him wishes to support dependents, he indeed is able to support his dependents.
He is <s>Ayāsya Āṅgirasa</s>, for he is the essence of the limbs.
<s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed the essence of the limbs.
For <s>prāṇa</s> is indeed the essence of the limbs.

children.text: tasmād yasmāt kasmāccāṅgāt prāṇa utkrāmati tad eva tacchuṣyati
children.translated_text: Therefore, from whatever limb <s>prāṇa</s> departs, that very limb dries up.
For this indeed is the essence of the limbs.
This indeed is <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
Speech is the <s>bṛhatī</s>.

children.text: tasyā eṣa patis tasmād u bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is her lord; therefore he is <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
This indeed is <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>.
Speech is <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: tasyā eṣa patis tasmād u brahmaṇaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is her lord; therefore he is <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>.
This indeed is the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: vāg vai sāmaiṣa sā cāmaś ceti tat sāmnaḥ sāmatvam
children.translated_text: Speech is "sā," and this is "ama"; this is the <s>sāman</s>-nature of the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: yadveva samaḥ pluṣiṇā samo maśakena samo nāgena sama ebhis tribhir lokaiḥ samo 'nena sarveṇa tasmādveva sāma
children.translated_text: Or else, because he is equal with a termite, equal with a mosquito, equal with an elephant, equal with these three worlds, and equal with all this, therefore indeed he is the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: aśnute sāmnaḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatām ya evam etat sāma veda ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows this <s>sāman</s> thus obtains union with the <s>sāman</s> and dwelling in the same world as it.
This indeed is the <s>udgītha</s>.

children.text: prāṇo vā ut prāṇena hīdaṃ sarvam uttabdham
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed "ut," for by <s>prāṇa</s> all this is upheld.
Speech alone is the "gīthā."
Because it is "ut" and "gīthā," it is the <s>udgītha</s>.

children.text: taddhāpi brahmadattaś caikitāneyo rājānaṃ bhakṣayann uvāca
children.translated_text: Indeed, <s>Brahmadatta Caikitāneya</s>, while partaking of the king, said this:

children.text: ayaṃ tyasya rājā mūrdhānaṃ vipātayatād yad ito 'yāsya āṅgiraso 'nyenodagāyad iti
children.translated_text: "May this king make that man's head fall off if <s>Ayāsya Āṅgirasa</s> sang the <s>udgītha</s> with anything other than this."

children.text: vācā ca hy eva sa prāṇena codagāyad iti ||
children.translated_text: For he sang the <s>udgītha</s> with speech and with <s>prāṇa</s> alone.

children.text: tasya haitasya sāmno yaḥ svaṃ veda bhavati hāsya svam
children.translated_text: Of this <s>sāman</s>, whoever knows its own property, his own property indeed comes to be.
Its own property is indeed the tone.

children.text: tasmād ārtvijyaṃ kariṣyan vāci svaram iccheta
children.translated_text: Therefore one who is going to perform priestly service should seek tone in speech.
With that speech, endowed with tone, he should perform the priestly service.
Therefore in a sacrifice they desire to see one possessed of tone.
And also, for one whose own property exists,

children.text: bhavati hāsya svaṃ ya evam etat sāmnaḥ svaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: his own property indeed comes to be, whoever knows this own property of the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: tasya haitasya sāmno yaḥ suvarṇaṃ veda bhavati hāsya suvarṇam
children.translated_text: Of this <s>sāman</s>, whoever knows its gold, his gold indeed comes to be.
Its gold is indeed the tone.

children.text: bhavati hāsya suvarṇaṃ ya evam etat sāmnaḥ suvarṇaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: His gold indeed comes to be, whoever knows this gold of the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: tasya haitasya sāmno yaḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ veda prati ha tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: Of this <s>sāman</s>, whoever knows its foundation, he stands firmly.
Its foundation is indeed speech.

children.text: vāci hi khalv eṣa etat prāṇaḥ pratiṣṭhito gīyate
children.translated_text: For on speech, surely, this <s>prāṇa</s> is established and is sung.
Some say, however, that it is on food.
Now then, there is the ascent of the <s>pavamāna</s> chants.

children.text: sa vai khalu prastotā sāma prastauti
children.translated_text: The <s>prastotṛ</s>, surely, begins the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: sa yatra prastuyāt tad etāni japet
children.translated_text: When he begins it, then one should murmur these words:

children.text: asato mā sad gamaya tamaso mā jyotir gamaya mṛtyor māmṛtaṃ gamayeti
children.translated_text: "Lead me from the unreal to the real; lead me from darkness to light; lead me from death to immortality."

children.text: sa yad āhāsato mā sad gamayeti
children.translated_text: When he says, "Lead me from the unreal to the real,"

children.text: mṛtyur vā asat sad amṛtaṃ mṛtyor māmṛtaṃ gamayāmṛtaṃ mā kurv ity evaitad āha
children.translated_text: death indeed is the unreal, and the real is immortality; by saying, "Lead me from death to immortality," he says just this: "Make me immortal."
When he says, "Lead me from darkness to light,"

children.text: mṛtyur vai tamo jyotir amṛtaṃ mṛtyor māmṛtaṃ gamayāmṛtaṃ mā kurv ity evaitad āha
children.translated_text: death indeed is darkness, and light is immortality; by saying, "Lead me from death to immortality," he says just this: "Make me immortal."
When he says, "Lead me from death to immortality,"
there is nothing here, as it were, concealed.

children.text: atha yānītarāṇi stotrāṇi teṣv ātmane 'nnādyam āgāyet
children.translated_text: Then, in the other hymns of praise, he should sing food to be eaten for himself.
Therefore in them he should choose a boon,
whatever desire he may desire.

children.text: sa eṣa evaṃvid udgātātmane vā yajamānāya vā yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate tam āgāyati
children.translated_text: An <s>udgātṛ</s> who knows thus sings that desire for himself or for the sacrificer, whatever desire he desires.
This indeed is a winner of worlds.

children.text: na haivālokyatāyā āśāsti ya evam etat sāma veda ||
children.translated_text: For one who knows this <s>sāman</s> thus has no anxiety about not obtaining a world.
In the beginning this was just the self, in the form of a person.
Looking around, he saw nothing other than himself.
At first he uttered, "I am."
From that he became named "I."

children.text: tasmād apy etarhy āmantrito 'ham ayam ity evāgra uktvāthānyan nāma prabrūte yad asya bhavati
children.translated_text: Therefore even now, when addressed, one first says, "It is I," and then states whatever other name he has.

children.text: sa yat pūrvo 'smāt sarvasmāt sarvān pāpmana auṣat tasmāt puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Because he, being prior to all this, burned away all evils, therefore he is the person.

children.text: oṣati ha vai sa taṃ yo 'smāt pūrvo bubhūṣati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He indeed burns up the one who wishes to be before him, whoever knows thus.
He was afraid; therefore one who is alone is afraid.

children.text: sa hāyam īkṣāṃcakre yan mad anyan nāsti kasmān nu bibhemīti
children.translated_text: He reflected: "Since there is nothing other than me, of what should I be afraid?"
Then his fear departed at once.
For of what should he have been afraid?
Fear comes, indeed, from a second.
He, indeed, did not delight.
Therefore one who is alone does not delight.
He desired a second.

children.text: sa haitāvān āsa yathā strīpumāṃsau sampariṣvaktau
children.translated_text: He was of this size, like a woman and a man closely embracing.
He split this very self in two.
From that husband and wife came into being.

children.text: tasmād idam ardhabṛgalam iva sva iti ha smāha yājñavalkyaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore this self is like one half of a split pea, so <s>Yājñavalkya</s> used to say.

children.text: tasmād ayam ākāśaḥ striyā pūryata eva
children.translated_text: Therefore this space is filled by a woman.
He united with her.
From that human beings were born.

children.text: so heyam īkṣāṃcakre kathaṃ nu mātmana eva janayitvā sambhavati
children.translated_text: She reflected: "How can he unite with me after producing me from himself?"
"Well then, let me hide."
She became a cow; the other became a bull.
He united with her there too.
From that cattle were born.
The one became a mare; the other became a stallion.
The one became a she-ass; the other became a male ass.
He united with her there too.
From that the one-hoofed animals were born.
The one became a she-goat; the other became a buck.
The one became a ewe; the other became a ram.
He united with her there too.
From that goats and sheep were born.

children.text: evam eva yad idaṃ kiñca mithunam ā pipīlikābhyas tat sarvam asṛjata ||
children.translated_text: In this very way he created all that exists here as a pair, down to the ants.

children.text: so 'ved ahaṃ vāva sṛṣṭir asmy ahaṃ hīdaṃ sarvam asṛkṣīti
children.translated_text: He knew: "I truly am creation, for I have created all this."
From that he became creation.

children.text: sṛṣṭyāṃ hāsyaitasyāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows thus comes to be in this creation of his.
Then he rubbed thus.

children.text: sa mukhāc ca yoner hastābhyāṃ cāgnim asṛjata
children.translated_text: From his mouth as the womb, and with his hands, he created <s>Agni</s>.
Therefore both of these are hairless on the inside.
For the womb is hairless on the inside.

children.text: tad yad idam āhur amuṃ yajāmuṃ yajety ekaikaṃ devam etasyaiva sā visṛṣṭiḥ
children.translated_text: When people say, "Sacrifice to this one, sacrifice to that one," each individual god is just this emanation of his.

children.text: eṣa u hy eva sarve devāḥ
children.translated_text: For he indeed is all the gods.

children.text: atha yat kiñcedam ārdraṃ tad retaso 'sṛjata
children.translated_text: Then whatever here is moist he created from semen.
That indeed is <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: etāvad vā idaṃ sarvam annaṃ caivānnādaś ca
children.translated_text: All this is just so much: food and the eater of food.
<s>Soma</s> indeed is food, and <s>Agni</s> is the eater of food.
This is the surpassing creation of <s>Brahman</s>:

children.text: yacchreyaso devān asṛjatātha yan martyaḥ sann amṛtān asṛjata tasmād atisṛṣṭiḥ
children.translated_text: that he created the gods, who are superior, and that, though mortal, he created immortals; therefore it is a surpassing creation.

children.text: atisṛṣṭyāṃ hāsyaitasyāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows thus comes to be in this surpassing creation of his.
This, then, at that time was undifferentiated.

children.text: tan nāmarūpābhyām eva vyākriyatāsau nāmāyam idaṃrūpa iti
children.translated_text: It was differentiated only by name and form: "This one has such a name; this has such a form."

children.text: tad idam apy etarhi nāmarūpābhyām eva vyākriyata asau nāmāyam idaṃrūpa iti
children.translated_text: This, even now, is differentiated only by name and form: "This one has such a name; this has such a form."

children.text: sa eṣa iha praviṣṭa ā nakhāgrebhyo yathā kṣuraḥ kṣuradhāne 'vahitaḥ syād viśvambharo vā viśvambharakulāye
children.translated_text: This same one has entered here, right to the tips of the nails, as a razor might be placed in a razor-case, or as the all-sustainer in the nest of the all-sustainer.
They do not see him.

children.text: akṛtsno hi saḥ prāṇann eva prāṇo nāma bhavati
children.translated_text: For he is incomplete: when breathing, he is called <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: vadan vāk paśyaṃś cakṣuḥ śṛṇvañchrotraṃ manvāno manaḥ
children.translated_text: When speaking, he is speech; when seeing, the eye; when hearing, the ear; when thinking, the mind.
These are merely names of his actions.

children.text: sa yo 'ta ekaikam upāste na sa veda
children.translated_text: Whoever worships one single one of these does not know.
For by any single one of these he is incomplete.
One should worship him only as <s>ātmā</s>.

children.text: atra hy ete sarva ekaṃ bhavanti
children.translated_text: For in this all these become one.

children.text: tad etat padanīyam asya sarvasya yad ayam ātmā
children.translated_text: This is the track to be followed of all this, namely this <s>ātmā</s>.
For through this one knows all this.

children.text: yathā ha vai padenānuvinded evaṃ kīrtiṃ ślokaṃ vindate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Just as one would find something by its track, so one finds fame and praise, whoever knows thus.

children.text: tad etat preyaḥ putrāt preyo vittāt preyo 'nyasmāt sarvasmād antarataraṃ yad ayam ātmā
children.translated_text: This, this <s>ātmā</s>, is dearer than a son, dearer than wealth, dearer than anything else, and more inward than all.

children.text: sa yo 'nyam ātmanaḥ priyaṃ bruvāṇaṃ brūyāt priyaṃ rotsyatītīśvaro ha tathaiva syāt
children.translated_text: If one were to say to a person who declares something other than the self to be dear, 'What is dear to you will perish,' it would indeed be liable to happen just so.
One should worship the <s>ātmā</s> alone as dear.

children.text: sa ya ātmānam eva priyam upāste na hāsya priyaṃ pramāyukaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For the one who worships the <s>ātmā</s> alone as dear, what is dear to him does not perish.

children.text: tad āhur yad brahmavidyayā sarvaṃ bhaviṣyanto manuṣyā manyante
children.translated_text: They say, 'Since people think that by knowledge of <s>brahman</s> they will become everything,

children.text: kim u tad brahmāved yasmāt tat sarvam abhavad iti ||
children.translated_text: what did that <s>brahman</s> know, by which it became all this?'
In the beginning this was indeed <s>brahman</s>.
It knew only itself:
'I am <s>brahman</s>.'
Therefore it became all this.

children.text: tad yo yo devānāṃ pratyabudhyata sa eva tad abhavat
children.translated_text: Whichever of the gods awakened to this became that very thing.
So too among the seers,
and so too among human beings.

children.text: taddhaitat paśyann ṛṣir vāmadevaḥ pratipede 'haṃ manur abhavaṃ sūryaś ceti
children.translated_text: Seeing this, the seer <s>Vāmadeva</s> realized, 'I became <s>Manu</s> and the <s>Sūrya</s>.'

children.text: tad idam apy etarhi ya evaṃ vedāhaṃ brahmāsmīti sa idaṃ sarvaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: So even now, whoever knows thus, 'I am <s>brahman</s>,' becomes this whole world.

children.text: tasya ha na devāś canābhūtyā īśate
children.translated_text: Not even the gods have power to prevent his becoming so.
For he becomes their <s>ātmā</s>.

children.text: atha yo 'nyāṃ devatām upāste 'nyo 'sāvanyo 'ham asmīti na sa veda
children.translated_text: But whoever worships another deity, thinking, 'That one is different, and I am different,' does not know.
He is like an animal for the gods.

children.text: yathā ha vai bahavaḥ paśavo manuṣyaṃ bhuñjyur evam ekaikaḥ puruṣo devān bhunakti
children.translated_text: Just as many animals serve a human being, so each single person serves the gods.

children.text: ekasminn eva paśāv ādīyamāne 'priyaṃ bhavati kimu bahuṣu
children.translated_text: When even one animal is taken away, it is unpleasant; how much more when many are taken.

children.text: tasmād eṣāṃ tan na priyaṃ yad etan manuṣyā vidyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it is not dear to them that human beings should know this.

children.text: brahma vā idam agra āsīd ekam eva
children.translated_text: In the beginning this was indeed <s>brahman</s>, one alone.
Being one, it did not flourish.

children.text: tacchreyo rūpam atyasṛjata kṣatraṃ yāny etāni devatrā kṣatrāṇīndro varuṇaḥ somo rudraḥ parjanyo yamo mṛtyur īśāna iti
children.translated_text: It created a superior form: <s>kṣatra</s>, those ruling powers among the gods, namely <s>Indra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Mṛtyu</s>, and <s>Īśāna</s>.
Therefore there is nothing higher than <s>kṣatra</s>.

children.text: tasmād brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyaṃ adhastād upāste rājasūye
children.translated_text: Therefore, at the <s>rājasūya</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> sits below the <s>kṣatriya</s> and worships him.
He thereby places glory in <s>kṣatra</s> itself.
This <s>brahman</s> is the womb of <s>kṣatra</s>.

children.text: tasmād yady api rājā paramatāṃ gacchati brahmaivāntata upaniśrayati svāṃ yonim
children.translated_text: Therefore, even if a king attains the highest rank, in the end he takes refuge in <s>brahman</s> itself, his own womb.

children.text: ya u enaṃ hinasti svāṃ sa yonim ṛcchati
children.translated_text: Whoever injures him strikes at his own womb.

children.text: sa pāpīyān bhavati yathā śreyāṃsaṃ hiṃsitvā ||
children.translated_text: He becomes worse, just as one becomes worse after injuring a superior.
It still did not flourish.
It created the <s>viś</s>, the common people.

children.text: yāny etāni devajātāni gaṇaśa ākhyāyante vasavo rudrā ādityā viśve devā maruta iti ||
children.translated_text: These divine groups are named collectively: the <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s>, and <s>Maruts</s>.
It still did not flourish.
It created the <s>śaudra</s> order, <s>Pūṣan</s>.
This earth is indeed <s>Pūṣan</s>.

children.text: iyaṃ hīdaṃ sarvaṃ puṣyati yad idaṃ kiñca ||
children.translated_text: For this earth nourishes all this, whatever there is here.
It still did not flourish.
It created a superior form: <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tad etat kṣatrasya kṣatraṃ yad dharmaḥ
children.translated_text: This <s>dharma</s> is the ruling power of ruling power.
Therefore there is nothing higher than <s>dharma</s>.
And so a weaker man hopes to overcome a stronger man by means of <s>dharma</s>,
just as through a king.

children.text: yo vai sa dharmaḥ satyaṃ vai tat
children.translated_text: That which is <s>dharma</s> is indeed truth.

children.text: tasmāt satyaṃ vadantam āhur dharmaṃ vadatīti
children.translated_text: Therefore, when someone speaks truth, they say, 'He speaks <s>dharma</s>.'
Or when someone speaks <s>dharma</s>, they say, 'He speaks truth.'
For both of these are just this same thing.

children.text: tad etad brahma kṣatraṃ viṭ śūdraḥ
children.translated_text: This, then, is <s>brahman</s>, <s>kṣatra</s>, <s>viṭ</s>, and <s>śūdra</s>.

children.text: tad agninaiva deveṣu brahmābhavad brāhmaṇo manuṣyeṣu kṣatriyeṇa kṣatriyaḥ vaiśyena vaiśyaḥ śūdreṇa śūdraḥ
children.translated_text: Among the gods it became <s>brahman</s> only through <s>Agni</s>; among human beings, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; through the <s>kṣatriya</s>, a <s>kṣatriya</s>; through the <s>vaiśya</s>, a <s>vaiśya</s>; and through the <s>śūdra</s>, a <s>śūdra</s>.

children.text: tasmād agnāv eva deveṣu lokam icchante brāhmaṇe manuṣyeṣu
children.translated_text: Therefore among the gods they seek a world in <s>Agni</s>, and among human beings in a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
For by these two forms it became <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: atha yo ha vā asmāl lokāt svaṃ lokam adṛṣṭvā praiti sa enam avidito na bhunakti yathā vedo vānanūkto 'nyad vā karmākṛtam
children.translated_text: But whoever departs from this world without having seen his own world, that world, being unknown, does not benefit him, like a Veda not recited or some act not performed.

children.text: yadi ha vā apy anevaṃvin mahatpuṇyaṃ karma karoti taddhāsyāntataḥ kṣīyata eva
children.translated_text: Even if one who does not know in this way performs a deed of great merit, in the end it is surely exhausted for him.
One should worship the <s>ātmā</s> alone as one's world.

children.text: sa ya ātmānam eva lokam upāste na hāsya karma kṣīyate
children.translated_text: For the one who worships the <s>ātmā</s> alone as his world, his work is not exhausted.
For from this very <s>ātmā</s> he creates whatever he desires.

children.text: atho ayaṃ vā ātmā sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ lokaḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, this <s>ātmā</s> is the world of all beings.

children.text: sa yaj juhoti yad yajate tena devānāṃ lokaḥ
children.translated_text: Insofar as he offers in the fire and sacrifices, by that he is the world of the gods.
And insofar as he recites, by that he is the world of the seers.

children.text: atha yat pitṛbhyo nipṛṇāti yat prajām icchate tena pitṝṇām
children.translated_text: And insofar as he makes offerings to the ancestors and desires offspring, by that he is the world of the ancestors.

children.text: atha yan manuṣyān vāsayate yad ebhyo 'śanaṃ dadāti tena manuṣyāṇām
children.translated_text: And insofar as he houses people and gives them food, by that he is the world of human beings.

children.text: atha yat paśubhyas tṛṇodakaṃ vindati tena paśūnām
children.translated_text: And insofar as he finds grass and water for animals, by that he is the world of animals.

children.text: yad asya gṛheṣu śvāpadā vayāṃsy ā pipīlikābhya upajīvanti tena teṣāṃ lokaḥ
children.translated_text: And insofar as wild creatures, birds, and even ants live in his houses, by that he is their world.

children.text: yathā ha vai svāya lokāyāriṣṭim icchet
children.translated_text: Just as one would wish freedom from harm for one's own world,

children.text: evaṃ haivaṃvide sarvadā sarvāṇi bhūtāny ariṣṭim icchanti
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, for one who knows in this way, all beings always desire freedom from harm.
This indeed has been known and carefully considered.
In the beginning this was the <s>ātman</s> (self) alone, one only.

children.text: so 'kāmayata jāyā me syād atha prajāyeya
children.translated_text: It desired: "May I have a wife; then may I produce offspring.

children.text: atha vittaṃ me syād atha karma kurvīyeti
children.translated_text: Then may I have wealth; then may I perform action."
Desire, indeed, is just this much.
Even while desiring, one would not obtain anything more than this.

children.text: tasmād apy etarhy ekākī kāmayate jāyā me syād atha prajāyeyātha vittaṃ me syād atha karma kurvīyeti
children.translated_text: Therefore even now a solitary man desires: "May I have a wife; then may I produce offspring; then may I have wealth; then may I perform action."

children.text: sa yāvad apy eteṣām ekaikaṃ na prāpnoty akṛtsna eva tāvan manyate
children.translated_text: So long as he does not obtain even one of these, he thinks himself incomplete.
Now this is his completeness.
The mind itself is his self.
Speech is his wife.
<s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is his offspring.
The eye is human wealth.
For by the eye he obtains that.
The ear is divine wealth.
For by the ear he hears that.
The self itself is his action.
For by the self he performs action.
This is the fivefold sacrifice.
The animal is fivefold.
The person is fivefold.

children.text: pāṅktam idaṃ sarvaṃ yad idaṃ kiñca
children.translated_text: All this, whatever there is here, is fivefold.

children.text: tad idaṃ sarvam āpnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows thus obtains all this.
The father generated seven foods by insight and austerity.

children.text: ekam asya sādhāraṇaṃ dve devān abhājayat
children.translated_text: One of his was common; two he apportioned to the gods.
Three he made for himself; one he gave to the animals.

children.text: tasmin sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ yacca prāṇiti yacca na
children.translated_text: In that all is established, whatever breathes and whatever does not.

children.text: kasmāt tāni na kṣīyante adyamānāni sarvadā
children.translated_text: Why are those not exhausted, though they are always being eaten?

children.text: yo vai tām akṣitiṃ veda so 'nnam atti pratīkena
children.translated_text: He who knows that inexhaustibility eats food with the mouth.

children.text: sa devān apigacchati sa ūrjam upajīvati
children.translated_text: He reaches the gods; he lives upon vigor.
Thus are the verses.
"The father generated seven foods by insight and austerity":

children.text: medhayā hi tapasājanayat pitaikam asya sādhāraṇam iti
children.translated_text: for the father generated them by insight and austerity. "One of his was common":

children.text: idam evāsya tat sādhāraṇam annaṃ yad idam adyate
children.translated_text: this very common food of his is whatever is eaten here.

children.text: sa ya etad upāste na sa pāpmano vyāvartate
children.translated_text: Whoever worships this does not turn away from evil.
For this is mixed.
"He apportioned two to the gods":
the oblation and the further offering.

children.text: tasmād devebhyo juhvati ca pra ca juhvati
children.translated_text: Therefore they offer to the gods and they make further offerings.
Others say that these are the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices.
Therefore one should not be a mere sacrificer with iṣṭi-offerings.
"He gave one to the animals":
that is milk.

children.text: payo hy evāgre manuṣyāś ca paśavaś copajīvanti
children.translated_text: For at first humans and animals live on milk alone.

children.text: tasmāt kumāraṃ jātaṃ ghṛtaṃ vaivāgre pratilehayanti stanaṃ vānudhāpayanti
children.translated_text: Therefore, when a child is born, at first they make him lick ghee or they put him to the breast.

children.text: atha vatsaṃ jātam āhus tṛṇād iti
children.translated_text: And when a calf is born, they say of it, "It is a grass-eater."

children.text: tasmin sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ yacca prāṇiti yacca neti
children.translated_text: "In that all is established, whatever breathes and whatever does not":

children.text: payasi hīdaṃ sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ yacca prāṇiti yacca na
children.translated_text: for in milk all this is established, whatever breathes and whatever does not.

children.text: tad yad idam āhuḥ saṃvatsaraṃ payasā juhvad apa punarmṛtyuṃ jayatīti
children.translated_text: As to what they say, "By offering with milk for a year one conquers repeated death,"
one should not understand it in that way.

children.text: yad ahar eva juhoti tad ahaḥ punarmṛtyum apajayaty evaṃ vidvān
children.translated_text: On whatever day he offers, on that very day he conquers repeated death, if he knows in this way.
For he gives all food fit to be eaten to the gods.

children.text: kasmāt tāni na kṣīyante adyamānāni sarvadeti
children.translated_text: "Why are those not exhausted, though they are always being eaten?":
The person, indeed, is inexhaustibility.

children.text: sa hīdam annaṃ punaḥ punar janayate
children.translated_text: For he generates this food again and again.
"He who knows that inexhaustibility":
the person, indeed, is inexhaustibility.

children.text: sa hīdam annaṃ dhiyādhiyā janayate karmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: For through thought after thought and through actions he generates this food.
If he did not do this, it would indeed be exhausted.
"He eats food with the mouth":
the mouth is the face; "with the mouth" is what this means.

children.text: sa devān apigacchati sa ūrjam upajīvatīti praśaṃsā ||
children.translated_text: "He reaches the gods; he lives upon vigor": this is praise.

children.text: trīṇy ātmane 'kuruteti mano vācaṃ prāṇaṃ tāny ātmane 'kuruta
children.translated_text: "He made three for himself": he made mind, speech, and <s>prāṇa</s> for himself.

children.text: anyatramanā abhūvaṃ nādarśam anyatramanā abhūvaṃ nāśrauṣam iti manasā hy eva paśyati manasā śṛṇoti
children.translated_text: "I was absent-minded, so I did not see; I was absent-minded, so I did not hear"; for one sees with the mind and hears with the mind.

children.text: kāmaḥ saṃkalpo vicikitsā śraddhāśraddhā dhṛtir adhṛtir hrīr dhīr bhīr ity etat sarvaṃ mana eva
children.translated_text: Desire, resolve, doubt, faith, lack of faith, firmness, lack of firmness, shame, understanding, and fear: all this is simply mind.

children.text: tasmād api pṛṣṭhata upaspṛṣṭo manasā vijānāti
children.translated_text: Therefore even when touched from behind, one knows it with the mind.

children.text: yaḥ kaśca śabdo vāg eva sā
children.translated_text: Whatever sound there is, that is speech itself.

children.text: eṣā hy antaṃ āyattaiṣā hi na
children.translated_text: For this depends on its limit; for this is not otherwise.

children.text: prāṇo 'pāno vyāna udānaḥ samāno 'na ity etat sarvaṃ prāṇa eva
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>vyāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, <s>samāna</s>, and breathing: all this is simply <s>prāṇa</s>.
This self is made of these.
It is made of speech, made of mind, and made of <s>prāṇa</s>.
The three worlds are just these.

children.text: vāg evāyaṃ loko mano 'ntarikṣalokaḥ prāṇo 'sau lokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Speech is this world; mind is the intermediate world; <s>prāṇa</s> is that world.
The three Vedas are just these.

children.text: vāg evargvedo mano yajurvedaḥ prāṇaḥ sāmavedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Speech is the <s>Ṛgveda</s>; mind is the <s>Yajurveda</s>; <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>Sāmaveda</s>.
The gods, the ancestors, and human beings are just these.

children.text: vāg eva devā manaḥ pitaraḥ prāṇo mānuṣyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Speech is the gods; mind is the ancestors; <s>prāṇa</s> is human beings.
Father, mother, and offspring are just these.

children.text: mana eva pitā vāṅ mātā prāṇaḥ prajā ||
children.translated_text: Mind is the father; speech is the mother; <s>prāṇa</s> is the offspring.
The known, what is to be known, and the unknown are just these.

children.text: yat kiñca vijñātaṃ vācas tad rūpam
children.translated_text: Whatever is known has speech as its form.
For speech is known.
Speech, having become that, protects him.

children.text: yat kiñca vijijñāsyaṃ manasas tad rūpam
children.translated_text: Whatever is to be known has mind as its form.
For mind is what is to be known.
Mind, having become that, protects him.
Whatever is unknown has <s>prāṇa</s> as its form.
For <s>prāṇa</s> is unknown.
<s>Prāṇa</s>, having become that, protects him.
Of that speech, earth is the body.
This <s>Agni</s> is its luminous form.

children.text: tad yāvaty eva vāk tāvatī pṛthivī tāvān ayam agniḥ ||
children.translated_text: As far as speech extends, so far extends earth, and so far extends this <s>Agni</s>.
Now of this mind, heaven is the body.
Yonder <s>Āditya</s> is its luminous form.

children.text: tad yāvad eva manas tāvatī dyaus tāvān asāv ādityaḥ
children.translated_text: As far as mind extends, so far extends heaven, and so far extends yonder <s>Āditya</s>.
Those two came together as a pair.
From that <s>prāṇa</s> was born.
It is <s>Indra</s>.
It is this one without a rival.
A second, indeed, is a rival.

children.text: nāsya sapatno bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: No rival belongs to one who knows in this way.
Now waters are the body of this <s>prāṇa</s>.
Its luminous form is yonder <s>Candra</s>.

children.text: tad yāvān eva prāṇas tāvatya āpas tāvān asau candraḥ
children.translated_text: As great as <s>prāṇa</s> is, so great are the waters, and so great is yonder <s>Candra</s>.

children.text: ta ete sarva eva samāḥ sarve 'nantāḥ
children.translated_text: All these indeed are equal; all are infinite.

children.text: sa yo haitān antavata upāste 'ntavantaṃ sa lokaṃ jayati
children.translated_text: He who worships these as finite wins a finite world.

children.text: atha yo haitān anantān upāste 'nantaṃ sa lokaṃ jayati ||
children.translated_text: But he who worships these as infinite wins an infinite world.
This year is <s>Prajāpati</s>, possessing sixteen parts.
Its nights are precisely fifteen parts.
Its sixteenth part is fixed.

children.text: sa rātribhir evā ca pūryate 'pa ca kṣīyate
children.translated_text: By the nights it becomes full and also wanes away.

children.text: so 'māvāsyāṃ rātrim etayā ṣoḍaśyā kalayā sarvam idaṃ prāṇabhṛd anupraviśya tataḥ prātar jāyate
children.translated_text: On the new-moon night, with this sixteenth part, it enters all this that has breath, and then is born in the morning.

children.text: tasmād etāṃ rātriṃ prāṇabhṛtaḥ prāṇaṃ na vicchindyād api kṛkalāsasyaitasyā eva devatāyā apacityai ||
children.translated_text: Therefore on this night one should not cut off the life of anything that has breath, even of a lizard, out of reverence for this very deity.

children.text: yo vai sa saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ ṣoḍaśakālo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam evaṃvit puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: That year, <s>Prajāpati</s>, sixteenfold, is this very person here who knows thus.
His wealth is precisely the fifteen parts.
The self is his sixteenth part.

children.text: sa vittenaivā ca pūryate 'pa ca kṣīyate
children.translated_text: By wealth he becomes full and also diminishes.

children.text: tad etan nabhyaṃ yad ayam ātmā
children.translated_text: This self here is the nave.
Wealth is the rim.

children.text: tasmād yady api sarvajyāniṃ jīyata ātmanā cej jīvati pradhināgād ity evāhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, even if one suffers the loss of everything, if he lives by the self, they say simply, "He has lost only the rim."

children.text: atha trayo vāva lokā manuṣyalokaḥ pitṛloko devaloka iti
children.translated_text: Now there are indeed three worlds: the human world, the world of the fathers, and the world of the gods.

children.text: so 'yaṃ manuṣyalokaḥ putreṇaiva jayyo nānyena karmaṇā
children.translated_text: This human world is to be won by a son alone, not by any other act.
The world of the fathers is won by ritual action.
The world of the gods is won by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge).
The world of the gods is indeed the best of worlds.
Therefore they praise <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge).
Now, then, the transmission.

children.text: yadā praiṣyan manyate 'tha putram āha tvaṃ brahma tvaṃ yajñas tvaṃ loka iti
children.translated_text: When he thinks that he is about to depart, he says to his son, "You are <s>brahman</s>; you are sacrifice; you are the world."

children.text: sa putraḥ pratyāhāhaṃ brahmāhaṃ yajño 'ham loka iti
children.translated_text: The son replies, "I am <s>brahman</s>; I am sacrifice; I am the world."

children.text: yad vai kiñcānūktaṃ tasya sarvasya brahmety ekatā
children.translated_text: Whatever has been recited, of all that <s>brahman</s> is the unity.

children.text: ye vai ke ca yajñās teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ yajña ity ekatā
children.translated_text: Whatever sacrifices there are, of all of them sacrifice is the unity.

children.text: ye vai ke ca lokās teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ loka ity ekatā
children.translated_text: Whatever worlds there are, of all of them world is the unity.
All this is only so much.

children.text: etan mā sarvaṃ sann ayam ito bhunajad iti
children.translated_text: "May this one, being all this, enjoy and sustain it for me from here."
Therefore they call an instructed son fit for the world.
Therefore he instructs him.

children.text: sa yadaivaṃvid asmāl lokāt praity athaibhir eva prāṇaiḥ saha putram āviśati
children.translated_text: When one who knows thus departs from this world, then with these very <s>prāṇas</s> he enters his son.

children.text: sa yady anena kiṃcid akṣṇayā kṛtaṃ bhavati tasmād enaṃ sarvasmāt putro muñcati tasmāt putro nāma
children.translated_text: If anything has been done wrongly by him, from all that the son releases him; therefore he is called son.
Through his son he is established in this world.

children.text: athainam ete devāḥ prāṇā amṛtā āviśanti ||
children.translated_text: Then these immortal divine <s>prāṇas</s> enter him.

children.text: pṛthivyai cainam agneś ca daivī vāg āviśati
children.translated_text: Divine speech, from the earth and from <s>Agni</s>, enters him.

children.text: sā vai daivī vāg yayā yad yad eva vadati tat tad bhavati ||
children.translated_text: That is divine speech, by which whatever he says comes to be just that.

children.text: divaś cainam ādityāc ca daivaṃ mana āviśati
children.translated_text: The divine mind, from heaven and from <s>Āditya</s>, enters him.

children.text: tad vai daivaṃ mano yenānandy eva bhavaty atho na śocati ||
children.translated_text: That is the divine mind by which he becomes joyful, and also does not grieve.

children.text: adbhyaś cainaṃ candramasaś ca daivaḥ prāṇa āviśati
children.translated_text: The divine <s>prāṇa</s>, from the waters and from <s>Candra</s>, enters him.

children.text: sa vai daivaḥ prāṇo yaḥ saṃcaraṃś cāsaṃcaraṃś ca na vyathate 'tho na riṣyati
children.translated_text: That is the divine <s>prāṇa</s> which, moving and not moving, is not distressed and also does not perish.

children.text: sa eṣa evaṃvit sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām ātmā bhavati
children.translated_text: One who knows thus becomes the self of all beings.
As this deity is, so is he.

children.text: yathaitāṃ devatāṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāny avanty evaṃ haivaṃvidaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāny avanti
children.translated_text: As all beings protect this deity, so indeed all beings protect the one who knows thus.

children.text: yad u kiñcemāḥ prajāḥ śocanty amaivāsāṃ tad bhavati
children.translated_text: Whatever these creatures grieve over remains with them alone.
Only merit goes to him.

children.text: na ha vai devān pāpaṃ gacchati ||
children.translated_text: Evil does not go to the gods.
Now, then, the inquiry into the vow.
<s>Prajāpati</s> created the functions.
Once created, they competed with one another.
Speech resolved, "I alone will speak."
The eye resolved, "I will see."
The ear resolved, "I will hear."
So also the other functions, each according to its function.
Death, becoming weariness, seized them.
It reached them.
Having reached them, death held them fast.
Therefore speech does become weary.
The eye becomes weary.
The ear becomes weary.

children.text: athemam eva nāpnot yo 'yaṃ madhyamaḥ prāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But it did not reach this one, the central <s>prāṇa</s>.
They resolved to recognize him.

children.text: ayaṃ vai naḥ śreṣṭho yaḥ saṃcaraṃś cāsaṃcaraṃś ca na vyathate 'tho na riṣyati
children.translated_text: "This indeed is the best of us, who, moving and not moving, is not distressed and also does not perish.
Come, let us all become his form alone."
They all became his form alone.
Therefore these are named by this one's name: <s>prāṇas</s>.

children.text: tena ha vāva tat kulam ācakṣate yasmin kule bhavati ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: By him, indeed, they name that family in which one who knows thus is born.
Whoever competes with one who knows thus dries up.
Having dried up, in the end he dies. This is with reference to the self.

children.text: athādhidevataṃ jvaliṣyāmy evāham ity agnir dadhre
children.translated_text: Now with reference to the deities: <s>Agni</s> resolved, "I alone will blaze."
<s>Āditya</s> resolved, "I will give heat."
<s>Candra</s> resolved, "I will shine."
So also the other deities, each according to its deity.

children.text: sa yathaiṣāṃ prāṇānāṃ madhyamaḥ prāṇa evam etāsāṃ devatānāṃ vāyuḥ
children.translated_text: As the central <s>prāṇa</s> is among these <s>prāṇas</s>, so <s>Vāyu</s> is among these deities.

children.text: mlocanti hy anyā devatā na vāyuḥ
children.translated_text: For the other deities set, but not <s>Vāyu</s>.
This non-setting deity is <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: athaiṣa śloko bhavati yataś codeti sūryo 'staṃ yatra ca gacchatīti
children.translated_text: Now this verse occurs: "From where the sun rises, and where he goes to set,"

children.text: prāṇād vā eṣa udeti prāṇe 'stam eti
children.translated_text: from <s>prāṇa</s> indeed he rises; in <s>prāṇa</s> he sets.

children.text: taṃ devāś cakrire dharmaṃ sa evādya sa u śva iti
children.translated_text: The gods made that their <s>dharma</s> (fixed order); it is the same today and it will be the same tomorrow.

children.text: yad vā ete 'murhy adhriyanta tad evāpy adya kurvanti
children.translated_text: What they upheld then in former days, that indeed they do even today.

children.text: tasmād ekam eva vrataṃ caret prāṇyāccaivāpānyāc ca
children.translated_text: Therefore one should practice this one vow: one should breathe in and breathe out.

children.text: nen mā pāpmā mṛtyur āpnavad iti
children.translated_text: Thinking, "May evil, may death, not reach me."

children.text: yady u caret samāpipayiṣet teno etasyai devatāyai sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ||
children.translated_text: If one should practice it, one should bring it to completion; through it one wins union with this deity and dwelling in the same world as it.

children.text: trayaṃ vā idaṃ nāma rūpaṃ karma
children.translated_text: This, indeed, is threefold: name, form, and action.

children.text: teṣāṃ nāmnāṃ vāg ity etad eṣām uktham
children.translated_text: Of those names, speech is their uktha.
For from it all names arise.
It is their sāman.
For it is equal with all names.
It is their brahman.
For it bears all names.

children.text: atha rūpāṇāṃ cakṣur ity etad eṣām uktham
children.translated_text: Now, of forms, the eye is their uktha.
For from it all forms arise.
It is their sāman.
For it is equal with all forms.
It is their brahman.
For it bears all forms.

children.text: atha karmaṇām ātmety etad eṣām uktham
children.translated_text: Now, of actions, the self is their uktha.
For from it all actions arise.
It is their sāman.
For it is equal with all actions.
It is their brahman.
For it bears all actions.

children.text: tad etat trayaṃ sad ekam ayam ātmā
children.translated_text: This triad, though it exists, is one: this self.
The self, though one, is this triad.
This immortal thing is covered by truth.
Breath, indeed, is the immortal.
Name and form are truth.
By those two this breath is covered.
<s>Dṛptabālāki Gārgya</s> was a learned reciter.

children.text: sa hovācājātaśatruṃ kāśyaṃ brahma te bravāṇīti
children.translated_text: He said to <s>Ajātaśatru</s> of <s>Kāśi</s>, "Let me tell you brahman."

children.text: sa hovācājātaśatruḥ sahasram etasyāṃ vāci dadmaḥ janako janaka iti vai janā dhāvantīti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, "We give a thousand for such a statement. People indeed run about saying, \"<s>Janaka</s>, <s>Janaka</s>.\""

children.text: sa hovāca gārgyaḥ ya evāsāv āditye puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said, "That person who is there in the sun: him alone I worship as brahman."
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, "Do not discuss this with me in that way.

children.text: atiṣṭhāḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ mūrdhā rājeti vā aham etam upāsa iti
children.translated_text: I worship him as the one standing above, the head and king of all beings."

children.text: sa ya etam evam upāste 'tiṣṭhāḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ mūrdhā rājā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Whoever worships him thus becomes one who stands above, the head and king of all beings.

children.text: sa hovāca gārgyaḥ ya evāsau candre puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said, "That person who is there in the moon: him alone I worship as brahman."
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, "Do not discuss this with me in that way.

children.text: bṛhan pāṇḍaravāsāḥ somo rājeti vā aham etam upāsa iti
children.translated_text: I worship him as the great one clothed in white, as <s>Soma</s> the king."

children.text: sa ya etam evam upāste 'harahar sutaḥ prasuto bhavati
children.translated_text: For whoever worships him thus, the pressed Soma is freshly pressed for him day after day.
His food does not diminish.

children.text: sa hovāca gārgyaḥ ya evāsau vidyuti puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said, "That person who is there in lightning: him alone I worship as brahman."
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, "Do not discuss this with me in that way.

children.text: tejasvīti vā aham etam upāsa iti
children.translated_text: I worship him as brilliant."

children.text: sa ya etam evam upāste tejasvī ha bhavati
children.translated_text: Whoever worships him thus becomes brilliant indeed.
His offspring too become brilliant.

children.text: sa hovāca gārgyaḥ ya evāyam ākāśe puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said, "That person who is here in space: him alone I worship as brahman."
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, "Do not discuss this with me in that way.

children.text: pūrṇam apravartīti vā aham etam upāsa iti
children.translated_text: I worship him as full and unmoving."

children.text: sa ya etam evam upāste pūryate prajayā paśubhir nāsyāsmāl lokāt prajodvartate ||
children.translated_text: Whoever worships him thus is filled with offspring and cattle; his progeny does not turn away from this world.

children.text: sa hovāca gārgyaḥ ya evāyaṃ vāyau puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said, "That person who is here in the wind: him alone I worship as brahman."
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, "Do not discuss this with me in that way.

children.text: indro vaikuṇṭho 'parājitā seneti vā aham etam upāsa iti
children.translated_text: I worship him as <s>Indra Vaikuṇṭha</s>, as an unconquered army."

children.text: sa ya etam evam upāste jiṣṇur hāparājiṣṇur bhavaty anyatastyajāyī ||
children.translated_text: Whoever worships him thus becomes victorious, unconquered, and a conqueror of others.

children.text: sa hovāca gārgyaḥ ya evāyam agnau puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said, "That person who is here in fire: him alone I worship as brahman."
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, "Do not discuss this with me in that way.

children.text: viṣāsahir iti vā aham etam upāsa iti
children.translated_text: I worship him as the overcomer."

children.text: sa ya etam evam upāste viṣāsahir ha bhavati
children.translated_text: Whoever worships him thus becomes an overcomer indeed.
His offspring too become overcomers.

children.text: sa hovāca gārgyaḥ ya evāyam apsu puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said, "That person who is here in the waters: him alone I worship as brahman."
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, "Do not discuss this with me in that way.

children.text: pratirūpa iti vā aham etam upāsa iti
children.translated_text: I worship him as the fitting counterpart."

children.text: sa ya etam evam upāste pratirūpaṃ haivainam upagacchati nāpratirūpam
children.translated_text: Whoever worships him thus, what is fitting comes to him, not what is unfitting.
And from him one who is fitting is born.

children.text: sa hovāca gārgyaḥ ya evāyam ādarśe puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said, "That person who is here in a mirror: him alone I worship as brahman."
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, "Do not discuss this with me in that way.

children.text: rociṣṇur iti vā aham etam upāsa iti
children.translated_text: I worship him as shining."

children.text: sa ya etam evam upāste rociṣṇur ha bhavati
children.translated_text: Whoever worships him thus becomes shining indeed.
His offspring too become shining.
And those with whom he comes together,
he outshines them all.

children.text: sa hovāca gārgyaḥ ya evāyaṃ yantaṃ paścācchabbo 'nūdety etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said, "That person who is this sound that follows behind one as one goes: him alone I worship as brahman."
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, "Do not discuss this with me in that way.

children.text: asur iti vā aham etam upāsa iti
children.translated_text: I worship him as life."

children.text: sa ya etam evam upāste sarvaṃ haivāsmiṃlloka āyur eti
children.translated_text: Whoever worships him thus attains the full span of life in this world.
Breath does not leave him before the proper time.

children.text: sa hovāca gārgyaḥ ya evāyaṃ dikṣu puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said, "That person who is here in the directions: him alone I worship as brahman."
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, "Do not discuss this with me in that way.

children.text: dvitīyo 'napaga iti vā aham etam upāsa iti
children.translated_text: I worship him as a second companion who does not depart."

children.text: sa ya etam evam upāste dvitīyavān ha bhavati
children.translated_text: Whoever worships him thus becomes possessed of a second companion.
A following is not cut off from him.

children.text: sa hovāca gārgyaḥ ya evāyaṃ chāyāmayaḥ puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said, "That person who consists of shadow: him alone I worship as brahman."
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, "Do not discuss this with me in that way.

children.text: mṛtyur iti vā aham etam upāsa iti
children.translated_text: “As death,” indeed, “I worship this one.”

children.text: sa ya etam evam upāste sarvaṃ haivāsmiṃl loka āyur eti
children.translated_text: He who worships this one in this way reaches the full span of life in this world.
Death does not come to him before the proper time.

children.text: sa hovāca gārgyaḥ ya evāyam ātmani puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said, “That person who is here in the self: I worship this very one as <s>Brahman</s>.”
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, “Do not converse with me about this one.

children.text: ātmanvīti vā aham etam upāsa iti
children.translated_text: As self-possessed, indeed, I worship this one.”

children.text: sa ya etam evam upāsta ātmanvī ha bhavati
children.translated_text: He who worships this one in this way becomes self-possessed.
His offspring too becomes self-possessed.
Then <s>Gārgya</s> fell silent.
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, “Is that all?”
“That is all indeed.”
“By only so much, it is not known.”
<s>Gārgya</s> said, “Let me come to you as a pupil.”

children.text: sa hovācājātaśatruḥ pratilomaṃ caitad yad brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyam upeyād brahma me vakṣyatīti
children.translated_text: <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, “This is contrary to the regular order, that a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should approach a <s>kṣatriya</s> saying, ‘He will tell me <s>Brahman</s>.’
Still, I will make you understand it clearly.”
Taking him by the hand, he rose.
The two of them came to a man who was asleep.

children.text: tam etair nāmabhir āmantrayāṃcakre bṛhan pāṇḍaravāsaḥ soma rājann iti
children.translated_text: He addressed him by these names: “Great one, white-clad one, <s>Soma</s>, king!”
He did not get up.
He awakened him by rubbing him with his hand.
He got up.

children.text: sa hovācājātaśatruḥ yatraiṣa etat supto 'bhūd ya eṣa vijñānamayaḥ puruṣaḥ kvaiṣa tadābhūt kuta etad āgād iti
children.translated_text: <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, “When this one here was asleep, this person made of consciousness, where then was he, and from where did he come back?”

children.text: tad u ha na mene gārgyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> did not know that.

children.text: sa hovācājātaśatruḥ yatraiṣa etat supto 'bhūd ya eṣa vijñānamayaḥ puruṣas tad eṣāṃ prāṇānāṃ vijñānena vijñānam ādāya ya eṣo 'ntar hṛdaya ākāśas tasmiñchete
children.translated_text: <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said, “When this one here was asleep, this person made of consciousness, then, having taken the consciousness of these <s>prāṇas</s> (vital powers) by his consciousness, he lies in that space within the heart.
When he takes hold of them,
then this person is said to be sleeping.
Then the <s>prāṇa</s> is taken hold of.
Speech is taken hold of.
The eye is taken hold of.
The ear is taken hold of.
The mind is taken hold of.

children.text: sa yatraitat svapnyayā carati te hāsya lokāḥ
children.translated_text: When he moves about in this dream-state, those are his worlds.

children.text: tad uteva mahārājo bhavaty uteva mahābrāhmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then he is as it were a great king, or as it were a great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
Or else he meets with high and low conditions.

children.text: sa yathā mahārājo jānapadān gṛhītvā sve janapade yathākāmaṃ parivartetaivam evaiṣa etat prāṇān gṛhītvā sve śarīre yathākāmaṃ parivartate ||
children.translated_text: Just as a great king, having taken his people, might move about at will in his own realm, so this one, having taken the <s>prāṇas</s>, moves about at will in his own body.
But when he becomes deeply asleep,
when he knows nothing at all,

children.text: hitā nāma nādyo dvāsaptatiḥ sahasrāṇi hṛdayāt purītatam abhipratiṣṭhante
children.translated_text: then the channels called <s>hitā</s>, seventy-two thousand in number, extend from the heart to the <s>purītat</s> (body-enclosure).
Having slipped back through them, he lies in the <s>purītat</s>.

children.text: sa yathā kumāro vā mahārājo vā mahābrāhmaṇo vātighnīm ānandasya gatvā śayīta
children.translated_text: Just as a boy, or a great king, or a great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having reached the highest degree of bliss, might lie down,
so this one lies there in just that way.

children.text: sa yathorṇavābhis tantunoccared yathā agneḥ kṣudrā viṣphuliṅgā vyuccaranty evam evāsmād ātmanaḥ sarve prāṇāḥ sarve lokāḥ sarve devāḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni vyuccaranti
children.translated_text: As a spider comes out with its thread, and as small sparks fly out from a fire, so from this <s>ātman</s> (self) all <s>prāṇas</s>, all worlds, all gods, and all beings come forth.
Its secret teaching is: the truth of truth.

children.text: prāṇā vai satyaṃ teṣām eṣa satyam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>prāṇas</s> are truth; this one is their truth.

children.text: yo ha vai śiśuṃ sādhānaṃ sapratyādhānaṃ sasthūṇaṃ sadāmaṃ veda sapta ha dviṣato bhrātṛvyān avaruṇaddhi
children.translated_text: He who knows the child together with its support, its counter-support, its post, and its cord keeps away seven hateful rivals.

children.text: ayaṃ vāva śiśur yo 'yaṃ madhyamaḥ prāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: This child is indeed this middle <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: tasyedam evādhānam idaṃ pratyādhānaṃ prāṇaḥ sthūṇānnaṃ dāma ||
children.translated_text: This is its support; this is its counter-support; the <s>prāṇa</s> is its post; food is its cord.
These seven imperishable ones attend upon it.

children.text: tad yā imā akṣaṃl lohinyo rājayas tābhir enaṃ rudro 'nvāyattaḥ
children.translated_text: By those red streaks in the eye, <s>Rudra</s> is attached to it.

children.text: atha yā akṣann āpas tābhiḥ parjanyaḥ
children.translated_text: By the waters in the eye, <s>Parjanya</s> is attached.
By the pupil, <s>Āditya</s> is attached.
By what is black, <s>Agni</s> is attached.
By what is white, <s>Indra</s> is attached.
By the lower eyelid, <s>Pṛthivī</s> is attached to it.
By the upper one, <s>Dyauḥ</s> is attached.
The food of one who knows this is not exhausted.
On this there is the following verse:

children.text: arvāgbilaś camasa ūrdhvabudhnas tasmin yaśo nihitaṃ viśvarūpam
children.translated_text: “The cup has its mouth turned downward and its bottom turned upward; in it is placed glory of every form.

children.text: tasyāsata ṛṣayaḥ sapta tīre vāg aṣṭamī brahmaṇā saṃvidāneti
children.translated_text: Seven seers sit on its rim; speech, as the eighth, is in communion with <s>Brahman</s>.”
“The cup has its mouth turned downward and its bottom turned upward”:

children.text: idaṃ taccharīra eṣa hyarvāgbilaś camasa ūrdhvabudhnaḥ
children.translated_text: this body is that, for this body is the cup with mouth turned downward and bottom turned upward.
“In it is placed glory of every form”:
the <s>prāṇas</s> are indeed glory of every form.
This refers to the <s>prāṇas</s>.
“Seven seers sit on its rim”:
the <s>prāṇas</s> are indeed the seers.
This refers to the <s>prāṇas</s>.
“Speech, as the eighth, is in communion with <s>Brahman</s>”:
for speech, as the eighth, is joined with <s>Brahman</s>.
These two are <s>Gotama</s> and <s>Bharadvāja</s>.
This one is <s>Gotama</s>; this one is <s>Bharadvāja</s>.
These two are <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and <s>Jamadagni</s>.
This one is <s>Viśvāmitra</s>; this one is <s>Jamadagni</s>.
These two are <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
This one is <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>; this one is <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
Speech alone is <s>Atri</s>.
For by speech food is eaten.

children.text: attir ha vai nāmaitad yad autrir iti
children.translated_text: This is indeed called “eater,” that is, <s>Atri</s>.
He becomes the eater of everything.

children.text: sarvam asyānnaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Everything becomes food for one who knows this.
There are indeed two forms of <s>Brahman</s>:
the formed and the formless,
the mortal and the immortal,
the stationary and the moving,
the existent and the yonder.

children.text: tad etan mūrtaṃ yad anyad vāyoś cāntarikṣācca
children.translated_text: Of these, the formed is what is other than air and space.
This is mortal.
This is stationary.
This is the existent.

children.text: tasyaitasya mūrtasyaitasya martyasyaitasya sthitasyaitasya sata eṣa raso ya eṣa tapati
children.translated_text: The essence of this formed, mortal, stationary, existent one is that one who burns there.
For he is the essence of the existent.
Now the formless:
air and space.
This is immortal.
This is the moving.
This is the yonder.

children.text: tasyaitasyāmūrtasyaitasyāmṛtasyaitasya yata etasya tyasyaiṣa raso ya eṣa etasmin maṇḍale puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Of that formless, that immortal, that moving, that yonder, the essence is this person who is in that disk.

children.text: tyasya hy eṣa rasa ity adhidaivatam ||
children.translated_text: For he is the essence of that yonder entity; thus with reference to the gods.
Now with reference to the self.

children.text: idam eva mūrtaṃ yad anyat prāṇācca yaś cāyam antar ātmann ākāśaḥ
children.translated_text: This indeed is the formed: whatever is other than the vital breath and this space within the self.
This is mortal.
This is stationary.
This is existent.

children.text: tasyaitasya mūrtasyaitasya martyasyaitasya sthitasyaitasya sata eṣa raso yaccakṣuḥ
children.translated_text: Of this formed, this mortal, this stationary, this existent, the essence is the eye.
For the eye is the essence of the existent.

children.text: athāmūrtaṃ prāṇaś ca yaścāyam antar ātmann ākāśaḥ
children.translated_text: Now the formless is the vital breath and this space within the self.
This is immortal.
This is the moving.
This is that yonder.

children.text: tasyaitasyāmūrtasyaitasyāmṛtasyaitasya yata etasya tyasyaiṣa raso yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣan puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Of that formless, that immortal, that moving, that yonder, the essence is this person who is in the right eye.
For he is the essence of that yonder entity.
Now, of this person, the form is:

children.text: yathā māhārajanaṃ vāso yathā pāṇḍvāvikaṃ yathendragopo yathāgnyarcir yathā puṇḍarīkaṃ yathā sakṛdvidyuttam
children.translated_text: like a saffron-colored garment, like white sheep's wool, like an <s>Indragopa</s> insect, like a flame of fire, like a lotus, like a sudden flash of lightning.

children.text: sakṛdvidyutteva ha vā asya śrīr bhavati ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: The splendor of one who knows this becomes just like a sudden flash of lightning.
Now therefore the instruction: not this, not this.

children.text: na hy etasmād iti nety anyat param asti
children.translated_text: For there is nothing higher than this, beyond saying, not this.
And its name is: the truth of truth.
The vital breaths, indeed, are truth.
This is the truth of them.

children.text: maitreyīti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ udyāsyan vā are 'ham asmāt sthānād asmi
children.translated_text: <s>Maitreyī</s>, said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, dear one, I am about to depart from this state.
Come, let me make an arrangement for you and this <s>Kātyāyanī</s>.

children.text: sā hovāca maitreyī yan nu ma iyaṃ bhagoḥ sarvā pṛthivī vittena pūrṇā syāt kathaṃ tenāmṛtā syām iti
children.translated_text: She said, <s>Maitreyī</s> said: Venerable sir, if this whole earth, full of wealth, were mine, would I become immortal by that?
No, said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: yathaivopakaraṇavatāṃ jīvitaṃ tathaiva te jīvitaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: Your life would be just like the life of those who possess means.
But there is no hope of immortality through wealth.

children.text: sā hovāca maitreyī yenāhaṃ nāmṛtā syāṃ kim ahaṃ tena kuryām
children.translated_text: She said, <s>Maitreyī</s> said: What should I do with that by which I would not become immortal?

children.text: yad eva bhagavān veda tad eva me brūhīti ||
children.translated_text: Tell me only what the revered one knows.

children.text: sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ priyā batāre naḥ satī priyaṃ bhāṣase
children.translated_text: He said, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said: Dear indeed to us you are, dear one, and you speak what is dear.
Come, sit down.
I will explain it to you.
But as I explain, attend to it in deep reflection.

children.text: sa hovāca na vā are patyuḥ kāmāya patiḥ priyo bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya patiḥ priyo bhavati
children.translated_text: He said: A husband is not dear for the sake of the husband, dear one; rather, a husband is dear for the sake of the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: na vā are jāyāyai kāmāya jāyā priyā bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya jāyā priyā bhavati
children.translated_text: A wife is not dear for the sake of the wife, dear one; rather, a wife is dear for the sake of the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: na vā are putrāṇāṃ kāmāya putrāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya putrāḥ priyā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Children are not dear for the sake of the children, dear one; rather, children are dear for the sake of the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: na vā are vittasya kāmāya vittaṃ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya vittaṃ priyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: Wealth is not dear for the sake of wealth, dear one; rather, wealth is dear for the sake of the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: na vā are brahmaṇaḥ kāmāya brahma priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya brahma priyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is not dear for the sake of <s>Brahman</s>, dear one; rather, <s>Brahman</s> is dear for the sake of the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: na vā are kṣatrasya kāmāya kṣatraṃ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya kṣatraṃ priyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣatra</s> (royal power) is not dear for the sake of <s>kṣatra</s>, dear one; rather, <s>kṣatra</s> is dear for the sake of the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: na vā are lokānāṃ kāmāya lokāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya lokāḥ priyā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Worlds are not dear for the sake of the worlds, dear one; rather, worlds are dear for the sake of the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: na vā are devānāṃ kāmāya devāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya devāḥ priyā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Gods are not dear for the sake of the gods, dear one; rather, gods are dear for the sake of the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: na vā are bhūtānāṃ kāmāya bhūtāni priyāṇi bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya bhūtāni priyāṇi bhavanti
children.translated_text: Beings are not dear for the sake of beings, dear one; rather, beings are dear for the sake of the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: na vā are sarvasya kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: Everything is not dear for the sake of everything, dear one; rather, everything is dear for the sake of the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyo maitreyi
children.translated_text: The <s>ātman</s> (Self), dear <s>Maitreyī</s>, must be seen, must be heard, must be reflected upon, and must be meditated upon.

children.text: ātmano vā are darśanena śravaṇena matyā vijñānenedaṃ sarvaṃ viditam ||
children.translated_text: For by seeing the <s>ātman</s> (Self), by hearing it, by thinking about it, and by knowing it, all this is known.

children.text: brahma taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmano brahma veda
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> abandons the one who knows <s>Brahman</s> as elsewhere than the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: kṣatraṃ taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmanaḥ kṣatraṃ veda
