children.translated_text: <s>Kṣatra</s> abandons the one who knows <s>kṣatra</s> as elsewhere than the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: lokās taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano lokān veda
children.translated_text: The worlds abandon the one who knows the worlds as elsewhere than the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: devās taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano devān veda
children.translated_text: The gods abandon the one who knows the gods as elsewhere than the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: bhūtāni taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano bhūtāni veda
children.translated_text: Beings abandon the one who knows beings as elsewhere than the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: sarvaṃ taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmanaḥ sarvaṃ veda
children.translated_text: Everything abandons the one who knows everything as elsewhere than the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: idaṃ brahmedaṃ kṣatram ime lokā ime devā imāni bhūtānīdaṃ sarvaṃ yad ayam ātmā ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Brahman</s>, this <s>kṣatra</s>, these worlds, these gods, these beings, all this is this <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: sa yathā dundubher hanyamānasya na bāhyāñchabdāñchaknuyād grahaṇāya
children.translated_text: As, when a drum is being beaten, one could not grasp the external sounds separately,

children.text: dundubhes tu grahaṇena dundubhyāghātasya vā śabdo gṛhītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but by grasping the drum, or the beating of the drum, the sound is grasped;

children.text: sa yathā śaṅkhasya dhmāyamānasya na bāhyāñchabdāñchaknuyād grahaṇāya śaṅkhasya tu grahaṇena śaṅkhadhmasya vā śabdo gṛhītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as, when a conch is being blown, one could not grasp the external sounds separately, but by grasping the conch, or the blowing of the conch, the sound is grasped;

children.text: sa yathā vīṇāyai vādyamānāyai na bāhyāñchabdāñchaknuyād grahaṇāya vīṇāyai tu grahaṇena vīṇāvādasya vā śabdo gṛhītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as, when a <s>vīṇā</s> is being played, one could not grasp the external sounds separately, but by grasping the <s>vīṇā</s>, or the playing of the <s>vīṇā</s>, the sound is grasped;

children.text: sa yathārdraidhāgner abhyāhitāt pṛthag dhūmā viniścaranty eva vā are 'sya mahato bhūtasya niḥśvasitam etad yad ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvāṅgirasa itihāsaḥ purāṇaṃ vidyā upaniṣadaḥ ślokāḥ sūtrāṇy anuvyākhyānāni vyākhyānāni
children.translated_text: as separate clouds of smoke issue from a fire kindled with damp fuel, so indeed, dear one, this is the breathing forth of this great being: the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s>, history, ancient lore, sciences, upaniṣads, verses, sūtras, supplementary explanations, and explanations.
These are the very exhalations of this one.

children.text: sa yathā sarvāsām apāṃ samudra ekāyanam
children.translated_text: As the ocean is the single destination of all waters,
so the skin is the single destination of all touches.
Thus the nose is the one convergence for all smells.
Thus the tongue is the one convergence for all tastes.
Thus the eye is the one convergence for all forms.
Thus the ear is the one convergence for all sounds.
Thus the mind is the one convergence for all intentions.
Thus the heart is the one convergence for all forms of knowledge.
Thus the hands are the one convergence for all actions.
Thus the generative organ is the one convergence for all pleasures.
Thus the anus is the one convergence for all excretions.
Thus the feet are the one convergence for all paths.
Thus speech is the one convergence for all the Vedas.

children.text: sa yathā saindhavakhilya udake prāsta udakam evānuvilīyeta na hāsyodgrahaṇāyeva syāt
children.translated_text: Just as a lump of salt, thrown into water, would dissolve into water alone and would not be available for taking out again,
yet from whatever place one might take it, it would be salty,

children.text: evaṃ vā ara idaṃ mahad bhūtam anantam apāraṃ vijñānaghana eva
children.translated_text: so indeed, my dear, this great being is infinite, boundless, only a mass of cognition.
Having arisen from these elements, it disappears into them alone.
After death there is no distinct awareness, my dear, I say.
Thus spoke <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: sā hovāca maitreyī atraiva mā bhagavān amūmuhan na pretya saṃjñāstīti
children.translated_text: <s>Maitreyī</s> said, "Here indeed, revered sir, you have bewildered me by saying, 'After death there is no distinct awareness.'"

children.text: sa hovāca na vā are 'haṃ mohaṃ bravīmi
children.translated_text: He said, "No, my dear, I am not speaking bewilderment.
This is indeed sufficient for understanding.

children.text: yatra hi dvaitam iva bhavati tad itara itaraṃ jighrati tad itara itaraṃ paśyati tad itara itaraṃ śṛṇoti tad itara itaraṃ jighrati tad itara itaram abhivadati tad itara itaraṃ manute tad itara itaraṃ vijānāti
children.translated_text: For where there is duality, as it were, there one smells another, there one sees another, there one hears another, there one smells another, there one addresses another, there one thinks of another, there one knows another.

children.text: yatra vāsya sarvam ātmaivābhūt tat kena kaṃ jighret tat kena kaṃ jighret tat kena kaṃ paśyet tat kena kaṃ śṛṇuyāt tat kena kam abhivadet tat kena kaṃ manvīta tat kena kaṃ vijānīyāt
children.translated_text: But where everything has become only the <s>ātman</s> (self) for him, then by what and whom should one smell, by what and whom should one smell, by what and whom should one see, by what and whom should one hear, by what and whom should one address, by what and whom should one think, by what and whom should one know?

children.text: yenedaṃ sarvaṃ vijānāti taṃ kena vijānīyāt
children.translated_text: By what should one know that through which one knows all this?
By what, my dear, should one know the knower?
This earth is honey for all beings.
All beings are honey for this earth.

children.text: yaś cāyam asyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaścāyam adhyātmaṃ śārīras tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā
children.translated_text: And the radiant, immortal person who is in this earth, and the radiant, immortal person who, with reference to the self, is embodied: this one is just that one, who is this <s>ātman</s> (self).
This is immortal; this is <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality); this is all.
These waters are honey for all beings.
All beings are honey for these waters.

children.text: yaś cāyam āsv apsu tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaścāyam adhyātmaṃ raitasas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā
children.translated_text: And the radiant, immortal person who is in these waters, and the radiant, immortal person who, with reference to the self, is seminal: this one is just that one, who is this <s>ātman</s> (self).
This is immortal; this is <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality); this is all.
This <s>Agni</s> is honey for all beings.
All beings are honey for this <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: yaś cāyam asminn agnau tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaścāyam adhyātmaṃ vāṅmayas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā
children.translated_text: And the radiant, immortal person who is in this <s>Agni</s>, and the radiant, immortal person who, with reference to the self, is made of speech: this one is just that one, who is this <s>ātman</s> (self).
This is immortal; this is <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality); this is all.
This <s>Vāyu</s> is honey for all beings.
All beings are honey for this <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: yaś cāyam asmin vāyau tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ prāṇas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā
children.translated_text: And the radiant, immortal person who is in this <s>Vāyu</s>, and the radiant, immortal person who, with reference to the self, is <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath): this one is just that one, who is this <s>ātman</s> (self).
This is immortal; this is <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality); this is all.
This <s>Āditya</s> is honey for all beings.
All beings are honey for this <s>Āditya</s>.

children.text: yaś cāyam asminn āditye tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ cākṣuṣas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā
children.translated_text: And the radiant, immortal person who is in this <s>Āditya</s>, and the radiant, immortal person who, with reference to the self, belongs to the eye: this one is just that one, who is this <s>ātman</s> (self).
This is immortal; this is <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality); this is all.
These directions are honey for all beings.
All beings are honey for these directions.

children.text: yaś cāyam āsu dikṣu tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ śrautraḥ prātiśrutkas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā
children.translated_text: And the radiant, immortal person who is in these directions, and the radiant, immortal person who, with reference to the self, belongs to hearing and echo: this one is just that one, who is this <s>ātman</s> (self).
This is immortal; this is <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality); this is all.
This <s>Candra</s> is honey for all beings.
All beings are honey for this <s>Candra</s>.

children.text: yaś cāyam asmin candre tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ mānasas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmedam amṛtam
children.translated_text: And the radiant, immortal person who is in this <s>Candra</s>, and the radiant, immortal person who, with reference to the self, is mental: this one is just that one, who is this <s>ātman</s> (self); this is immortal.
This is <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality); this is all.
This lightning is honey for all beings.
All beings are honey for this lightning.

children.text: yaś cāyam asyāṃ vidyuti tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ taijasas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā
children.translated_text: And the radiant, immortal person who is in this lightning, and the radiant, immortal person who, with reference to the self, is fiery: this one is just that one, who is this <s>ātman</s> (self).
This is immortal; this is <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality); this is all.
This thunder is honey for all beings.
All beings are honey for this thunder.

children.text: yaś cāyam asminstanayitnau tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ śābdaḥ sauvaras tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā
children.translated_text: And the radiant, immortal person who is in this thunder, and the radiant, immortal person who, with reference to the self, is sound-formed and voice-toned: this one is just that one, who is this <s>ātman</s> (self).
This is immortal; this is <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality); this is all.
This space is honey for all beings.
All beings are honey for this space.

children.text: yaś cāyam asminn ākāśe tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ hṛdy ākāśas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā
children.translated_text: And the person here in this space, made of light and made of immortality, and the person here internally, in the space within the heart, made of light and made of immortality: he is just this one who is this self.
This is immortal; this is <s>brahman</s>; this is all.
This <s>dharma</s> is the honey of all beings.
All beings are the honey of this <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: yaś cāyam asmin dharme tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ dhārmas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā
children.translated_text: And the person here in this <s>dharma</s>, made of light and made of immortality, and the person here internally, belonging to <s>dharma</s>, made of light and made of immortality: he is just this one who is this self.
This is immortal; this is <s>brahman</s>; this is all.
This truth is the honey of all beings.
All beings are the honey of this truth.

children.text: yaś cāyam asmin satye tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ sātyas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā
children.translated_text: And the person here in this truth, made of light and made of immortality, and the person here internally, belonging to truth, made of light and made of immortality: he is just this one who is this self.
This is immortal; this is <s>brahman</s>; this is all.
This human principle is the honey of all beings.
All beings are the honey of this human principle.

children.text: yaś cāyam asmin mānuṣe tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ mānuṣas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā
children.translated_text: And the person here in this human principle, made of light and made of immortality, and the person here internally, belonging to the human principle, made of light and made of immortality: he is just this one who is this self.
This is immortal; this is <s>brahman</s>; this is all.
This self is the honey of all beings.
All beings are the honey of this self.

children.text: yaś cāyam asminn ātmani tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam ātmā tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā
children.translated_text: And the person here in this self, made of light and made of immortality, and this self made of light and made of immortality: he is just this one who is this self.
This is immortal; this is <s>brahman</s>; this is all.

children.text: sa vā ayam ātmā sarveṣāṃ adhipatiḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ rājā
children.translated_text: This very self is the overlord of all, the king of all beings.

children.text: tad yathā rathanābhau ca rathanemau cārāḥ sarve samarpitāḥ
children.translated_text: As all the spokes are fixed in the nave of a chariot wheel and in the rim of a chariot wheel,

children.text: evam evāsminn ātmani sarvāṇi bhūtāni sarve devāḥ sarve lokāḥ sarve prāṇāḥ sarva eta ātmānaḥ samarpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so indeed in this self all beings, all gods, all worlds, all <s>prāṇas</s>, and all these selves are fixed.

children.text: idaṃ vai tan madhu dadhyaṅṅ ātharvaṇo 'śvibhyām uvāca
children.translated_text: This indeed is that honey which <s>Dadhyaṅ Ātharvaṇa</s> taught to the <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: tad etad ṛṣiḥ paśyann avocat tad vāṃ narā sanaye daṃsa ugram āviṣkṛṇomi tanyatur na vṛṣṭim
children.translated_text: Seeing this, the seer said: "That fierce deed of yours, O heroes, I reveal for gain, like the thunderer revealing rain.

children.text: dadhyaṅ ha yan madhv ātharvaṇo vām aśvasya śīrṣṇā pra yad īm uvāceti ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Dadhyaṅ Ātharvaṇa</s> proclaimed the honey to you with a horse's head," so it says.

children.text: idaṃ vai tan madhu dadhyaṅṅ ātharvaṇo 'śvibhyām uvāca
children.translated_text: This indeed is that honey which <s>Dadhyaṅ Ātharvaṇa</s> taught to the <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: tad etad ṛṣiḥ paśyann avocat ātharvaṇāyāśvinau dadhīce 'śvyaṃ śiraḥ praty airayatam
children.translated_text: Seeing this, the seer said: "O <s>Aśvins</s>, for <s>Dadhīc Ātharvaṇa</s> you set on a horse's head.

children.text: sa vāṃ madhu pravocad ṛtāyan tvāṣṭraṃ yad dasrāv apikakṣyaṃ vām iti ||
children.translated_text: He proclaimed to you the honey, going in accordance with truth, the work of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, which, O wonder-workers, had been hidden from you," so it says.

children.text: idaṃ vai tan madhu dadhyaṅṅ ātharvaṇo 'śvibhyām uvāca
children.translated_text: This indeed is that honey which <s>Dadhyaṅ Ātharvaṇa</s> taught to the <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: tad etad ṛṣiḥ paśyann avocat puraścakre dvipadaḥ puraścakre catuṣpadaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing this, the seer said: "He made a front for the two-footed; he made a front for the four-footed.

children.text: puraḥ sa pakṣī bhūtvā puraḥ puruṣa āviśad iti
children.translated_text: Having become a bird in front, the person entered the fronts," so it says.

children.text: sa vā ayaṃ puruṣaḥ sarvāsu pūrṣu puriśayaḥ
children.translated_text: This person indeed, lying in the citadel, is present in all citadels.
Nothing whatever is left uncovered by him.
Nothing whatever is left unenclosed by him.

children.text: idaṃ vai tan madhu dadhyaṅṅ ātharvaṇo 'śvibhyām uvāca
children.translated_text: This indeed is that honey which <s>Dadhyaṅ Ātharvaṇa</s> taught to the <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: tad etad ṛṣiḥ paśyann avocat rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva tad asya rūpaṃ praticakṣaṇāya
children.translated_text: Seeing this, the seer said: "Form by form he became the corresponding form; that form of his is for being seen.

children.text: indro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate yuktā hy asya harayaḥ śatā daśeti
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, through his powers of illusion, goes about in many forms, for his bay steeds are yoked, ten hundreds," so it says.

children.text: ayaṃ vai harayo 'yaṃ vai daśa ca sahasrāṇi bahūni cānantāni ca
children.translated_text: These indeed are the bay steeds; these indeed are the ten, and the thousands, and the many, and the endless.

children.text: tad etad brahmāpūrvam anaparam anantaram abāhyam
children.translated_text: That is this <s>brahman</s>, without what is before, without what is after, without what is within, and without what is outside.
This self is <s>brahman</s>, experiencing all.
Thus is the instruction.
Now the lineage.
<s>Pautimāṣya</s> from <s>Gaupavana</s>.
<s>Gaupavana</s> from <s>Paśutimāṣya</s>.
<s>Paśutimāṣya</s> from <s>Gaupavana</s>.
<s>Gaupavana</s> from <s>Kauśika</s>.
<s>Kauśika</s> from <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>.
<s>Kauṇḍinya</s> from <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>.
<s>Śāṇḍilya</s> from <s>Kauśika</s> and from <s>Gautama</s>.
<s>Gautama</s>
from <s>Āgniveśya</s>.
<s>Āgniveśya</s> from <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> and from <s>Ānabhimlāta</s>.
<s>Ānabhimlāta</s> from <s>Ānabhimlāta</s>.
<s>Ānabhimlāta</s> from <s>Ānabhimlāta</s>.
<s>Ānabhimlāta</s> from <s>Gautama</s>.
<s>Gautama</s> from <s>Saitava</s> and <s>Prācīnayogya</s>.
<s>Saitava</s> and <s>Prācīnayogya</s> from <s>Pārāśarya</s>.
<s>Pārāśarya</s> from <s>Bhāradvāja</s>.
<s>Bhāradvāja</s> from <s>Bhāradvāja</s> and from <s>Gautama</s>.
<s>Gautama</s> from <s>Bhāradvāja</s>.
<s>Bhāradvāja</s> from <s>Pārāśarya</s>.
<s>Pārāśarya</s> from <s>Vaijavāpāyana</s>.
<s>Vaijavāpāyana</s> from <s>Kauśikāyani</s>.
<s>Kauśikāyani</s>
from <s>Ghṛtakauśika</s>.
<s>Ghṛtakauśika</s> from <s>Prāśaryāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Pāraśaryāyaṇa</s> from <s>Pārāśarya</s>.
<s>Pārāśarya</s> from <s>Jātūkarṇya</s>.
<s>Jātūkarṇya</s> from <s>Āsurāyaṇa</s> and from <s>Yāska</s>.
<s>Āsurāyaṇa</s> from <s>Traivaṇi</s>.
<s>Traivaṇi</s> from <s>Aupajandhani</s>.
<s>Aupajandhani</s> from <s>Āsuri</s>.
<s>Āsuri</s> from <s>Bhāradvāja</s>.
<s>Bhāradvāja</s> from <s>Ātreya</s>.
<s>Ātreya</s> from <s>Māṇṭi</s>.
<s>Māṇṭi</s> from <s>Gautama</s>.
<s>Gautama</s> from <s>Vātsya</s>.
<s>Vātsya</s> from <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>.
<s>Śāṇḍilya</s> from <s>Kaiśorya Kāpya</s>.
<s>Kaiśorya Kāpya</s> from <s>Kumārahārita</s>.
<s>Kumārahārita</s> from <s>Gālava</s>.
<s>Gālava</s> from <s>Vidarbhīkauṇḍinya</s>.
<s>Vidarbhīkauṇḍinya</s> from <s>Vatsanapāt Bābhrava</s>.
<s>Vatsanapāt Bābhrava</s> from <s>Panthā Saubhara</s>.
<s>Panthā Saubhara</s> from <s>Ayāsya Āṅgirasa</s>.
<s>Ayāsya Āṅgirasa</s> from <s>Ābhūti Tvāṣṭra</s>.
<s>Ābhūti Tvāṣṭra</s> from <s>Viśvarūpa Tvāṣṭra</s>.
<s>Viśvarūpa Tvāṣṭra</s> from the <s>Aśvins</s>.
The <s>Aśvins</s> from <s>Dadhīc Ātharvaṇa</s>.
<s>Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa</s> received it from <s>Atharvan Daiva</s>.
<s>Atharvan Daiva</s> received it from <s>Mṛtyu Prādhvaṃsana</s>.
<s>Mṛtyu Prādhvaṃsana</s> received it from <s>Pradhvaṃsana</s>.
<s>Pradhvaṃsana</s> received it from <s>Ekarṣi</s>.
<s>Ekarṣi</s> received it from <s>Vipracitti</s>.
<s>Vipracitti</s> received it from <s>Vyaṣṭi</s>.
<s>Vyaṣṭi</s> received it from <s>Sanāru</s>.
<s>Sanāru</s> received it from <s>Sanātana</s>.
<s>Sanātana</s> received it from <s>Sanaga</s>.
<s>Sanaga</s> received it from <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
<s>Parameṣṭhin</s> received it from <s>Brahman</s>.
<s>Brahman</s> is self-born.
Homage to <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality).
<s>Janaka Vaideha</s> once performed a sacrifice with many gifts.

children.text: tatra ha kurupañcālānāṃ brāhmaṇā abhisametā babhūvuḥ
children.translated_text: There the Brahmins of the <s>Kuru-Pañcālas</s> had assembled.

children.text: tasya ha janakasya vaidehasya vijijñāsā babhūva kaḥ svid eṣāṃ brāhmaṇānām anūcānatama iti
children.translated_text: This desire to know arose in that <s>Janaka Vaideha</s>: "Which of these Brahmins is the most learned in recitation?"
He had a thousand cows penned in.

children.text: daśadaśa pādā ekaikasyāḥ śṛṅgayor ābaddhā babhūvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ten gold pieces were fastened to each cow's two horns.

children.text: tān hovāca brāhmaṇā bhagavanto yo vo brahmiṣṭhaḥ sa etā gā udajatām iti
children.translated_text: He said to them, "Revered Brahmins, whichever of you is the most versed in <s>brahman</s>, let him drive away these cows."
But the Brahmins did not dare.

children.text: atha ha yājñavalkyaḥ svam eva brahmacāriṇam uvāca etāḥ saumyodaja sāmaśravā3 iti
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said to his own brahmacārin, "My dear <s>Sāmaśravas</s>, drive these away."
He drove them away.

children.text: te ha brāhmaṇāś cukrudhuḥ kathaṃ nu no brahmiṣṭho bruvīteti
children.translated_text: The Brahmins became angry: "How can he call himself the most versed in <s>brahman</s> among us?"

children.text: atha ha janakasya vaidehasya hotāśvalo babhūva
children.translated_text: Now <s>Aśvala</s> was the hotṛ (invoking priest) of that <s>Janaka Vaideha</s>.

children.text: sa hainaṃ papraccha tvaṃ nu khalu no yājñavalkya brahmiṣṭho 'sī3 iti
children.translated_text: He asked him, "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, are you indeed the most versed in <s>brahman</s> among us?"

children.text: sa hovāca namo vayaṃ brahmiṣṭhāya kurmo gokāmā eva vayaṃ sma iti
children.translated_text: He said, "We bow to the one who is most versed in <s>brahman</s>; we simply desire the cows."

children.text: taṃ ha tata eva praṣṭuṃ dadhre hotāśvalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the hotṛ <s>Aśvala</s> undertook to question him right there.

children.text: yājñavalkyeti hovāca yad idaṃ sarvaṃ mṛtyunāptaṃ sarvaṃ mṛtyunābhipannaṃ kena yajamāno mṛtyor āptim atimucyata iti
children.translated_text: He said, "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, since all this is reached by death and all this is overcome by death, by what does the sacrificer pass beyond the reach of death?"
"By the hotṛ priest, by <s>Agni</s>, by speech."
Speech is indeed the hotṛ of the sacrifice.

children.text: tad yeyaṃ vāk so 'yam agniḥ sa hotā sā muktiḥ sātimuktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That which is this speech is this <s>Agni</s>; he is the hotṛ. This is liberation; this is complete liberation.

children.text: yājñavalkyeti hovāca yad idaṃ sarvam ahorātrābhyām āptaṃ sarvam ahorātrābhyām abhipannaṃ kena yajamāno 'horātrayor āptim atimucyata iti
children.translated_text: He said, "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, since all this is reached by day and night and all this is overcome by day and night, by what does the sacrificer pass beyond the reach of day and night?"
"By the adhvaryu priest, by the eye, by <s>Āditya</s>."
The eye is indeed the adhvaryu of the sacrifice.

children.text: tad yad idaṃ cakṣuḥ so 'sāv ādityaḥ
children.translated_text: That which is this eye is that <s>Āditya</s>.
He is the adhvaryu. This is liberation; this is complete liberation.

children.text: yājñavalkyeti hovāca yad idaṃ sarvaṃ pūrvapakṣāparapakṣābhyām āptaṃ sarvaṃ pūrvapakṣāparapakṣābhyām abhipannaṃ kena yajamānaḥ pūrvapakṣāparapakṣayor āptim atimucyata iti
children.translated_text: He said, "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, since all this is reached by the bright fortnight and the dark fortnight and all this is overcome by the bright fortnight and the dark fortnight, by what does the sacrificer pass beyond the reach of the bright and dark fortnights?"
"By the udgātṛ priest, by <s>Vāyu</s>, by prāṇa (vital breath)."
Prāṇa is indeed the udgātṛ of the sacrifice.

children.text: tad yo 'yaṃ prāṇaḥ sa vāyuḥ sa udgātā
children.translated_text: That which is this prāṇa is <s>Vāyu</s>; he is the udgātṛ.
This is liberation; this is complete liberation.

children.text: yājñavalkyeti hovāca yad idam antarikṣam anārambaṇam iva kenākrameṇa yajamānaḥ svargaṃ lokam ākramata iti
children.translated_text: He said, "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, since this midspace is as if without support, by what ascent does the sacrificer ascend to the heavenly world?"
"By the brahman priest, by the mind, by <s>Candra</s>."
The mind is indeed the brahman priest of the sacrifice.

children.text: tad yad idaṃ manaḥ so 'sau candraḥ sa brahmā sa muktiḥ sātimuktir ity atimokṣā
children.translated_text: That which is this mind is that <s>Candra</s>; he is the brahman priest. This is liberation; this is complete liberation. Thus much on the surpassing liberations.
Now, the attainments.

children.text: yājñavalkyeti hovāca katibhir ayam adyargbhir hotāsmin yajñe kariṣyatīti
children.translated_text: He said, "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, with how many verses will the hotṛ perform in this sacrifice today?"
"With three," he said.
"Which are those three?"

children.text: puronuvākyā ca yājyā ca śasyaiva tṛtīyā
children.translated_text: "The preliminary invitation, the offering verse, and the recitation as the third."
"What does he win by them?"
"Whatever here has breath."

children.text: yājñavalkyeti hovāca katy ayam adyādhvaryur asmin yajña āhutīr hoṣyatīti
children.translated_text: He said, "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, how many oblations will the adhvaryu offer in this sacrifice today?"
"Three," he said.
"Which are those three?"

children.text: yā hutā ujjvalanti yā hutā atinedanti yā hutā adhiśerate
children.translated_text: "Those that, when offered, blaze up; those that, when offered, make a great sound; and those that, when offered, lie down."
"What does he win by them?"

children.text: yā hutā ujjvalanti devalokam eva tābhir jayati
children.translated_text: "Those that, when offered, blaze up: by them he wins the world of the gods.
For the world of the gods is as if blazing.

children.text: yā hutā atinedante pitṛlokam eva tābhir jayati
children.translated_text: Those that, when offered, make a great sound: by them he wins the world of the ancestors.
For the world of the ancestors is, as it were, beyond.

children.text: yā hutā adhiśerate manuṣyalokam eva tābhir jayati
children.translated_text: Those that, when offered, lie down: by them he wins the human world.
For the human world is, as it were, below."

children.text: yājñavalkyeti hovāca katibhir ayam adya brahmā yajñaṃ dakṣiṇato devatābhir gopāyatīti
children.translated_text: He said, "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, with how many deities will the brahman priest protect the sacrifice on the southern side today?"
"With one," he said.
"Which is that one?"
"The mind alone," he said.
The mind is indeed endless, and the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> are endless.

children.text: anantam eva sa tena lokaṃ jayati ||
children.translated_text: By that he wins an endless world.

children.text: yājñavalkyeti hovāca katy ayam adyodgātāsmin yajñe stotriyāḥ stoṣyatīti
children.translated_text: He said, "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, how many stotriya chants will the udgātṛ chant in this sacrifice today?"
"Three," he said.
"Which are those three?"

children.text: puronuvākyā ca yājyā ca śasyaiva tṛtīyā
children.translated_text: "The preliminary invitation, the offering verse, and the recitation as the third."
"Which are they?"
"Those that pertain to the self."

children.text: prāṇa eva puronuvākyāpāno yājyā vyānaḥ śasyā
children.translated_text: Prāṇa is the preliminary invitation; apāna is the offering verse; vyāna is the recitation.
"What does he win by them?"

children.text: pṛthivīlokam eva puronuvākyayā jayaty antarikṣalokaṃ yājyayā dyulokaṃ śasyayā
children.translated_text: "By the preliminary invitation he wins the earthly world, by the offering verse the midspace world, and by the recitation the heavenly world."
Then the hotṛ <s>Aśvala</s> fell silent.
Then <s>Jāratkārava Ārtabhāga</s> asked him.

children.text: yājñavalkyeti hovāca kati grahāḥ katy atigrahā iti
children.translated_text: He said, "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, how many grahas (seizers) and how many atigrahas (over-seizers) are there?"
"There are eight grahas and eight atigrahas," he said.

children.text: ye te 'ṣṭau grahā aṣṭāv atigrahāḥ katame ta iti ||
children.translated_text: "Those eight grahas and eight atigrahas: which are they?"
"Prāṇa is indeed a graha.
It is seized by apāna as its atigraha.
For by prāṇa one smells odors.
Speech is indeed a graha.
It is seized by name as its atigraha.
For by speech one speaks names.
The tongue is indeed a graha.
It is seized by taste as its atigraha."
For with the tongue one discerns tastes.
The eye, indeed, is a grasper.
It is held by form as the over-grasper.
For with the eye one sees forms.
The ear, indeed, is a grasper.
It is held by sound as the over-grasper.
For with the ear one hears sounds.
The mind, indeed, is a grasper.
It is held by desire as the over-grasper.
For with the mind one desires desires.
The two hands, indeed, are a grasper.
They are held by action as the over-grasper.
For with the two hands one performs action.
The skin, indeed, is a grasper.
It is held by touch as the over-grasper.
For with the skin one experiences touches.
Thus there are eight graspers and eight over-graspers.

children.text: yājñavalkyeti hovāca yad idaṃ sarvaṃ mṛtyor annaṃ kā svit sā devatā yasyā mṛtyur annam iti
children.translated_text: "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>," he said, "since all this is food for death, what, then, is that deity for whom death is food?"
"Fire, indeed, is death; it is the food of the waters.
One conquers further death."

children.text: yājñavalkyeti hovāca yatrāyaṃ puruṣo mriyata ud asmāt prāṇāḥ krāmanty āho neti
children.translated_text: "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>," he said, "when this person dies, do the vital breaths go out from him, or not?"
"No," said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
"They are gathered together right here.
He swells up.
He becomes inflated.
Inflated, he lies dead."
"<s>Yājñavalkya</s>," he said, "when this person dies,
what does not abandon him?"
"Name," he said.
"Name, indeed, is endless; the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> are endless.

children.text: anantam eva sa tena lokaṃ jayati ||
children.translated_text: By that he wins an endless world."

children.text: yājñavalkyeti hovāca yatrāsya puruṣasya mṛtasyāgniṃ vāg apyeti vātaṃ prāṇaś cakṣur ādityaṃ manaś candraṃ diśaḥ śrotraṃ pṛthivīṃ śarīram ākāśam ātmauṣadhīr lomāni vanaspatīn keśā apsu lohitaṃ ca retaś ca nidhīyate kvāyaṃ tadā puruṣo bhavatīti
children.translated_text: "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>," he said, "when, after this person has died, speech enters fire, breath enters wind, the eye enters the sun, mind enters the moon, hearing enters the directions, the body enters the earth, the self enters space, the body-hairs enter the herbs, the head-hairs enter the trees, and the blood and semen are deposited in the waters, where then is this person?"
"Bring your hand here, dear <s>Ārtabhāga</s>.

children.text: āvām evaitasya vediṣyāvo na nāv etat sajana iti
children.translated_text: We two alone shall know of this; this is not for us to discuss publicly."
The two went aside and deliberated.

children.text: tau ha yad ūcatuḥ karma haiva tad ūcatuḥ
children.translated_text: What they spoke of was action alone.

children.text: atha ha yat praśaṃsatuḥ karma haiva tat praśaśaṃsatuḥ
children.translated_text: And what they praised was action alone.

children.text: puṇyo vai puṇyena karmaṇā bhavati pāpaḥ pāpeneti
children.translated_text: One becomes virtuous by virtuous action, and sinful by sinful action.
Then <s>Jāratkārava Ārtabhāga</s> became silent.

children.text: atha hainaṃ bhujyur lāhyāyaniḥ papraccha yājñavalkyeti hovāca madreṣu carakāḥ paryavrajāma
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bhujyu Lāhyāyani</s> questioned him. "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>," he said, "we were wandering as students among the <s>Madras</s>.
We came to the house of <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s>.
He had a daughter possessed by a <s>Gandharva</s>.
We asked him, 'Who are you?'
He said, 'I am <s>Sudhanvan Āṅgirasa</s>.'
When we asked him about the ends of the worlds,

children.text: athainam abrūma kva pārikṣitā abhavann iti
children.translated_text: then we said to him, 'Where have the <s>Pārikṣitas</s> gone?'
Where have the <s>Pārikṣitas</s> gone?
I ask you that, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>:
where have the <s>Pārikṣitas</s> gone?"
He said, "He did indeed say it.

children.text: agacchan vai te tad yatrāśvamedhayājino gacchantīti
children.translated_text: They went, indeed, to where those who perform the horse sacrifice go."
"Where, then, do the performers of the horse sacrifice go?"
"This world is thirty-two days' journeys by the chariot of the gods.
The earth surrounds it on every side, twice as large.

children.text: tāṃ samantaṃ pṛthivīṃ dvistāvat samudraḥ paryeti
children.translated_text: The ocean surrounds that earth on every side, twice as large.

children.text: tad yāvatī kṣurasya dhārā yāvad vā makṣikāyāḥ pattraṃ tāvān antareṇākāśaḥ tān aindraḥ suparṇo bhūtvā vāyave prāyacchat
children.translated_text: Between them there is a space as wide as the edge of a razor or as wide as a fly's wing; becoming <s>Indra</s>'s eagle, he handed them over to <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: tān vāyur ātmani dhitvā tatrāgamayad yatrāśvamedhayājino 'bhavann iti
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s>, placing them in himself, brought them there, where the performers of the horse sacrifice were."

children.text: evam iva vai sa vāyum eva praśaśaṃsa tasmād vāyur eva vyaṣṭir vāyuḥ samaṣṭiḥ
children.translated_text: In this way, indeed, he praised <s>Vāyu</s> alone; therefore <s>Vāyu</s> alone is the individual, <s>Vāyu</s> the totality.

children.text: apa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: One conquers further death who knows thus.
Then <s>Bhujyu Lāhyāyani</s> became silent.
Then <s>Uṣasta Cākrāyaṇa</s> questioned him.

children.text: yājñavalkyeti hovāca yat sākṣād aparokṣād brahma ya ātmā sarvāntaras taṃ me vyācakṣveti
children.translated_text: "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>," he said, "explain to me that which is <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality), directly and immediately present, the <s>ātman</s> (self) that is within all."
"This is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the one within all.

children.text: yaḥ prāṇena prāṇiti sa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ
children.translated_text: He who breathes by the <s>prāṇa</s> (in-breath) is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the one within all.
He who breathes down by the <s>apāna</s> (down-breath) is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the one within all.

children.text: yo vyānena vyaniti sa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ
children.translated_text: He who breathes through by the <s>vyāna</s> (diffusive breath) is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the one within all.

children.text: ya udānenodaniti sa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ
children.translated_text: He who breathes up by the <s>udāna</s> (up-breath) is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the one within all.
This is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the one within all."

children.text: sa hovācoṣastaś cākrāyaṇaḥ yathā vai brūyād asau gaur asāv aśva ity evam evaitad vyapadiṣṭaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: <s>Uṣasta Cākrāyaṇa</s> said, "Just as one might say, 'This is a cow, this is a horse,' so this has merely been pointed out.

children.text: yad eva sākṣād aparokṣād brahma ya ātmā sarvāntaras taṃ me vyācakṣveti
children.translated_text: Explain to me precisely that which is <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality), directly and immediately present, the <s>ātman</s> (self) that is within all."
"This is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the one within all."
"Which one, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, is the one within all?"
"You cannot see the seer of seeing.
You cannot hear the hearer of hearing.
You cannot think the thinker of thought.
You cannot know the knower of knowledge.
This is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the one within all.
Anything other than this is afflicted."
Then <s>Uṣasta Cākrāyaṇa</s> became silent.

children.text: atha hainaṃ kaholaḥ kauṣītakeyaḥ papraccha yājñavalkyeti hovāca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kahola Kauṣītakeya</s> questioned him. "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>," he said,

children.text: yad eva sākṣād aparokṣād brahma ya ātmā sarvāntaras taṃ me vyācakṣveti
children.translated_text: "explain to me precisely that which is <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality), directly and immediately present, the <s>ātman</s> (self) that is within all."
"This is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the one within all."
"Which one, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, is the one within all?"

children.text: yo 'śanāyāpipāse śokaṃ mohaṃ jarāṃ mṛtyum atyeti
children.translated_text: "The one who passes beyond hunger and thirst, grief, delusion, old age, and death.

children.text: etaṃ vai tam ātmānaṃ viditvā brāhmaṇāḥ putraiṣaṇāyāś ca vittaiṣaṇāyāś ca lokaiṣaṇāyāś ca vyutthāyātha bhikṣācaryaṃ caranti
children.translated_text: Having known this very <s>ātman</s> (self), brāhmaṇas, rising beyond desire for sons, desire for wealth, and desire for worlds, then practice the life of begging.

children.text: yā hy eva putraiṣaṇā sā vittaiṣaṇā yā vittaiṣaṇā sā lokaiṣaṇā
children.translated_text: For the desire for sons is just the desire for wealth, and the desire for wealth is just the desire for worlds.

children.text: ubhe hy ete eṣaṇe eva bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: For both of these are indeed desires.

children.text: tasmād brāhmaṇaḥ pāṇḍityaṃ nirvidya bālyena tiṣṭhāset
children.translated_text: Therefore a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having become disenchanted with learning, should remain in childlikeness.

children.text: bālyaṃ ca pāṇḍityaṃ ca nirvidyātha muniḥ
children.translated_text: Having become disenchanted with childlikeness and learning, then he is a sage.

children.text: amaunaṃ ca maunaṃ ca nirvidyātha brāhmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having become disenchanted with non-silence and silence, then he is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: sa brāhmaṇaḥ kena syād yena syāt tenedṛśa eva
children.translated_text: By what would he be a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>? By whatever he would be, he is just such.
Anything other than this is afflicted.
Then <s>Kahola Kauṣītakeya</s> fell silent.

children.text: atha hainaṃ gārgī vācaknavī papraccha yājñavalkyeti hovāca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gārgī Vācaknavī</s> questioned him. "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>," she said.

children.text: yad idaṃ sarvam apsv otaṃ ca protaṃ ca kasmin nu khalv āpa otāś ca protāś ceti
children.translated_text: "Since all this is woven and interwoven in the waters, in what, then, are the waters woven and interwoven?"
"In air, <s>Gārgī</s>."

children.text: kasmin nu khalu vāyur otaś ca protaś ceti
children.translated_text: "In what, then, is air woven and interwoven?"
"In the worlds of the midspace, <s>Gārgī</s>."

children.text: kasmin nu khalv antarikṣalokā otaś ca protaś ceti
children.translated_text: "In what, then, are the worlds of the midspace woven and interwoven?"
"In the worlds of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Gārgī</s>."

children.text: kasmin nu khalu gandharvalokā otāś ca protāś ceti
children.translated_text: "In what, then, are the worlds of the <s>Gandharvas</s> woven and interwoven?"
"In the worlds of the sun, <s>Gārgī</s>."

children.text: kasmin nu khalv ādityalokā otāś ca protāś ceti
children.translated_text: "In what, then, are the worlds of the sun woven and interwoven?"
"In the worlds of the moon, <s>Gārgī</s>."

children.text: kasmin nu khalu candralokā otāś ca protāś ceti
children.translated_text: "In what, then, are the worlds of the moon woven and interwoven?"
"In the worlds of the stars, <s>Gārgī</s>."

children.text: kasmin nu khalu nakṣatralokā otāś ca protāś ceti
children.translated_text: "In what, then, are the worlds of the stars woven and interwoven?"
"In the worlds of the gods, <s>Gārgī</s>."

children.text: kasmin nu khalu devalokā otāś ca protāś ceti
children.translated_text: "In what, then, are the worlds of the gods woven and interwoven?"
"In the worlds of <s>Indra</s>, <s>Gārgī</s>."

children.text: kasmin nu khalv indralokā otāś ca protāś ceti
children.translated_text: "In what, then, are the worlds of <s>Indra</s> woven and interwoven?"
"In the worlds of <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Gārgī</s>."

children.text: kasmin nu khalu prajāpatilokā otāś ca protāś ceti
children.translated_text: "In what, then, are the worlds of <s>Prajāpati</s> woven and interwoven?"
"In the worlds of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Gārgī</s>."

children.text: kasmin nu khalu brahmalokā otāś ca protāś ceti
children.translated_text: "In what, then, are the worlds of <s>Brahman</s> woven and interwoven?"
He said, "<s>Gārgī</s>, do not ask too far."
"Let your head not fall off."
"You are asking beyond bounds about a deity that must not be questioned beyond bounds."
"<s>Gārgī</s>, do not ask too far."
Then <s>Gārgī Vācaknavī</s> fell silent.

children.text: athainam uddālaka āruṇiḥ papraccha yājñavalkyeti hovāca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> questioned him. "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>," he said.

children.text: madreṣv avasāma patañcalasya kāpyasya gṛheṣu yajñam adhīyānāḥ
children.translated_text: "We were living among the <s>Madras</s>, in the houses of <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s>, studying sacrificial lore."
"His wife was possessed by a <s>Gandharva</s>."
"We asked him, 'Who are you?'"
"He said, 'I am <s>Kabandha Ātharvaṇa</s>.'"

children.text: so 'bravīt patañcalaṃ kāpyaṃ yājñikāṃś ca vettha nu tvaṃ kāpya tat sūtraṃ yasminn ayaṃ ca lokaḥ paraś ca lokaḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni saṃdṛbdhāni bhavantīti
children.translated_text: "He said to <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s> and to the ritualists, 'Do you know, <s>Kāpya</s>, that thread in which this world, the next world, and all beings are strung together?'"

children.text: so 'bravīt patañcalaḥ kāpyo nāhaṃ tad bhagavan vedeti
children.translated_text: "<s>Patañcala Kāpya</s> said, 'I do not know that, revered sir.'"
"He said to <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s> and to the ritualists,"

children.text: vettha nu tvaṃ kāpya tam antaryāmiṇaṃ ya imaṃ ca lokaṃ paraṃ ca lokaṃ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāny antaro yamayati
children.translated_text: "'Do you know, <s>Kāpya</s>, that <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller) who controls from within this world, the next world, and all beings?'"

children.text: so 'bravīt patañcalaḥ kāpyo nāhaṃ taṃ bhagavan vedeti
children.translated_text: "<s>Patañcala Kāpya</s> said, 'I do not know him, revered sir.'"
"He said to <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s> and to the ritualists,"

children.text: yo vai tat kāpya sūtraṃ vidyāt taṃ cāntaryāmiṇam iti sa brahmavit sa lokavit sa devavit sa vedavit sa ātmavit sa sarvavit
children.translated_text: "'Whoever knows that thread, <s>Kāpya</s>, and that <s>antaryāmin</s> is a knower of <s>brahman</s>, a knower of the worlds, a knower of the gods, a knower of the <s>Veda</s>, a knower of the self, a knower of all.'"
"Thus he spoke to them."
"I know that."

children.text: tac cet tvaṃ yājñavalkya sūtram avidvāṃs taṃ cāntaryāmiṇaṃ brahmagavīr udajase mūrdhā te vipatiṣyati
children.translated_text: "If you, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, without knowing that thread and that <s>antaryāmin</s>, drive away the <s>brahman</s>-cows, your head will fall off."

children.text: veda vā ahaṃ gautama tat sūtraṃ taṃ cāntaryāmiṇam iti
children.translated_text: "I do know, <s>Gautama</s>, that thread and that <s>antaryāmin</s>."

children.text: yo vā idaṃ kaśca brūyād veda vedeti yathā vettha tathā brūhīti ||
children.translated_text: "Anyone at all might say, 'I know, I know.' Tell it as you know it."

children.text: sa hovāca vāyur vai gautama tat sūtram
children.translated_text: He said, "Air, <s>Gautama</s>, is that thread."

children.text: vāyunā vai gautama sūtreṇāyaṃ ca lokaḥ paraś ca lokaḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni saṃdṛbdhāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: "By air as a thread, <s>Gautama</s>, this world, the next world, and all beings are strung together."

children.text: tasmād vai gautama puruṣaṃ pretam āhur vyasraṃsiṣatāsyāṅgānīti
children.translated_text: "Therefore, <s>Gautama</s>, people say of a man who has died, 'His limbs have come apart.'"

children.text: vāyunā hi gautama sūtreṇa saṃdṛbdhāni bhavantīti
children.translated_text: "For they are strung together by air as a thread, <s>Gautama</s>."
"That is exactly so, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>."
"Tell me of the <s>antaryāmin</s>."

children.text: yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan pṛthivyā antaro yaṃ pṛthivī na veda yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaḥ pṛthivīm antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "He who, standing in the earth, is within the earth, whom the earth does not know, whose body is the earth, who controls the earth from within: he is your self, the <s>antaryāmin</s>, immortal."

children.text: yo 'psu tiṣṭhann adbhyo 'ntaro yam āpo na vidur yasyāpaḥ śarīraṃ yo 'po 'ntaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "He who, standing in the waters, is within the waters, whom the waters do not know, whose body is the waters, who controls the waters from within: he is your self, the <s>antaryāmin</s>, immortal."

children.text: yo 'gnau tiṣṭhann agner antaro yam agnir na veda yasyāgniḥ śarīraṃ yo 'gnim antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "He who, standing in fire, is within fire, whom fire does not know, whose body is fire, who controls fire from within: he is your self, the <s>antaryāmin</s>, immortal."

children.text: yo 'ntarikṣe tiṣṭhann antarikṣād antaro yam antarikṣaṃ na veda yasyāntarikṣaṃ śarīraṃ yo 'ntarikṣam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "He who, standing in the midspace, is within the midspace, whom the midspace does not know, whose body is the midspace, who controls the midspace from within: he is your self, the <s>antaryāmin</s>, immortal."

children.text: yo vāyau tiṣṭhan vāyor antaro yaṃ vāyur na veda yasya vāyuḥ śarīraṃ yo vāyum antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "He who, standing in air, is within air, whom air does not know, whose body is air, who controls air from within: he is your self, the <s>antaryāmin</s>, immortal."

children.text: yo divi tiṣṭhan divo 'ntaro yaṃ dyaur na veda yasya dyauḥ śarīraṃ yo divam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "He who, standing in heaven, is within heaven, whom heaven does not know, whose body is heaven, who controls heaven from within: he is your self, the <s>antaryāmin</s>, immortal."

children.text: ya āditye tiṣṭhann ādityād antaro yam ādityo na veda yasyādityaḥ śarīraṃ ya ādityam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "He who, standing in the sun, is within the sun, whom the sun does not know, whose body is the sun, who controls the sun from within: he is your self, the <s>antaryāmin</s>, immortal."

children.text: yo dikṣu tiṣṭhan digbhyo 'ntaro yaṃ diśo na vidur yasya diśaḥ śarīraṃ yo diśo 'ntaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who stands in the directions, who is within the directions, whom the directions do not know, whose body is the directions, who controls the directions from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.

children.text: yaś candratārake tiṣṭhaṃścandratārakād antaro yaṃ candratārakaṃ na veda yasya candratārakaṃ śarīraṃ yaś candratārakam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who stands in the moon and stars, who is within the moon and stars, whom the moon and stars do not know, whose body is the moon and stars, who controls the moon and stars from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.

children.text: ya ākāśe tiṣṭhann ākāśād antaro yam ākāśo na veda yasyākāśaḥ śarīraṃ ya ākāśam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who stands in <s>ākāśa</s> (space), who is within <s>ākāśa</s>, whom <s>ākāśa</s> does not know, whose body is <s>ākāśa</s>, who controls <s>ākāśa</s> from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.

children.text: yas tamasi tiṣṭhaṃs tamaso 'ntaro yaṃ tamo na veda yasya tamaḥ śarīraṃ yas tamo 'ntaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who stands in darkness, who is within darkness, whom darkness does not know, whose body is darkness, who controls darkness from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.

children.text: yas tejasi tiṣṭhaṃs tejaso 'ntaro yaṃ tejo na veda yasya tejaḥ śarīraṃ yas tejo 'ntaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who stands in radiance, who is within radiance, whom radiance does not know, whose body is radiance, who controls radiance from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.
Now, with respect to beings.

children.text: yaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhan sarvebhyo bhūtebhyo 'ntaro yaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni na vidur yasya sarvāṇi bhūtāni śarīraṃ yaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāny antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: He who stands in all beings, who is within all beings, whom all beings do not know, whose body is all beings, who controls all beings from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.
So much with respect to beings.
Now, with respect to the self.

children.text: yaḥ prāṇe tiṣṭhan prāṇād antaro yaṃ prāṇo na veda yasya prāṇaḥ śarīraṃ yaḥ prāṇam antaro yamayati eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who stands in breath, who is within breath, whom breath does not know, whose body is breath, who controls breath from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.

children.text: yo vāci tiṣṭhan vāco 'ntaro yaṃ vāṅ na veda yasya vāk śarīraṃ yo vācam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who stands in speech, who is within speech, whom speech does not know, whose body is speech, who controls speech from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.

children.text: yaś cakṣuṣi tiṣṭhaṃścakṣuṣo 'ntaro yaṃ cakṣur na veda yasya cakṣuḥ śarīraṃ yaś cakṣur antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who stands in the eye, who is within the eye, whom the eye does not know, whose body is the eye, who controls the eye from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.

children.text: yaḥ śrotre tiṣṭhañchrotrād antaro yaṃ śrotraṃ na veda yasya śrotraṃ śarīraṃ yaḥ śrotram antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who stands in the ear, who is within the ear, whom the ear does not know, whose body is the ear, who controls the ear from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.

children.text: yo manasi tiṣṭhan manaso 'ntaro yaṃ mano na veda yasya manaḥ śarīraṃ yo mano 'ntaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who stands in the mind, who is within the mind, whom the mind does not know, whose body is the mind, who controls the mind from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.

children.text: yas tvaci tiṣṭhaṃs tvaco 'ntaro yaṃ tvaṅ na veda yasya tvak śarīraṃ yas tvacam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who stands in the skin, who is within the skin, whom the skin does not know, whose body is the skin, who controls the skin from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.

children.text: yo vijñāne tiṣṭhan vijñānād antaro yaṃ vijñānaṃ na veda yasya vijñānaṃ śarīraṃ yo vijñānam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who stands in cognition, who is within cognition, whom cognition does not know, whose body is cognition, who controls cognition from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.

children.text: yo retasi tiṣṭhan retaso 'ntaro yaṃ reto na veda yasya retaḥ śarīraṃ yo reto 'ntaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: He who stands in seed, who is within seed, whom seed does not know, whose body is seed, who controls seed from within: he is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.
Unseen, he is the seer; unheard, the hearer; unthought, the thinker; unknown, the knower.

children.text: nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā nānyo 'to 'sti śrotā nānyo 'to 'sti mantā nānyo 'to 'sti vijñātā
children.translated_text: There is no other seer than this; there is no other hearer than this; there is no other thinker than this; there is no other knower than this.
He is your <s>ātman</s> (self), the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the immortal.
Whatever is other than this is afflicted.
Then <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> fell silent.

children.text: atha ha vācaknavy uvāca brāhmaṇā bhagavanto hantāham imaṃ dvau praśnau prakṣyāmi
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vācaknavī</s> said, "Revered brahmins, come, I will ask this man two questions.
If he will answer them for me,

children.text: na vai jātu yuṣmākam imaṃ kaścid brahmodyaṃ jeteti
children.translated_text: then surely none of you will ever defeat him in this debate about <s>brahman</s>."
"Ask, <s>Gārgī</s>."

children.text: sā hovāca ahaṃ vai tvā yājñavalkya yathā kāśyo vā vaideho vograputra ujjyaṃ dhanur adhijyaṃ kṛtvā dvau bāṇavantau sapatnātivyādhinau haste kṛtvopottiṣṭhed evam evāhaṃ tvā dvābhyāṃ praśnābhyām upodasthām
children.translated_text: She said, "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, just as a man of <s>Kāśī</s> or <s>Videha</s>, the son of a warrior, might string an unstrung bow, take in his hand two enemy-piercing arrows, and rise up, so I have approached you with two questions.
Answer them for me."
"Ask, <s>Gārgī</s>."

children.text: sā hovāca yad ūrdhvaṃ yājñavalkya divo yad avāk pṛthivyā yadantarā dyāvāpṛthivī ime yad bhūtaṃ ca bhavac ca bhaviṣyac cety ācakṣate kasmiṃs tad otaṃ ca protaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: She said, "What is above heaven, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, what is below the earth, what is between these two, heaven and earth, and what they call the past, the present, and the future: in what is that woven, warp and woof?"

children.text: sa hovāca yad ūrdhvaṃ gārgi divo yad avāk pṛthivyā yadantarā dyāvāpṛthivī ime yad bhūtaṃ ca bhavac ca bhaviṣyac cety ācakṣata ākāśe tad otaṃ ca protaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "What is above heaven, <s>Gārgī</s>, what is below the earth, what is between these two, heaven and earth, and what they call the past, the present, and the future: that is woven, warp and woof, in <s>ākāśa</s> (space)."

children.text: sā hovāca namas te 'stu yājñavalkya yo ma etaṃ vyavoco 'parasmai dhārayasveti pṛccha gārgīti ||
children.translated_text: She said, "Reverence be to you, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, for you have explained this to me. Prepare yourself for the other question." "Ask, <s>Gārgī</s>."

children.text: sā hovāca yad ūrdhvaṃ yājñavalkya divo yad avāk pṛthivyā yadantarā dyāvāpṛthivī ime yad bhūtaṃ ca bhavac ca bhaviṣyac cety ācakṣate kasmiṃs tad otaṃ ca protaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: She said, "What is above heaven, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, what is below the earth, what is between these two, heaven and earth, and what they call the past, the present, and the future: in what is that woven, warp and woof?"

children.text: sa hovāca yad ūrdhvaṃ gārgi divo yad avāk pṛthivyā yadantarā dyāvāpṛthivī ime yad bhūtaṃ ca bhavac ca bhaviṣyac cety ācakṣata ākāśa eva tad otaṃ ca protaṃ ceti
children.translated_text: He said, "What is above heaven, <s>Gārgī</s>, what is below the earth, what is between these two, heaven and earth, and what they call the past, the present, and the future: that is woven, warp and woof, in <s>ākāśa</s> (space) alone."

children.text: kasmin nu khalv ākāśa otaś ca protaś ceti ||
children.translated_text: "In what, then, is <s>ākāśa</s> (space) woven, warp and woof?"

children.text: sa hovāca etad vai tad akṣaraṃ gārgi brāhmaṇā abhivadanty asthūlam anaṇv ahrasvam adīrgham alohitam asneham acchāyam atamo 'vāyv anākāśam asaṅgam arasam agandham acakṣuṣkam aśrotram avāg amano 'tejaskam aprāṇam amukham agātram anantaram abāhyam
children.translated_text: He said, "This indeed, <s>Gārgi</s>, is that imperishable which the brahmins describe: not coarse, not minute, not short, not long, not red, not fluid, without shadow, without darkness, without air, without space, unattached, without taste, without smell, without eye, without ear, without speech, without mind, without radiance, without breath, without mouth, without limbs, without interior, and without exterior.
It does not eat anything.
Nor does anyone eat it.

children.text: etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi sūryacandramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhataḥ
children.translated_text: Under the command of this imperishable, <s>Gārgi</s>, the sun and moon stand held in place.

children.text: etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi dyāvāpṛthivyau vidhṛte tiṣṭhataḥ
children.translated_text: Under the command of this imperishable, <s>Gārgi</s>, heaven and earth stand held in place.

children.text: etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi nimeṣā muhūrtā ahorātrāṇy ardhamāsā māsā ṛtavaḥ saṃvatsarā iti vidhṛtās tiṣṭhanti
children.translated_text: Under the command of this imperishable, <s>Gārgi</s>, instants, moments, days and nights, half-months, months, seasons, and years stand held in place.

children.text: etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi prācyo 'nyā nadyaḥ syandante śvetebhyaḥ parvatebhyaḥ pratīcyo 'nyā yāṃ yāṃ ca diśam anu
children.translated_text: Under the command of this imperishable, <s>Gārgi</s>, some rivers flow eastward from the white mountains, others westward, and others in whatever direction each takes.

children.text: etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi manuṣyāḥ praśasanti yajamānaṃ devā darvīṃ pitaro 'nvāyattāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Under the command of this imperishable, <s>Gārgi</s>, human beings praise the sacrificer; the gods and ancestors are dependent on the sacrificial ladle.

children.text: yo vā etad akṣaram gārgy aviditvāsmiṃlloke juhoti yajate tapas tapyate bahūni varṣasahasrāṇy antavad evāsya tad bhavati
children.translated_text: Whoever, <s>Gārgi</s>, without knowing this imperishable, offers oblations in this world, performs sacrifice, or practices austerity for many thousands of years, for him that becomes only finite.

children.text: yo vā etad akṣaram aviditvā gārgy aviditvāsmāllokāt praiti sa kṛpaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever, <s>Gārgi</s>, departs from this world without knowing this imperishable, without knowing it, is pitiable.

children.text: atha ya etad akṣaraṃ gārgi viditvāsmāl lokāt praiti sa brāhmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But whoever, <s>Gārgi</s>, departs from this world after knowing this imperishable, he is a brahmin in truth."

children.text: tad vā etad akṣaraṃ gārgy adṛṣṭaṃ draṣṭraśrutaṃ śrotramataṃ mantravijñātaṃ vijñātṛ
children.translated_text: This, then, <s>Gārgi</s>, is that imperishable: unseen, yet the seer; unheard, yet the hearer; unthought, yet the thinker; unknown, yet the knower.
There is no other seer than this.
There is no other hearer than this.
There is no other thinker than this.
There is no other knower than this.

children.text: etasmin nu khalv akṣare gārgy ākāśa otaś ca protaś ca ||
children.translated_text: In this very imperishable, <s>Gārgi</s>, space is woven, warp and woof."

children.text: sā hovāca brāhmaṇā bhagavantas tad eva bahu manyadhvaṃ yad asmān namaskāreṇa mucyedhvam
children.translated_text: She said, "Venerable brahmins, consider it a great thing indeed if you are released from him merely with a bow.

children.text: na vai jātu yuṣmākam imaṃ kaścid brahmodyaṃ jeteti
children.translated_text: Surely none among you will ever defeat him in this brahmodya (contest in sacred knowledge)."
Then <s>Vācaknavī</s> fell silent.

children.text: atha hainaṃ vidagdhaḥ śākalyaḥ papraccha kati devā yājñavalkyeti
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vidagdha Śākalya</s> asked him, "How many gods are there, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?"

children.text: sa haitayaiva nividā pratipede yāvanto vaiśvadevasya nividy ucyante
children.translated_text: He answered with this very nivid (invocatory formula): "As many as are mentioned in the nivid of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> rite."

children.text: trayaś ca trī ca śatā trayaś ca trī ca sahasreti
children.translated_text: "Three hundred and three, and three thousand and three."
"Om," he said.
"Just how many gods are there, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?"
"Thirty-three," he said.
"Om," he said.
"Just how many gods are there, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?"
"Six," he said.
"Om," he said.
"Just how many gods are there, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?"
"Three," he said.
"Om," he said.
"Just how many gods are there, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?"
"Two," he said.
"Om," he said.
"Just how many gods are there, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?"
"One and a half," he said.
"Om," he said.
"Just how many gods are there, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?"
"One," he said.
"Om," he said.

children.text: katame te trayaś ca trī ca śatā trayaś ca trī ca sahasreti ||
children.translated_text: "Which are those three hundred and three and three thousand and three?"
He said, "These are only their manifestations of greatness.
But the gods are in fact thirty-three."
"Which are those thirty-three?"

children.text: aṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityāḥ ta ekatriṃśad aindraś caiva prajāpatiś ca trayastriṃśāv iti ||
children.translated_text: "The eight <s>Vasu</s>s, the eleven <s>Rudra</s>s, and the twelve <s>Āditya</s>s: these are thirty-one; <s>Indra</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s> make the thirty-three."
"Which are the <s>Vasu</s>s?"

children.text: agniś ca pṛthivī ca vāyuś cāntarikṣaṃ cādityaś ca dyauḥ ca candramāś ca nakṣatrāṇi caite vasavaḥ
children.translated_text: "Fire, earth, wind, the midspace, the sun, heaven, the moon, and the stars: these are the <s>Vasu</s>s.

children.text: eteṣu hīdaṃ sarvaṃ vasu hitaṃ iti tasmād vasava iti ||
children.translated_text: For all this is placed in them as wealth; therefore they are called <s>Vasu</s>s."
"Which are the <s>Rudra</s>s?"
"These ten prāṇas (vital breaths) in a person, with the self as the eleventh.

children.text: te yadāsmāccharīrān martyād utkrāmanty atha rodayanti
children.translated_text: When they depart from this mortal body, then they make people weep.

children.text: tad yad rodayanti tasmād rudrā iti ||
children.translated_text: Because they make people weep, therefore they are called <s>Rudra</s>s."
"Which are the <s>Āditya</s>s?"
"The twelve months of the year: these are the <s>Āditya</s>s.
For they go on taking all this away.

children.text: te yad idaṃ sarvam ādadānā yanti tasmād ādityā iti ||
children.translated_text: Because they go on taking all this away, therefore they are called <s>Āditya</s>s."
"Which is <s>Indra</s>, and which is <s>Prajāpati</s>?"
"Thunder is <s>Indra</s>; sacrifice is <s>Prajāpati</s>."
"Which is thunder?"
"The lightning bolt," he said.
"Which is sacrifice?"
"The animals," he said.
"Which are the six?"

children.text: agniś ca pṛthivī ca vāyuś cāntarikṣaś cādityaś ca dyauś caite ṣaṭ
children.translated_text: "Fire, earth, wind, the midspace, the sun, and heaven: these are the six.
For all this is these six."
"Which are those three gods?"
"These very three worlds.
For in them are all these gods."
"Which are those two gods?"
"Food and prāṇa (vital breath)."
"Which is the one-and-a-half?"
"This one here that blows."

children.text: tad āhur yad ayam eka ivaiva pavate
children.translated_text: They say, "If this one blows as if it were one alone,
then how is it one and a half?"

children.text: yad asminn idaṃ sarvam adhyārdhnot tenādhyardha iti
children.translated_text: Because in it all this attains increase, therefore it is called one and a half.
"Which is the one god?"
"Prāṇa (vital breath)," he said.
They call it brahman, the 'that'."

children.text: pṛthivy eva yasyāyatanam agnir loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt
children.translated_text: "He whose abode is earth, whose world is fire, whose light is mind: whoever knows that person as the final goal of the whole self would indeed be a knower.

children.text: yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha
children.translated_text: <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I know that person, the final goal of the whole self, of whom you speak.

children.text: ya evāyaṃ śārīraḥ puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ
children.translated_text: This very person in the body is he.
Speak then, <s>Śākalya</s>: what is his deity?"
"Immortality," he said.

children.text: kāma eva yasyāyatanaṃ hṛdayaṃ loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt
children.translated_text: He whose abode is desire, whose world is the heart, whose light is the mind: whoever knows that person as the final refuge of every self would indeed be a knower.

children.text: yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha
children.translated_text: "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that person, the final refuge of every self, of whom you speak.

children.text: ya evāyaṃ kāmamayaḥ puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ
children.translated_text: That very person who consists of desire is this one.
Speak then, <s>Śākalya</s>: what is his deity?"
"Women," he said.

children.text: rūpāṇy eva yasyāyatanaṃ cakṣur loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt
children.translated_text: He whose abode is forms, whose world is the eye, whose light is the mind: whoever knows that person as the final refuge of every self would indeed be a knower.

children.text: yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha
children.translated_text: "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that person, the final refuge of every self, of whom you speak.

children.text: ya evāsāv āditye puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ
children.translated_text: That very person who is in the sun is this one.
Speak then, <s>Śākalya</s>: what is his deity?"
"Truth," he said.

children.text: ākāśa eva yasyāyatanaṃ śrotraṃ loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt
children.translated_text: He whose abode is space, whose world is hearing, whose light is the mind: whoever knows that person as the final refuge of every self would indeed be a knower.

children.text: yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha
children.translated_text: "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that person, the final refuge of every self, of whom you speak.

children.text: ya evāyam śrautaḥ prātiśrutkaḥ puruṣaḥ sa eṣa
children.translated_text: This very person who is heard and echoing is that one.
Speak then, <s>Śākalya</s>: what is his deity?"
"The directions," he said.

children.text: tama eva yasyāyatanaṃ hṛdayaṃ loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt
children.translated_text: He whose abode is darkness, whose world is the heart, whose light is the mind: whoever knows that person as the final refuge of every self would indeed be a knower.

children.text: yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha
children.translated_text: "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that person, the final refuge of every self, of whom you speak.

children.text: ya evāyaṃ chāyāmayaḥ puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ
children.translated_text: This very person who consists of shadow is that one.
Speak then, <s>Śākalya</s>: what is his deity?"
"Death," he said.

children.text: rūpāṇy eva yasyāyatanaṃ hṛdayaṃ loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt
children.translated_text: He whose abode is forms, whose world is the heart, whose light is the mind: whoever knows that person as the final refuge of every self would indeed be a knower.

children.text: yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha
children.translated_text: "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that person, the final refuge of every self, of whom you speak.

children.text: ya evāyam ādarśe puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ
children.translated_text: This very person who is in a mirror is that one.
Speak then, <s>Śākalya</s>: what is his deity?"
"Truth," he said.

children.text: āpa eva yasyāyatanaṃ hṛdayaṃ loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt
children.translated_text: He whose abode is the waters, whose world is the heart, whose light is the mind: whoever knows that person as the final refuge of every self would indeed be a knower.

children.text: yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha
children.translated_text: "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that person, the final refuge of every self, of whom you speak.

children.text: ya evāyaṃ apsu puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ
children.translated_text: This very person who is in the waters is that one.
Speak then, <s>Śākalya</s>: what is his deity?"
"<s>Varuṇa</s>," he said.

children.text: reta eva yasyāyatanaṃ hṛdayaṃ loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt
children.translated_text: He whose abode is seed, whose world is the heart, whose light is the mind: whoever knows that person as the final refuge of every self would indeed be a knower.

children.text: yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha
children.translated_text: "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that person, the final refuge of every self, of whom you speak.

children.text: ya evāyaṃ putramayaḥ puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ
children.translated_text: This very person who consists of a son is that one.
Speak then, <s>Śākalya</s>: what is his deity?"
"<s>Prajāpati</s>," he said.
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said, "<s>Śākalya</s>,

children.text: tvāṃ svid ime brāhmaṇā aṅgārāvakṣayaṇam akratā3 iti ||
children.translated_text: have these brahmins perhaps made you into a fire-pan for coals?"
<s>Śākalya</s> said, "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,

children.text: yad idaṃ kurupañcālānāṃ brāhmaṇān atyavadīḥ kiṃ brahma vidvān iti
children.translated_text: since you have spoken beyond these brahmins of the <s>Kuru-Pañcālas</s>, as though knowing <s>brahman</s>, what <s>brahman</s> do you know?"
"I know the directions together with their deities and their supports."
"If you know the directions together with their deities and their supports,
with what deity are you in this eastern direction?"
"With <s>Āditya</s> as deity."
"In what is that <s>Āditya</s> supported?"
"In the eye."
"In what, then, is the eye supported?"
"In forms."
For with the eye one sees forms.
"In what, then, are forms supported?"
"In the heart," he said.
For by the heart one knows forms.

children.text: hṛdaye hy eva rūpāṇi pratiṣṭhitāni bhavantīti
children.translated_text: Indeed, forms are supported in the heart itself.
"Just so, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>."
"With what deity are you in this southern direction?"
"With <s>Yama</s> as deity."
"In what is that <s>Yama</s> supported?"
"In the sacrifice."
"In what, then, is the sacrifice supported?"
"In the sacrificial gift."
"In what, then, is the sacrificial gift supported?"
"In faith."

children.text: yadā hy eva śraddhatte 'tha dakṣiṇāṃ dadāti
children.translated_text: For only when one has faith does one give a sacrificial gift.
Indeed, the sacrificial gift is supported in faith itself.
"In what, then, is faith supported?"
"In the heart," he said.
For by the heart one knows faith.

children.text: hṛdaye hy eva śraddhā pratiṣṭhitā bhavatīti
children.translated_text: Indeed, faith is supported in the heart itself.
"Just so, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>."
"With what deity are you in this western direction?"
"With <s>Varuṇa</s> as deity."
"In what is that <s>Varuṇa</s> supported?"
"In the waters."
"In what, then, are the waters supported?"
"In seed."
"In what, then, is seed supported?"
"In the heart."

children.text: tasmād api pratirūpaṃ jātam āhur hṛdayād iva sṛpto hṛdayād iva nirmita iti
children.translated_text: Therefore, when a likeness is born, they even say, "He seems to have slipped from the heart; he seems to have been formed from the heart."

children.text: hṛdaye hy eva retaḥ pratiṣṭhitaṃ bhavatīti
children.translated_text: Indeed, seed is supported in the heart itself.
"Just so, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>."
"With what deity are you in this northern direction?"
"With <s>Soma</s> as deity."
"In what is that <s>Soma</s> supported?"
"In consecration."
"In what, then, is consecration supported?"
"In truth."

children.text: tasmād api dīkṣitam āhuḥ satyaṃ vadeti
children.translated_text: Therefore they even say to one who has been consecrated, "Speak truth."
Indeed, consecration is supported in truth itself.
"In what, then, is truth supported?"
"In the heart," he said.
For by the heart one knows truth.

children.text: hṛdaye hy eva satyaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ bhavatīti
children.translated_text: For truth is established in the heart itself.
Just so is this, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
What deity do you have in this fixed direction?
Fire is the deity.
In what is that fire established?
In speech.
In what, then, is speech established?
In the heart.
In what, then, is the heart established?
"You fool," said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
Where would you suppose this to be, other than in ourselves?

children.text: yaddhyetad anyatrāsmat syācchvāno vainad adyur vayāṃsi vainad vimathnīran iti ||
children.translated_text: For if this were somewhere other than ourselves, dogs would surely eat it, or birds would tear it apart.

children.text: kasmin nu tvaṃ cātmā ca pratiṣṭhitau stha iti
children.translated_text: In what, then, are you and the <s>ātman</s> (self) established?
In <s>prāṇa</s> (breath).
In what, then, is <s>prāṇa</s> established?
In <s>apāna</s> (downward breath).
In what, then, is <s>apāna</s> established?
In <s>vyāna</s> (pervading breath).
In what, then, is <s>vyāna</s> established?
In <s>udāna</s> (upward breath).
In what, then, is <s>udāna</s> established?
In <s>samāna</s> (balancing breath).
This is that <s>ātman</s> (self) of "not this, not this."
It is ungraspable, for it is not grasped.
It is undecaying, for it does not decay.
It is unattached, for it does not attach itself.
It is unbound; it does not suffer pain.
It is not injured.

children.text: etāny aṣṭāv āyatanāny aṣṭau lokā aṣṭau devā aṣṭau puruṣāḥ
children.translated_text: These are the eight abodes, the eight worlds, the eight gods, and the eight persons.

children.text: sa yas tān puruṣān niruhya pratyuhyātyakrāmat taṃ tvaupaniṣadaṃ puruṣaṃ pṛcchāmi
children.translated_text: Having drawn out those persons and put them back, he passed beyond them; I ask you about that Upaniṣadic person.

children.text: taṃ cen me na vivakṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti
children.translated_text: If you will not explain him to me, your head will fall apart.
<s>Śākalya</s> did not know him.
Then his head fell apart.

children.text: api hāsya parimoṣiṇo 'sthīny apajahrur anyan manyamānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And thieves even carried off his bones, thinking them to be something else.

children.text: atha hovāca brāhmaṇā bhagavanto yo vaḥ kāmayate sa mā pṛcchatu
children.translated_text: Then he said, "Revered brahmins, whichever of you wishes may question me.
Or all of you may question me.

children.text: yo vaḥ kāmayate taṃ vaḥ pṛcchāmi sarvān vā vaḥ pṛcchāmīti
children.translated_text: Whichever of you wishes, I will question him, or I will question all of you."
Those brahmins did not dare.
He questioned them with these verses:
As a tree, a lord of the forest, is, so indeed is a person; this is no falsehood.

children.text: tasya lomāni parṇāni tvag asyotpāṭikā bahiḥ ||
children.translated_text: His hairs are its leaves; his skin is its outer bark.

children.text: tvaca evāsya rudhiraṃ prasyandi tvaca utpaṭaḥ
children.translated_text: From his skin the blood flows, just as sap flows from the bark.

children.text: tasmāt tad ātṛṇṇāt praiti raso vṛkṣād ivāhatāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, from one who is wounded, the fluid comes forth, as from a tree that has been struck.

children.text: māṃsāny asya śakarāṇi kināṭaṃ snāva tat sthiram
children.translated_text: His flesh is its inner bark; his sinews are the firm fibrous layer.

children.text: asthīny antarato dāruṇi majjā majjopamā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: His bones within are the wood; the marrow has been made like marrow.

children.text: yad vṛkṣo vṛkṇo rohati mūlān navataraḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: When a tree, cut down, grows again, newer from its roots,

children.text: martyaḥ svin mṛtyunā vṛkṇaḥ kasmān mūlāt prarohati ||
children.translated_text: from what root does a mortal, cut down by death, grow forth again?

children.text: retasa iti mā vocata jīvatas tat prajāyate
children.translated_text: Do not say, "From semen," for that is produced from one who is alive.

children.text: dhānāruha iva vai vṛkṣo 'ñjasā pretya sambhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Like a tree that sprouts from grain, there is indeed, plainly, arising after death.

children.text: yat samūlam āvṛheyur vṛkṣaṃ na punar ābhavet
children.translated_text: If they were to pull up a tree with its root, it would not come back again.

children.text: martyaḥ svin mṛtyunā vṛkṇaḥ kasmān mūlāt prarohati ||
children.translated_text: From what root does a mortal, cut down by death, grow forth again?

children.text: jāta eva na jāyate ko nv enaṃ janayet punaḥ
children.translated_text: Once born, he is not born again; who indeed would beget him again?

children.text: vijñānam ānandaṃ brahma rātir dātuḥ parāyaṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is knowledge and bliss, the delight and highest goal of the giver.

children.text: jāta eva na jāyate ko nvenaṃ janayet punaḥ
children.translated_text: Once born, he is not born again; who indeed would beget him again?

children.text: vijñānam ānandaṃ brahma rātir dātuḥ parāyaṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is knowledge and bliss, the delight and highest goal of the giver.
That belongs to the one who abides, knowing it.
<s>Janaka Vaideha</s> was seated.
Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> came near.

children.text: taṃ hovāca yājñavalkya kimartham acārīḥ paśūn icchan aṇvantānīti
children.translated_text: He said to him, "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, for what purpose have you come: desiring cattle, or subtle questions?"
"Both, O king," he said.
"Let us hear whatever anyone has told you."

children.text: abravīn me jitvā śailiniḥ vāg vai brahmeti
children.translated_text: "<s>Jitvan Śailini</s> told me, 'Speech indeed is <s>brahman</s>.'"

children.text: yathā mātṛmān pitṛmān ācāryavān brūyāt tathā tacchailinir abravīd vāg vai brahmeti
children.translated_text: "As one who has a mother, a father, and a teacher would speak, so <s>Śailini</s> spoke: 'Speech indeed is <s>brahman</s>.'
For what would there be for one who could not speak?
But did he tell you its abode and support?"
"He did not tell me."
"This, O king, is indeed one-footed."
"Then tell it to us, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>."

children.text: vāg evāyatanam ākāśaḥ pratiṣṭhā prajñety enad upāsīta
children.translated_text: "Speech itself is its abode; <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is its support. One should worship it as insight."
"What is its being insight, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?"
"Speech itself, O king," he said.
"For through speech, O king, a kinsman is recognized.

children.text: ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvāṅgirasa itihāsaḥ purāṇaṃ vidyā upaniṣadaḥ ślokāḥ sūtrāṇy anuvyākhyānāni vyākhyānānīṣṭaṃ hutam āśitaṃ pāyitam ayaṃ ca lokaḥ paraś ca lokaḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni vācaiva saṃrāṭ prajñāyante
