children.translated_text: Through speech alone, O king, the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s>, history, ancient lore, sciences, Upaniṣads, verses, sūtras, explanations, commentaries, what has been sacrificed, what has been offered, what has been eaten, what has been drunk, this world, the other world, and all beings are known.
Speech indeed, O king, is the highest <s>brahman</s>.
Speech does not abandon him.
All beings flow toward him.
Having become a god, he goes to the gods,
who, knowing thus, worships this."

children.text: hastyṛṣabhaṃ sahasraṃ dadāmīti hovāca janako vaidehaḥ
children.translated_text: "I give a thousand bulls as large as elephants," said <s>Janaka Vaideha</s>.

children.text: sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ pitā me 'manyata nānanuśiṣya hareteti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said, "My father held that one should not take without having instructed."

children.text: yad eva te kaścid abravīt tacchṛṇavāmeti
children.translated_text: "Let us hear whatever anyone has told you."
"<s>Udaṅka Śaulbāyana</s> told me,
'<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is <s>brahman</s>.'"

children.text: yathā mātṛmān pitṛmān ācāryavān brūyāt tathā tacchaulbāyano 'bravīt prāṇo vai brahmeti
children.translated_text: "As one who has a mother, a father, and a teacher would speak, so <s>Śaulbāyana</s> spoke: '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is <s>brahman</s>.'
For what would there be for one who did not breathe?
But did he tell you its abode and support?"
"He did not tell me."
"This, O king, is indeed one-footed."
"Then tell it to us, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>."
"<s>Prāṇa</s> itself is its abode; <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is its support.
One should worship it as dear."
"What is its being dear, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?"
"<s>Prāṇa</s> itself, O king," he said.
"For for the sake of <s>prāṇa</s>, O king, one causes a person unfit to sacrifice to perform sacrifice,
and one accepts from a person from whom one should not accept."

children.text: api tatra vadhāśaṅkā bhavati yāṃ diśam eti prāṇasyaiva samrāṭ kāmāya
children.translated_text: Even there there is fear of being killed, in whatever direction he goes, for the sake of <s>prāṇa</s>, O king.
<s>Prāṇa</s>, O king, is the supreme <s>brahman</s>.
<s>Prāṇa</s> does not abandon him.
All beings stream toward him.
Having become a god, he goes to the gods,
whoever, knowing thus, worships this.

children.text: hastyṛṣabhaṃ sahasraṃ dadāmīti hovāca janako vaidehaḥ
children.translated_text: "I give a thousand bulls as large as elephants," said <s>Janaka Vaideha</s>.

children.text: sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ pitā me 'manyata nānanuśiṣya hareteti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said, "My father thought that one should not take anything without having instructed."

children.text: yad eva te kaścid abravīt tacchṛṇavāmeti
children.translated_text: "Whatever anyone has told you, let us hear that."
"<s>Barku Vārṣṇa</s> told me,
'The eye indeed is <s>brahman</s>.'

children.text: yathā mātṛmān pitṛmān ācāryavān brūyāt tathā tad vārṣṇo 'bravīc cakṣur vai brahmeti
children.translated_text: Just as one with a mother, a father, and a teacher might speak, so <s>Vārṣṇa</s> said this: 'The eye indeed is <s>brahman</s>.'
For what would there be for one who did not see?"
"But did he tell you its abode and support?"
"He did not tell me."
"This, O king, is only one-footed."
"Then tell it to us, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>."
"The eye itself is its abode; space is its support.
One should worship it as truth."
"What is its truthfulness, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?"
"The eye itself, O king," he said.

children.text: cakṣuṣā vai samrāṭ paśyantam āhur adrākṣīr iti
children.translated_text: "For when a man is seeing with the eye, O king, people say to him, 'Did you see?'

children.text: sa āhādrākṣam iti tat satyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: He says, 'I saw'; that becomes true.
The eye, O king, is the supreme <s>brahman</s>.
The eye does not abandon him.
All beings stream toward him.
Having become a god, he goes to the gods,
whoever, knowing thus, worships this."

children.text: hastyṛṣabhaṃ sahasraṃ dadāmīti hovāca janako vaidehaḥ
children.translated_text: "I give a thousand bulls as large as elephants," said <s>Janaka Vaideha</s>.

children.text: sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ pitā me 'manyata nānanuśiṣya hareteti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said, "My father thought that one should not take anything without having instructed."

children.text: yad eva te kaścid abravīt tacchṛṇavāmeti
children.translated_text: "Whatever anyone has told you, let us hear that."
"<s>Gardabhīvipīta Bhāradvāja</s> told me,
'Hearing indeed is <s>brahman</s>.'

children.text: yathā mātṛmān pitṛmān ācāryavān brūyāt tathā tad bhāradvājo 'bravīcchrotraṃ vai brahmeti
children.translated_text: Just as one with a mother, a father, and a teacher might speak, so <s>Bhāradvāja</s> said this: 'Hearing indeed is <s>brahman</s>.'
For what would there be for one who did not hear?"
"But did he tell you its abode and support?"
"He did not tell me."
"This, O king, is only one-footed."
"Then tell it to us, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>."

children.text: śrotram evāyatanam ākāśaḥ pratiṣṭhānantam ity enad upāsīta
children.translated_text: "Hearing itself is its abode; space is its support. One should worship it as endless."
"What is its endlessness, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?"
"The directions themselves, O king," he said.

children.text: tasmād vai samrāḍ api yāṃ kāṃ ca diśaṃ gacchati naivāsyā antaṃ gacchati
children.translated_text: "Therefore, O king, in whatever direction a man goes, he never reaches its end.
For the directions are endless.
The directions, O king, are hearing.
Hearing, O king, is the supreme <s>brahman</s>.
Hearing does not abandon him.
All beings stream toward him.
Having become a god, he goes to the gods,
whoever, knowing thus, worships this."

children.text: hastyṛṣabhaṃ sahasraṃ dadāmīti hovāca janako vaidehaḥ
children.translated_text: "I give a thousand bulls as large as elephants," said <s>Janaka Vaideha</s>.

children.text: sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ pitā me 'manyata nānanuśiṣya hareteti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said, "My father thought that one should not take anything without having instructed."

children.text: yad eva te kaścid abravīt tacchṛṇavāmeti
children.translated_text: "Whatever anyone has told you, let us hear that."

children.text: abravīn me satyakāmo jābālaḥ mano vai brahmeti
children.translated_text: "<s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s> told me, 'Mind indeed is <s>brahman</s>.'

children.text: yathā mātṛmān pitṛmān ācāryavān brūyāt tathā taj jābālo 'bravīn mano vai brahmeti
children.translated_text: Just as one with a mother, a father, and a teacher might speak, so <s>Jābāla</s> said this: 'Mind indeed is <s>brahman</s>.'
For what would there be for one without mind?"
"But did he tell you its abode and support?"
"He did not tell me."
"This, O king, is only one-footed."
"Then tell it to us, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>."

children.text: mana evāyatanam ākāśaḥ pratiṣṭhānanda ity enad upāsīta
children.translated_text: "Mind itself is its abode; space is its support. One should worship it as bliss."
"What is its blissfulness, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?"

children.text: mana eva samrāḍ iti hovāca manasā vai samrāṭ striyam abhi hāryati tasyāṃ pratirūpaḥ putro jāyate
children.translated_text: "Mind itself, O king," he said. "For by the mind, O king, a man desires a woman; in her a son resembling him is born.
That is bliss.
Mind, O king, is the supreme <s>brahman</s>.
Mind does not abandon him.
All beings stream toward him.
Having become a god, he goes to the gods,
whoever, knowing thus, worships this."

children.text: hastyṛṣabhaṃ sahasraṃ dadāmīti hovāca janako vaidehaḥ
children.translated_text: "I give a thousand bulls as large as elephants," said <s>Janaka Vaideha</s>.

children.text: sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ pitā me 'manyata nānanuśiṣya hareteti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said, "My father thought that one should not take anything without having instructed."

children.text: yad eva te kaścid abravīt tacchṛṇavāmeti
children.translated_text: "Whatever anyone has told you, let us hear that."
"<s>Vidagdha Śākalya</s> told me,
'The heart indeed is <s>brahman</s>.'

children.text: yathā mātṛmān pitṛmān ācāryavān brūyāt tathā tacchākalyo 'bravīddhṛdayaṃ vai brahmeti
children.translated_text: Just as one with a mother, a father, and a teacher might speak, so <s>Śākalya</s> said this: 'The heart indeed is <s>brahman</s>.'
For what would there be for one without a heart?"
"But did he tell you its abode and support?"
"He did not tell me."
"This, O king, is only one-footed."
"Then tell it to us, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>."
"The heart itself is its abode; space is its support.
One should worship it as stability."
"What is its stability, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?"
"The heart itself, O king," he said.

children.text: hṛdayaṃ vai samrāṭ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām āyatanam
children.translated_text: "The heart, O king, is the abode of all beings.

children.text: hṛdayaṃ vai samrāṭ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ pratiṣṭhā
children.translated_text: The heart, O king, is the support of all beings.

children.text: hṛdaye hy eva samrāṭ sarvāṇi bhūtāni pratiṣṭhitāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: For in the heart itself, O king, all beings become established.
The heart, O king, is the supreme <s>brahman</s>.
The heart does not abandon him.
All beings stream toward him.
Having become a god, he goes to the gods,
whoever, knowing thus, worships this."

children.text: hastyṛṣabhaṃ sahasraṃ dadāmīti hovāca janako vaidehaḥ
children.translated_text: "I give a thousand bulls as large as elephants," said <s>Janaka Vaideha</s>.

children.text: sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ pitā me 'manyata nānanuśiṣya hareteti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said, "My father thought that one should not take anything without having instructed."

children.text: janako ha vaidehaḥ kūrcād upāvasarpann uvāca namas te 'stu yājñavalkya
children.translated_text: Then <s>Janaka Vaideha</s>, sliding down from his seat, said, "Reverence to you, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
Instruct me."

children.text: sa hovāca yathā vai samrāṇ mahāntam adhvānam eṣyan rathaṃ vā nāvaṃ vā samādadītaivam evaitābhir upaniṣadbhiḥ samāhitātmāsi
children.translated_text: He said: "Just as, O emperor, one about to go on a long journey would get ready a chariot or a boat, so you too are one whose self has been readied by these <s>upaniṣad</s> teachings.

children.text: evaṃ vṛndāraka āḍhyaḥ sann adhītaveda uktopaniṣatka ito vimucyamānaḥ kva gamiṣyasīti
children.translated_text: So, venerable one, being prosperous, having studied the Veda, and having been taught the <s>upaniṣad</s>, when you are released from here, where will you go?"

children.text: nāhaṃ tad bhagavan veda yatra gamiṣyāmīti
children.translated_text: "I do not know that, reverend sir, where I shall go."

children.text: atha vai te 'haṃ tad vakṣyāmi yatra gamiṣyasīti
children.translated_text: "Then I shall tell you where you will go."
"Let the reverend sir speak," he said.

children.text: indho ha vai nāmaiṣa yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣan puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>Indha</s>, indeed, is the name of this person who is in the right eye.

children.text: taṃ vā etam indhaṃ santam indra ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇaiva
children.translated_text: Although he is <s>Indha</s>, they call him <s>Indra</s> indirectly,
for the gods seem to love what is indirect and to dislike what is direct.

children.text: athaitad vāme 'kṣaṇi puruṣarūpam eṣāsya patnī virāṭ
children.translated_text: Now this person-form in the left eye is his wife, <s>Virāj</s>.

children.text: tayor eṣa saṃstāvo ya eṣo 'ntar hṛdaya ākāśaḥ
children.translated_text: Their meeting-place is this space within the heart.

children.text: athainayor etad annaṃ ya eṣo 'ntar hṛdaye lohitapiṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Their food is this red lump within the heart.

children.text: athainayor etat prāvaraṇaṃ yad etad antar hṛdaye jālakam iva
children.translated_text: Their covering is this net-like structure within the heart.

children.text: athainayor eṣā sṛtiḥ saṃcaraṇī yaiṣā hṛdayād ūrdhvā nāḍy uccarati
children.translated_text: Their path, their way of moving about, is this channel that goes upward from the heart.

children.text: yathā keśaḥ sahasradhā bhinna evam asyaitā hitā nāma nāḍyo 'ntar hṛdaye pratiṣṭhitā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Just as a hair split into a thousand parts, so these channels called <s>hitā</s> are established within his heart.
Through these, this flows out and flows along.

children.text: tasmād eṣa praviviktāhāratara iva bhavaty asmācchārīrād ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this one comes to have food that is, as it were, more refined than that of this bodily self.
His eastern direction is the eastward vital breaths.
The southern direction is the southward vital breaths.
The western direction is the westward vital breaths.
The northern direction is the northward vital breaths.
The upward direction is the upward vital breaths.
The downward direction is the downward vital breaths.
All directions are all the vital breaths.
This self is the one described as 'not this, not this.'
It is ungraspable, for it is not grasped.
It is undecaying, for it does not decay.
It is unattached, for it is not attached.
It is unbound; it does not suffer pain.
It is not injured.

children.text: abhayaṃ vai janaka prāpto 'sīti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ
children.translated_text: 'You have attained fearlessness, <s>Janaka</s>,' said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: sa hovāca janako vaideho 'bhayaṃ tvā gacchatād yājñavalkya yo no bhagavann abhayaṃ vedayase
children.translated_text: <s>Janaka Vaideha</s> said: 'May fearlessness come to you, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, reverend sir, since you make us know fearlessness.
Homage to you.
These <s>Videhas</s> are yours; I myself am yours.'"
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> went to <s>Janaka Vaideha</s>.
"I will converse with him," he thought.

children.text: atha ha yaj janakaś ca vaideho yājñavalkyaś cāgnihotre samūdāte
children.translated_text: Now, when <s>Janaka Vaideha</s> and <s>Yājñavalkya</s> had come together in discourse about the <s>agnihotra</s> ritual,
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> gave him a boon.
He chose only the boon of asking questions at will.
He granted it to him.

children.text: taṃ ha samrāḍ eva pūrvaḥ papraccha ||
children.translated_text: The emperor himself questioned him first.
"<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, what is the light of this person?"
"The sun is his light, O emperor," he said.

children.text: ādityenaivāyaṃ jyotiṣāste palyayate karma kurute vipalyetīti
children.translated_text: "With the sun as light, this person sits, moves about, does work, and returns."
"Just so indeed, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: astamita āditye yājñavalkya kiṃjyotir evāyaṃ puruṣa iti
children.translated_text: When the sun has set, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, what exactly is the light of this person?"
"The moon becomes his light."

children.text: candramasaivāyaṃ jyotiṣāste palyayate karma kurute vipalyetīti
children.translated_text: "With the moon as light, this person sits, moves about, does work, and returns."
"Just so indeed, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: astamita āditye yājñavalkya candramasy astamite kiṃjyotir evāyaṃ puruṣa iti
children.translated_text: When the sun has set, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, and the moon has set, what exactly is the light of this person?"
"Fire becomes his light."

children.text: agninaiva jyotiṣāste palyayate karma kurute vipalyetīti
children.translated_text: "With fire as light, this person sits, moves about, does work, and returns."
"Just so indeed, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: astamita āditye yājñavalkya candramasy astamite śānte 'gnau kiṃjyotir evāyaṃ puruṣa iti
children.translated_text: When the sun has set, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, the moon has set, and the fire is extinguished, what exactly is the light of this person?"
"Speech becomes his light."

children.text: vācaivāyaṃ jyotiṣāste palyayate karma kurute vipalyeti
children.translated_text: "With speech as light, this person sits, moves about, does work, and returns.

children.text: tasmād vai samrāḍ api yatra svaḥ pāṇir na vinirjñāyate 'tha yatra vāg uccaraty upaiva tatra nyetīti
children.translated_text: Therefore, O emperor, even where one's own hand cannot be distinguished, when speech is uttered, one goes toward that place."
"Just so indeed, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: astamita āditye yājñavalkya candramasy astamite śānte 'gnau śāntāyāṃ vāci kiṃjyotir evāyaṃ puruṣa iti
children.translated_text: When the sun has set, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, the moon has set, the fire is extinguished, and speech has fallen silent, what exactly is the light of this person?"
"The self itself becomes his light."

children.text: ātmanaivāyaṃ jyotiṣāste palyayate karma kurute vipalyetīti ||
children.translated_text: "With the self as light, this person sits, moves about, does work, and returns."

children.text: katama ātmeti yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣu hṛdy antarjyotiḥ puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: "Which self is it?" "This person here, made of cognition among the vital breaths, the inner light within the heart.

children.text: sa samānaḥ sann ubhau lokāv anusaṃcarati dhyāyatīva lelāyatīva
children.translated_text: Being the same, he moves through both worlds; he seems to meditate, he seems to stir.

children.text: sa hi svapno bhūtvemaṃ lokam atikrāmati mṛtyo rūpāṇi ||
children.translated_text: For, having become dream, he passes beyond this world and beyond the forms of death.

children.text: sa vā ayaṃ puruṣo jāyamānaḥ śarīram abhisaṃpadyamānaḥ pāpmabhiḥ saṃsṛjyate
children.translated_text: When this person is born and comes into a body, he becomes connected with evils.
When he departs, dying, he leaves those evils behind.

children.text: tasya vā etasya puruṣasya dve eva sthāne bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: For this person there are precisely two abodes:
this world and the abode of the other world.
There is a third, intermediate abode, the abode of dream.

children.text: tasmin saṃdhye sthāne tiṣṭhan ubhe sthāne paśyatīdaṃ ca paralokasthānaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Standing in that intermediate abode, he sees both abodes, this one and the abode of the other world.
Then, according to the approach he has in the other-worldly abode,

children.text: tam ākramam ākramyobhayān pāpmana ānandāṃś ca paśyati
children.translated_text: taking up that approach, he sees both evils and joys.

children.text: sa yatra prasvapity asya lokasya sarvāvato mātrām apādāya svayaṃ vihatya svayaṃ nirmāya svena bhāsā svena jyotiṣā prasvapiti
children.translated_text: When he falls asleep, taking the material from this entire world, himself breaking it apart and himself building it up, he sleeps by his own radiance, by his own light.
Here this person becomes self-luminous.

children.text: na tatra rathā na rathayogā na panthāno bhavanti
children.translated_text: There there are no chariots, no chariot-yokes, and no roads.
Then he creates chariots, chariot-yokes, and roads.
There there are no delights, joys, or rejoicings.
Then he creates delights, joys, and rejoicings.

children.text: na tatra veśāntāḥ puṣkariṇyaḥ sravantyo bhavanti
children.translated_text: There there are no tanks, lotus-ponds, or flowing streams.
Then he creates tanks, lotus-ponds, and flowing streams.
For he is the maker.
On this there are these verses:
By means of dream, having struck down what belongs to the body, though not asleep, he gazes upon those who are asleep.

children.text: śukram ādāya punar aiti sthānaṃ hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣa ekahaṃsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Taking the shining element, the golden person, the single swan, returns again to his place.

children.text: prāṇena rakṣann avaraṃ kulāyaṃ bahiṣkulāyād amṛtaś caritvā
children.translated_text: Protecting the lower nest by breath, having gone forth immortal from the nest,

children.text: sa īyate 'mṛto yatrakāmaṃ hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣa ekahaṃsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the immortal one, the golden person, the single swan, goes wherever he desires.

children.text: svapnānta uccāvacam īyamāno rūpāṇi devaḥ kurute bahūni
children.translated_text: Moving up and down in the realm of dream, the god makes many forms.

children.text: uteva strībhiḥ saha modamāno jakṣad utevāpi bhayāni paśyan ||
children.translated_text: As if rejoicing together with women, or laughing, or even seeing terrors.

children.text: ārāmam asya paśyanti na taṃ paśyati kaścaneti
children.translated_text: They see his pleasure-ground, but no one sees him.
Therefore they say, "One should not wake him suddenly."

children.text: durbhiṣajyaṃ hāsmai bhavati yam eṣa na pratipadyate
children.translated_text: For this becomes hard to cure for him, if he does not return to this body.

children.text: atho khalv āhur jāgaritadeśa evāsyaiṣa iti
children.translated_text: But others say, "This is only his waking place."

children.text: yāni hy eva jāgrat paśyati tāni supta iti
children.translated_text: For whatever he sees while awake, that he sees while asleep.
Here this person becomes self-luminous.
"So I give a thousand to your reverence.
Speak further for the sake of liberation."

children.text: sa vā eṣa etasmin saṃprasāde ratvā caritvā dṛṣṭvaiva puṇyaṃ ca pāpaṃ ca punaḥ pratinyāyaṃ pratiyony ādravati svapnāyaiva
children.translated_text: Now this person, having delighted, wandered, and seen good and evil in this state of serenity, returns again in reverse order to his former source, only for dream.

children.text: sa yat tatra kiṃcit paśyaty ananvāgatas tena bhavati
children.translated_text: Whatever he sees there, he is not followed by that.
For this person is unattached.
"Just so, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
So I give a thousand to your reverence.
Speak further only for the sake of liberation."

children.text: sa vā eṣa etasmin svapne ratvā caritvā dṛṣṭvaiva puṇyaṃ ca pāpaṃ ca punaḥ pratinyāyaṃ pratiyony ādravati buddhāntāyaiva
children.translated_text: Now this person, having delighted, wandered, and seen good and evil in this dream, returns again in reverse order to his former source, only to the waking state.

children.text: sa yat tatra kiṃcit paśyaty ananvāgatas tena bhavati
children.translated_text: Whatever he sees there, he is not followed by that.
For this person is unattached.
"Just so, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
So I give a thousand to your reverence.
Speak further only for the sake of liberation."

children.text: sa vā eṣa etasmin buddhānte ratvā caritvā dṛṣṭvaiva puṇyaṃ ca pāpaṃ ca punaḥ pratinyāyaṃ pratiyony ādravati svapnāntāyaiva ||
children.translated_text: Now this person, having delighted, wandered, and seen good and evil in this waking state, returns again in reverse order to his former source, only to the realm of dream.

children.text: tad yathā mahāmatsya ubhe kūle anusaṃcarati pūrvaṃ cāparaṃ ca
children.translated_text: As a great fish moves along both banks, the near one and the far one,

children.text: evam evāyaṃ puruṣa etāv ubhāv antāv anusaṃcarati svapnāntaṃ ca buddhāntaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: so this person moves along both these ends, the dream state and the waking state.

children.text: tad yathāsminn ākāśe śyeno vā suparṇo vā viparipatya śrāntaḥ saṃhatya pakṣau saṃlayāyaiva dhriyate
children.translated_text: As in this sky a falcon or eagle, after flying about and becoming tired, folds its wings and is borne down to rest,

children.text: evam evāyaṃ puruṣa etasmā antāya dhavati
children.translated_text: so this person runs toward that end

children.text: yatra supto na kaṃcana kāmaṃ kāmayate na kaṃcana svapnaṃ paśyati ||
children.translated_text: where, asleep, he desires no desire at all and sees no dream at all.

children.text: tā vā asyaitā hitā nāma nāḍyo yathā keśaḥ sahasradhā bhinnas tāvatāṇimnā tiṣṭhanti
children.translated_text: These, indeed, are his channels called hitā; they are as fine as a hair split a thousandfold.

children.text: śuklasya nīlasya piṅgalasya haritasya lohitasya pūrṇāḥ
children.translated_text: They are filled with white, blue, tawny, green, and red.

children.text: atha yatrainaṃ ghnantīva jinantīva hastīva vicchāyayati gartam iva patati
children.translated_text: Now when it seems that people strike him, or overcome him, or that an elephant chases him, or that he falls into a pit,

children.text: yad eva jāgrad bhayaṃ paśyati tad atrāvidyayā manyate
children.translated_text: whatever fear he sees while awake, that he imagines here through ignorance.

children.text: atha yatra deva iva rājevāham evedaṃ sarvo 'smīti manyate
children.translated_text: But when he thinks, "As if I were a god, as if I were a king; I alone am all this,"
that is his highest world.
Indeed, this is his form beyond desire, free from evil and free from fear.

children.text: tad yathā priyayā striyā sampariṣvakto na bāhyaṃ kiṃcana veda nāntaram
children.translated_text: As a man embraced by a beloved woman knows nothing external and nothing internal,

children.text: evam evāyaṃ puruṣaḥ prājñenātmanā sampariṣvakto na bāhyaṃ kiṃcana veda nāntaram
children.translated_text: so this person, embraced by the knowing self, knows nothing external and nothing internal.

children.text: tad vā asyaitad āptakāmam ātmakāmam akāmaṃ rūpam śokāntaram ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, this is his form whose desire is fulfilled, whose desire is the self, free from desire, and beyond sorrow.

children.text: atra pitāpitā bhavati mātāmātā lokā alokā devā adevā vedā avedāḥ
children.translated_text: Here a father is no father, a mother no mother, worlds no worlds, gods no gods, Vedas no Vedas.

children.text: atra steno 'steno bhavati bhrūṇahābhrūṇahā cāṇḍyālo 'caṇḍyālaḥ paulkaso 'paulkasaḥ śramaṇo 'śramaṇas tāpaso 'tāpasaḥ
children.translated_text: Here a thief is no thief, a killer of an embryo no killer of an embryo, a caṇḍāla no caṇḍāla, a paulkasa no paulkasa, an ascetic no ascetic, an austerity-practicer no austerity-practicer.
He is not followed by good; he is not followed by evil.

children.text: tīrṇo hi tadā sarvāñ śokān hṛdayasya bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For then he has crossed over all the sorrows of the heart.

children.text: yad vai tan na paśyati paśyan vai tan na paśyati
children.translated_text: When it is said that he does not see there, though seeing, he does not see.

children.text: na hi draṣṭur dṛṣṭer viparilopo vidyate 'vināśitvān
children.translated_text: For there is no cessation of the seeing of the seer, since it is imperishable.

children.text: na tu tad dvitīyam asti tato 'nyad vibhaktaṃ yat paśyet ||
children.translated_text: But there is no second thing, separate from him and distinct, that he might see.

children.text: yad vai tan na jighrati jighran vai tan na jighrati
children.translated_text: When it is said that he does not smell there, though smelling, he does not smell.

children.text: na hi ghrātur ghrāter viparilopo vidyate 'vināśitvāt
children.translated_text: For there is no cessation of the smelling of the smeller, since it is imperishable.

children.text: na tu tad dvitīyam asti tato 'nyad vibhaktaṃ yaj jighret ||
children.translated_text: But there is no second thing, separate from him and distinct, that he might smell.

children.text: yad vai tan na rasayati rasayan vai tan na rasayati
children.translated_text: When it is said that he does not taste there, though tasting, he does not taste.

children.text: na hi rasayitū rasayater viparilopo vidyate 'vināśitvāt
children.translated_text: For there is no cessation of the tasting of the taster, since it is imperishable.

children.text: na tu tad dvitīyam asti tato 'nyad vibhaktaṃ yad rasayet ||
children.translated_text: But there is no second thing, separate from him and distinct, that he might taste.

children.text: yad vai tan na vadati vadan vai tan na vadati
children.translated_text: When it is said that he does not speak there, though speaking, he does not speak.

children.text: na hi vaktur vakter viparilopo vidyate 'vināśitvāt
children.translated_text: For there is no cessation of the speaking of the speaker, since it is imperishable.

children.text: na tu tad dvitīyam asti tato 'nyad vibhaktaṃ yad vadet ||
children.translated_text: But there is no second thing, separate from him and distinct, that he might speak.

children.text: yad vai tan na śṛṇoti śṛṇvan vai tan na śṛṇoti
children.translated_text: When it is said that he does not hear there, though hearing, he does not hear.

children.text: na hi śrotuḥ śruter viparilopo vidyate 'vināśitvāt
children.translated_text: For there is no cessation of the hearing of the hearer, since it is imperishable.

children.text: na tu tad dvitīyam asti tato 'nyad vibhaktaṃ yacchṛṇuyāt ||
children.translated_text: But there is no second thing, separate from it, other than it, which one might hear.

children.text: yad vai tan na manute manvāno vai tan na manute
children.translated_text: That which indeed he does not think: while thinking, he indeed does not think that.

children.text: na hi mantur mater viparilopo vidyate 'vināśitvāt
children.translated_text: For there is no disappearance of the thinker's thinking, because it is imperishable.

children.text: na tu tad dvitīyam asti tato 'nyad vibhaktaṃ yan manvīta ||
children.translated_text: But there is no second thing, separate from it, other than it, which one might think.

children.text: yad vai tan na spṛśati spṛśan vai tan na spṛśati
children.translated_text: That which indeed he does not touch: while touching, he indeed does not touch that.

children.text: na hi spraṣṭuḥ spṛṣṭer viparilopo vidyate 'vināśitvāt
children.translated_text: For there is no disappearance of the toucher’s touch, because it is imperishable.

children.text: na tu tad dvitīyam asti tato 'nyad vibhaktaṃ yat spṛśet ||
children.translated_text: But there is no second thing, separate from it, other than it, which one might touch.

children.text: yad vai tan na vijānāti vijānan vai tan na vijānāti
children.translated_text: That which indeed he does not know: while knowing, he indeed does not know that.

children.text: na hi vijñātur vijñāter viparilopo vidyate 'vināśitvāt
children.translated_text: For there is no disappearance of the knower's knowledge, because it is imperishable.

children.text: na tu tad dvitīyam asti tato 'nyad vibhaktaṃ yad vijānīyāt ||
children.translated_text: But there is no second thing, separate from it, other than it, which one might know.

children.text: yatra vā anyad iva syāt tatrānyo 'nyat paśyed anyo 'nyaj jighred anyo 'nyad rasayed anyo 'nyad vaded anyo 'nyacchṛṇuyād anyo 'nyan manvītānyo 'nyat spṛśed anyo 'nyad vijānīyāt ||
children.translated_text: Where there would be, as it were, something other, there one would see something else, one would smell something else, one would taste something else, one would speak something else, one would hear something else, one would think something else, one would touch something else, and one would know something else.
He becomes like a mass of water, one seer, without a second.
This is <s>Brahmaloka</s>, O king.
Thus <s>Yājñavalkya</s> instructed him.
This is his highest goal.
This is his highest attainment.
This is his highest world.
This is his highest bliss.
Other beings live upon only a measure of this very bliss.

children.text: sa yo manuṣyāṇāṃ rāddhaḥ samṛddho bhavaty anyeṣām adhipatiḥ sarvair mānuṣyakair bhogaiḥ sampannatamaḥ sa manuṣyāṇāṃ parama ānandaḥ
children.translated_text: A man who is successful among men, prosperous, lord over others, and most fully endowed with all human enjoyments: that is the highest bliss among men.

children.text: atha ye śataṃ manuṣyāṇām ānandāḥ sa ekaḥ pitṝṇāṃ jitalokānām ānandaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, a hundred blisses of men are one bliss of the ancestors who have won their worlds.

children.text: atha ye śataṃ pitṝṇāṃ jitalokānām ānandāḥ sa eko gandharvaloka ānandaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, a hundred blisses of the ancestors who have won their worlds are one bliss in the world of the <s>Gandharvas</s>.

children.text: atha ye śataṃ gandharvaloka ānandāḥ sa ekaḥ karmadevānām ānando ye karmaṇā devatvam abhisaṃpadyante
children.translated_text: Now, a hundred blisses in the world of the <s>Gandharvas</s> are one bliss of the gods by merit, those who attain divinity through action.

children.text: atha ye śataṃ karmadevānām ānandāḥ sa eka ājānadevānām ānandaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, a hundred blisses of the gods by merit are one bliss of the gods born as such.
And so too is that of a learned Vedic man, free from crookedness and unstruck by desire.

children.text: atha ye śatam ājānadevānām ānandāḥ sa ekaḥ prajāpatiloka ānandaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, a hundred blisses of the gods born as such are one bliss in the world of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
And so too is that of a learned Vedic man, free from crookedness and unstruck by desire.

children.text: atha ye śataṃ prajāpatiloka ānandāḥ sa eko brahmaloka ānandaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, a hundred blisses in the world of <s>Prajāpati</s> are one bliss in <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
And so too is that of a learned Vedic man, free from crookedness and unstruck by desire.
Now this very one is the highest bliss.
This is <s>Brahmaloka</s>, O king.
So said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
"I therefore give a thousand to the venerable one.
From here onward, speak only for the sake of liberation."

children.text: atra ha yājñavalkyo bibhayāṃcakāra medhāvī rājā sarvebhyo māntebhya udarautsīd iti ||
children.translated_text: At this <s>Yājñavalkya</s> became afraid: "The intelligent king has driven me out of all my limits."

children.text: sa vā eṣa etasmin svapnānte ratvā caritvā dṛṣṭvaiva puṇyaṃ ca pāpaṃ ca punaḥ pratinyāyaṃ pratiyony ādravati buddhāntāyaiva ||
children.translated_text: Having delighted, wandered, and seen both merit and demerit in this dream-state, he again runs back, according to his course and according to his origin, precisely to the waking state.

children.text: tad yathānaḥ susamāhitam utsarjaṃ yāyād evam evāyaṃ śārīra ātmā prājñenātmanānvārūḍha utsarjaṃ yāti
children.translated_text: As a well-loaded cart might go along creaking, so this bodily self, mounted by the knowing self, goes along creaking
when this becomes one whose breath is moving upward.

children.text: sa yatrāyam aṇimānaṃ nyeti jarayā vopatapatā vāṇimānaṃ nigacchati
children.translated_text: When this self comes to thinness, or reaches thinness through old age or illness,

children.text: tad yathāmraṃ vodumbaraṃ vā pippalaṃ vā bandhanāt pramucyate
children.translated_text: then, just as a mango, or a fig, or a fruit of the sacred fig is released from its bond,

children.text: evam evāyaṃ puruṣa ebhyo 'ṅgebhyaḥ sampramucya punaḥ pratinyāyaṃ pratiyony ādravati prāṇāyaiva ||
children.translated_text: so this person is released from these limbs and again runs back, according to his course and according to his origin, precisely to the vital breath.

children.text: tad yathā rājānam āyantam ugrāḥ pratyenasaḥ sūtagrāmaṇyo 'nnaiḥ pānair avasathaiḥ pratikalpante 'yam āyāty ayam āgacchatīti
children.translated_text: As, when a king is coming, officers, police, charioteers, and village-heads prepare themselves with food, drinks, and lodging, saying, "He is coming, he is arriving,"

children.text: evaṃ haivaṃvidaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni pratikalpanta idaṃ brahmāyātīdam āgacchatīti ||
children.translated_text: so all beings prepare themselves for one who knows thus, saying, "This brahman is coming, this is arriving."

children.text: tad yathā rājānaṃ prayiyāsantam ugrāḥ pratyenasaḥ sūtagrāmaṇyo 'bhisamāyanti
children.translated_text: As, when a king is about to depart, officers, police, charioteers, and village-heads gather around him,

children.text: evam evemam ātmānam antakāle sarve prāṇā abhisamāyanti
children.translated_text: so, at the final time, all the vital powers gather around this self
when this becomes one whose breath is moving upward.

children.text: sa yatrāyam ātmābalyaṃ nyetya saṃmoham iva nyeti
children.translated_text: When this self comes to weakness and comes, as it were, to bewilderment,
then these vital powers gather around it.

children.text: sa etās tejomātrāḥ samabhyādadāno hṛdayam evānvavakrāmati
children.translated_text: Gathering up these measures of radiance, it goes down into the heart itself.

children.text: sa yatraiṣa cākṣuṣaḥ puruṣaḥ parāṅ paryāvartate
children.translated_text: When this person in the eye turns away outward,
then he becomes one who no longer knows forms.
"He has become one; he does not see," they say.
"He has become one; he does not smell," they say.
"He has become one; he does not taste," they say.
"He has become one; he does not speak," they say.
"He has become one; he does not hear," they say.
"He has become one; he does not think," they say.
"He has become one; he does not touch," they say.
"He has become one; he does not know," they say.
The tip of this heart of his lights up.
By that light this self departs,

children.text: cakṣuṣṭo vā mūrdhno vānyebhyo vā śarīradeśebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: either through the eye, or through the head, or through other parts of the body.
As it departs, the vital breath departs after it.
As the vital breath departs after it, all the vital powers depart after it.
It is endowed with consciousness.
It moves on together with consciousness itself.
Knowledge and action take hold of it, and so does its former awareness.

children.text: tad yathā tṛṇajalāyukā tṛṇasyāntaṃ gatvānyam ākramam ākramyātmānam upasaṃharati
children.translated_text: Then, just as a grass-leech, having reached the end of a blade of grass, takes hold of another support and draws itself together,

children.text: evam evāyam ātmedaṃ śarīraṃ nihatyāvidyāṃ gamayitvānyam ākramam ākramyātmānam upasaṃharati ||
children.translated_text: In just this way this <s>ātman</s> (self), striking down this body and bringing it to unconsciousness, mounts another approach and, having mounted it, gathers itself together.

children.text: tad yathā peśaskārī peśaso mātrām apādāyānyan navataraṃ kalyāṇataraṃ rūpaṃ tanute
children.translated_text: Just as a goldsmith, taking a measure of gold, fashions another form, newer and more beautiful,

children.text: evam evāyam ātmedaṃ śarīraṃ nihatyāvidyāṃ gamayitvānyan navataraṃ kalyāṇataraṃ rūpaṃ kurute
children.translated_text: so too this <s>ātman</s>, striking down this body and bringing it to unconsciousness, makes another form, newer and more beautiful:

children.text: pitryaṃ vā gāndharvaṃ vā daivaṃ vā prājāpatyaṃ vā brāhmaṃ vānyeṣāṃ vā bhūtānām ||
children.translated_text: one belonging to the ancestors, or to the <s>Gandharvas</s>, or divine, or belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s>, or brahmanic, or one belonging to other beings.

children.text: sa vā ayam ātmā brahma vijñānamayo manomayo prāṇamayaś cakṣurmayaḥ śrotramayaḥ pṛthivīmaya āpomayo vāyumaya ākāśamayas tejomayo 'tejomayaḥ kāmamayo 'kāmamayaḥ krodhamayo 'krodhamayo dharmamayo 'dharmamayaḥ sarvamayaḥ
children.translated_text: Now this very <s>ātman</s> is <s>brahman</s> (ultimate reality), made of cognition, made of mind, made of vital breath, made of sight, made of hearing, made of earth, made of waters, made of wind, made of space, made of light and made of non-light, made of desire and made of non-desire, made of anger and made of non-anger, made of <s>dharma</s> and made of non-<s>dharma</s>, made of everything.
Therefore it is said: 'It is made of this; it is made of that.'
As one acts, as one conducts oneself, so one becomes.
One who does good becomes good.
One who does evil becomes evil.
One becomes meritorious by meritorious action, evil by evil action.
And then, indeed, they say:
'This person is precisely made of desire.'
As his desire is, so is his resolve.
As his resolve is, so is the deed he performs.
Whatever deed he performs, that he comes to attain.
On this there is this verse:

children.text: tad eva saktaḥ saha karmaṇaiti liṅgaṃ mano yatra niṣaktam asya
children.translated_text: Attached to that, together with his karma, he goes to the subtle mark where his mind is fastened.

children.text: prāpyāntaṃ karmaṇas tasya yat kiñceha karoty ayam
children.translated_text: Having reached the end of that karma, whatever he does here,

children.text: tasmāllokāt punar aity asmai lokāya karmaṇe
children.translated_text: from that world he comes back again to this world for action.
So it is with one who has desire.

children.text: athākāmayamāno yo 'kāmo niṣkāma āptakāma ātmakāmo na tasya prāṇā utkrāmanti
children.translated_text: But as for one who is without desire, who is free from desire, whose desire is fulfilled, whose desire is the <s>ātman</s>, his vital breaths do not depart.
Being <s>brahman</s> itself, he goes to <s>brahman</s>.
On this there is this verse:

children.text: yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye 'sya hṛdi śritāḥ
children.translated_text: When all the desires that have taken shelter in his heart are released,

children.text: atha martyo 'mṛto bhavaty atra brahma samaśnuta iti
children.translated_text: then the mortal becomes immortal; here he attains <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: tad yathāhinirlvayanī valmīke mṛtā pratyastā śayīta
children.translated_text: Just as a dead snake's sloughed-off skin might lie cast away on an anthill,
so indeed this body lies.

children.text: athāyam aśarīro 'mṛtaḥ prāṇo brahmaiva teja eva
children.translated_text: But this bodiless, immortal vital principle is <s>brahman</s> itself, is radiance itself.

children.text: so 'haṃ bhagavate sahasraṃ dadāmīti hovāca janako vaidehaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'I give a thousand to the reverend one,' said <s>Janaka Vaideha</s>.
On this there are these verses:

children.text: aṇuḥ panthā vitataḥ purāṇo māṃ spṛṣṭo 'nuvitto mayaiva
children.translated_text: Subtle is the path, stretched out, ancient, touched by me and found by me alone.

children.text: tena dhīrā apiyanti brahmavidaḥ svargaṃ lokam ita ūrdhvaṃ vimuktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By it the wise, knowers of <s>brahman</s>, freed from here, go upward to the heavenly world.

children.text: tasmiñśuklam uta nīlam āhuḥ piṅgalaṃ haritaṃ lohitaṃ ca
children.translated_text: On it, they say, are white and also blue, tawny, green, and red;

children.text: eṣa panthā brahmaṇā hānuvittas tenaiti brahmavit puṇyakṛt taijasaś ca ||
children.translated_text: this path has indeed been found by <s>brahman</s>; by it goes the knower of <s>brahman</s>, the doer of merit, and the radiant one.
They enter blind darkness who worship ignorance;

children.text: tato bhūya iva te tamo ya u vidyāyāṃ ratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: into a darkness as though still greater go those who delight in knowledge alone.

children.text: anandā nāma te lokā andhena tamasāvṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Joyless, they say, are those worlds, covered with blind darkness;
after death, ignorant, undiscerning people go to them.

children.text: ātmānaṃ ced vijānīyād ayam asmīti puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: If a person were to know the <s>ātman</s> as 'I am this one,'

children.text: kim icchan kasya kāmāya śarīram anu saṃjvaret ||
children.translated_text: then desiring what, and for whose desire, would he suffer along with the body?

children.text: yasyānuvittaḥ pratibuddha ātmāsmin saṃdehye gahane praviṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: He whose <s>ātman</s>, entered into this doubtful and dense body, has been found and awakened,

children.text: sa viśvakṛt sa hi sarvasya kartā tasya lokaḥ sa u loka eva ||
children.translated_text: is the maker of all; for he is the maker of everything. His world is his; indeed, he himself is the world.

children.text: ihaiva santo 'tha vidmas tad vayaṃ na ced avedir mahatī vinaṣṭiḥ
children.translated_text: Being here itself, we have come to know that. If one has not known it, the loss is great.

children.text: ye tad vidur amṛtās te bhavanty athetare duḥkham evāpiyanti ||
children.translated_text: Those who know that become immortal; others, however, go only to suffering.
When one directly sees this <s>ātman</s> as the god,
the lord of what has been and what will be, then one no longer shrinks away from it.
That before which the year revolves with the days,

children.text: tad devā jyotiṣāṃ jyotir āyur hopāsate 'mṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the gods worship as the light of lights, as life, as immortal.

children.text: yasmin pañca pañcajanā ākāśaś ca pratiṣṭhitaḥ
children.translated_text: In whom the five groups of five, and space, are established,

children.text: tam eva manya ātmānaṃ vidvān brahmāmṛto 'mṛtam ||
children.translated_text: that very one I consider the <s>ātman</s>; knowing <s>brahman</s>, the immortal, one is immortal.

children.text: prāṇasya prāṇam uta cakṣuṣaś cakṣur uta śrotrasya śrotram manaso ye mano viduḥ
children.translated_text: Those who know the breath of breath, the eye of the eye, the ear of the ear, and the mind of the mind,
they have understood <s>brahman</s>, ancient and foremost.
It is to be seen only by the mind; there is no plurality here at all.

children.text: mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyum āpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati
children.translated_text: From death to death goes one who sees here as if there were plurality.
This immeasurable, fixed one is to be seen as one alone:

children.text: virajaḥ para ākāśād aja ātmā mahān dhruvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: stainless, beyond space, unborn, the great, fixed <s>ātman</s>.

children.text: tam eva dhīro vijñāya prajñāṃ kurvīta brāhmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing that alone, the wise <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should cultivate wisdom.

children.text: nānudhyāyād bahūñchabdān vāco viglāpanaṃ hi tad iti ||
children.translated_text: He should not ponder many words, for that is a weariness of speech.

children.text: sa vā eṣa mahān aja ātmā yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣu
children.translated_text: Now this is the great unborn <s>ātman</s>, this one who is made of cognition among the vital breaths.
This space here within the heart: in it he lies,
ruler of all,
lord of all,
sovereign of all.
He does not become greater by good action,
nor lesser by bad action.
He is lord of all.
He is sovereign over beings.
He is protector of beings.

children.text: eṣa setur vidharaṇa eṣāṃ lokānām asaṃbhedāya
children.translated_text: He is the bridge, the boundary, for keeping these worlds from being confounded.

children.text: tam etaṃ vedānuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti yajñena dānena tapasānāśakena
children.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know him through recitation of the Vedas, through sacrifice, through gift, and through austerity consisting in fasting.
Having known this very one, a sage becomes a <s>muni</s>.

children.text: etam eva pravrājino lokam icchantaḥ pravrajanti ||
children.translated_text: Desiring this very world, renouncers go forth into renunciation.
This has been declared by a verse:

children.text: eṣa nityo mahimā brāhmaṇasya na karmaṇā vardhate no kanīyān
children.translated_text: This is the eternal greatness of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; it does not increase by action, nor does it become less.

children.text: tasyaiva syāt padavittaṃ viditvā na lipyate karmaṇā pāpakeneti
children.translated_text: One should know only its path and find it; knowing it, one is not stained by evil action.

children.text: tasmād evaṃvicchānto dānta uparatas titikṣuḥ samāhito bhūtvātmany evātmānaṃ paśyati
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who knows thus, having become calm, restrained, withdrawn, patient, and collected, sees the self in the self alone.
He sees everything as the self.
Evil does not cross over him.
He crosses over all evil.
Evil does not burn him.
He burns up all evil.
Free from evil, stainless, and without doubt, he becomes a brāhmaṇa.
This is <s>Brahmaloka</s>, O king.
"You have been brought to it," said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: so 'haṃ bhagavate videhān dadāmi mām cāpi saha dāsyāyeti ||
children.translated_text: So he said, "I give the <s>Videhas</s> to the venerable one, and myself too along with them as a slave."

children.text: sa vā eṣa mahān aja ātmānnādo vasudānaḥ
children.translated_text: This, indeed, is that great unborn self, the eater of food and the giver of wealth.
He obtains wealth who knows thus.

children.text: sa vā eṣa mahān aja ātmājaro 'maro 'mṛto 'bhayo brahma
children.translated_text: This, indeed, is that great unborn self, undecaying, immortal, deathless, fearless, brahman.
Brahman, indeed, is fearlessness.

children.text: abhayaṃ hi vai brahma bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: For one who knows thus indeed becomes fearless brahman.

children.text: atha ha yājñavalkyasya dve bhārye babhūvatur maitreyī ca kātyāyanī ca
children.translated_text: Now <s>Yājñavalkya</s> had two wives, <s>Maitreyī</s> and <s>Kātyāyanī</s>.
Of the two, <s>Maitreyī</s> was a speaker of brahman.
At that time <s>Kātyāyanī</s> had just the ordinary understanding of women.
Now <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, intending to enter another way of life,
said, "<s>Maitreyī</s>," said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: pravrajiṣyan vā are 'ham asmāt sthānād asmi
children.translated_text: "Dear one, I am about to go forth from this station.
Come, let me make a settlement between you and this <s>Kātyāyanī</s>."
<s>Maitreyī</s> said:

children.text: yan nu ma iyam bhagoḥ sarvā pṛthivī vittena pūrṇā syāt syāṃ nv ahaṃ tenāmṛtāho3 neti
children.translated_text: "Venerable sir, if this whole earth filled with wealth were mine, would I become immortal through it, or not?"
"No," said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
"As is the life of those who possess means,
so would your life be.
But there is no hope of immortality through wealth."
<s>Maitreyī</s> said:

children.text: yenāhaṃ nāmṛtā syām kim ahaṃ tena kuryām
children.translated_text: "What should I do with that by which I would not become immortal?

children.text: yad eva bhagavān veda tad eva me brūhīti ||
children.translated_text: Tell me only what the venerable one knows."
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:

children.text: priyā vai khalu no bhavatī satī priyam avṛdhat
children.translated_text: "You have indeed been dear to us, and, being dear, you have increased what is dear.
Come then.
I will explain this to you.
But as I explain, meditate carefully on it."
He said:

children.text: na vā are patyuḥ kāmāya patiḥ priyo bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya patiḥ priyo bhavati
children.translated_text: "It is not for the sake of the husband, dear one, that the husband is dear; rather, for the sake of the self the husband is dear.

children.text: na vā are jāyāyai kāmāya jāyā priyā bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya jāyā priyā bhavati
children.translated_text: It is not for the sake of the wife, dear one, that the wife is dear; rather, for the sake of the self the wife is dear.

children.text: na vā are putrāṇāṃ kāmāya putrāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya putrāḥ priyā bhavanti
children.translated_text: It is not for the sake of sons, dear one, that sons are dear; rather, for the sake of the self sons are dear.

children.text: na vā are vittasya kāmāya vittaṃ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya vittaṃ priyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: It is not for the sake of wealth, dear one, that wealth is dear; rather, for the sake of the self wealth is dear.

children.text: na vā are paśūnāṃ kāmāya paśavaḥ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya paśavaḥ priyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: It is not for the sake of cattle, dear one, that cattle are dear; rather, for the sake of the self cattle are dear.

children.text: na vā are brahmaṇaḥ kāmāya brahma priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya brahma priyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: It is not for the sake of brahman, dear one, that brahman is dear; rather, for the sake of the self brahman is dear.

children.text: na vā are kṣatrasya kāmāya kṣatraṃ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya kṣatraṃ priyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: It is not for the sake of the kṣatra, dear one, that the kṣatra is dear; rather, for the sake of the self the kṣatra is dear.

children.text: na vā are lokānāṃ kāmāya lokāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya lokāḥ priyā bhavanti
children.translated_text: It is not for the sake of the worlds, dear one, that the worlds are dear; rather, for the sake of the self the worlds are dear.

children.text: na vā are devānāṃ kāmāya devāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya devāḥ priyā bhavanti
children.translated_text: It is not for the sake of the gods, dear one, that the gods are dear; rather, for the sake of the self the gods are dear.

children.text: na vā are vedānāṃ kāmāya vedāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya vedāḥ priyā bhavanti
children.translated_text: It is not for the sake of the Vedas, dear one, that the Vedas are dear; rather, for the sake of the self the Vedas are dear.

children.text: na vā are bhūtānāṃ kāmāya bhūtāni priyāṇi bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya bhūtāni priyāṇi bhavanti
children.translated_text: It is not for the sake of beings, dear one, that beings are dear; rather, for the sake of the self beings are dear.

children.text: na vā are sarvasya kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: It is not for the sake of all, dear one, that all is dear; rather, for the sake of the self all is dear.

children.text: ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyo maitreyi
children.translated_text: The self, dear <s>Maitreyī</s>, is to be seen, to be heard, to be reflected upon, and to be meditated upon.

children.text: ātmani khalv are dṛṣṭe śrute mate vijñāta idaṃ sarvaṃ viditam ||
children.translated_text: For when the self, dear one, has been seen, heard, thought upon, and known, all this is known.

children.text: brahma taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmano vedān veda
children.translated_text: Brahman rejects the one who knows the Vedas as apart from the self.

children.text: kṣatraṃ taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmanaḥ kṣatraṃ veda
children.translated_text: The kṣatra rejects the one who knows the kṣatra as apart from the self.

children.text: lokās taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano lokān veda
children.translated_text: The worlds reject the one who knows the worlds as apart from the self.

children.text: devās taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano devān veda
children.translated_text: The gods reject the one who knows the gods as apart from the self.

children.text: vedās taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano vedān veda
children.translated_text: The Vedas reject the one who knows the Vedas as apart from the self.

children.text: bhūtāni taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano bhūtāni veda
children.translated_text: Beings reject the one who knows beings as apart from the self.

children.text: sarvaṃ taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmanaḥ sarvaṃ veda
children.translated_text: All rejects the one who knows all as apart from the self.

children.text: idaṃ brahmedaṃ kṣatram ime lokā ime devā ime vedā imāni bhūtānīdaṃ sarvaṃ yad ayam ātmā ||
children.translated_text: This brahman, this kṣatra, these worlds, these gods, these Vedas, these beings, this whole all is this self.

children.text: sa yathā dundubher hanyamānasya na bāhyāñchabdāñchaknuyād grahaṇāya
children.translated_text: Just as, when a drum is being beaten, one would not be able to grasp its external sounds,

children.text: dundubhes tu grahaṇena dundubhyāghātasya vā śabdo gṛhītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but by grasping the drum, or the beating of the drum, the sound is grasped;

children.text: sa yathā śaṅkhasya dhmāyamānasya na bāhyāñchabdāñchaknuyād grahaṇāya
children.translated_text: just as, when a conch is being blown, one would not be able to grasp its external sounds,

children.text: śaṅkhasya tu grahaṇena śaṅkhadhmasya vā śabdo gṛhītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but by grasping the conch, or the blowing of the conch, the sound is grasped;

children.text: sa yathā vīṇāyai vādyamānāyai na bāhyāñchabdāñchaknuyād grahaṇāya
children.translated_text: just as, when a vīṇā is being played, one would not be able to grasp its external sounds,

children.text: vīṇāyai tu grahaṇena vīṇāvādasya vā śabdo gṛhītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but by grasping the vīṇā, or the playing of the vīṇā, the sound is grasped.

children.text: sa yathārdraidhāgnerabhyāhitasya pṛthag dhūmā viniścarantyevaṃ vā are 'sya mahato bhūtasya niḥśvasitam etad yad ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvāṅgirasa itihāsaḥ purāṇaṃ vidyā upaniṣadaḥ ślokāḥ sūtrāṇy anuvyākhyānāni vyākhyānānīṣṭaṃ hutam āśitaṃ pāyitam ayaṃ ca lokaḥ paraś ca lokaḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni
children.translated_text: As, when damp fuel has been placed upon a fire, separate streams of smoke come forth, so indeed, dear one, this is the exhalation of this great being: the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s>, history, ancient lore, the sciences, the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, verses, sūtras, supplementary explanations, explanations, what is offered, what is poured in sacrifice, what is eaten, what is drunk, this world and the world beyond, and all beings.
All these are indeed the exhalations of that very one.

children.text: sa yathā sarvāsām apāṃ samudra ekāyanam
children.translated_text: As the ocean is the single destination of all waters,
so the skin is the single destination of all touches.
So the two nostrils are the single destination of all smells.
So the tongue is the single destination of all tastes.
So the eye is the single destination of all forms.
So the ear is the single destination of all sounds.
So the mind is the single destination of all intentions.
So the heart is the single destination of all forms of knowledge.
So the two hands are the single destination of all actions.
So the generative organ is the single destination of all pleasures.
So the anus is the single destination of all excretions.
So the two feet are the single destination of all paths.
So speech is the single destination of all the Vedas.

children.text: sa yathā saindhavaghano 'nantaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtsno rasaghana eva
children.translated_text: As a lump of salt has no inside or outside, but is wholly a mass of taste alone,

children.text: evaṃ vā are 'yam ātmānantaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtsnaḥ prajñānaghana eva
children.translated_text: so indeed, dear one, this self has no inside or outside, but is wholly a mass of consciousness alone.
Having arisen from these elements, it is led back into those very elements.
After death there is no distinguishing awareness, dear one; this I say.
So spoke <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
<s>Maitreyī</s> said:
Right here, venerable sir, you have brought me to the end of bewilderment.
For I do not understand this.

children.text: sa hovāca na vā are 'haṃ mohaṃ bravīmi
children.translated_text: He said: Dear one, I am not speaking bewilderment.
This self, dear one, is indestructible, of a nature that cannot be cut off.

children.text: yatra hi dvaitam iva bhavati tad itara itaraṃ paśyati tad itara itaraṃ jighrati tad itara itaraṃ rasayate tad itara itaram abhivadati tad itara itaraṃ śṛṇoti tad itara itaraṃ manute tad itara itaraṃ spṛśati tad itara itaraṃ vijānāti
children.translated_text: For where there is duality, as it were, there one sees another, there one smells another, there one tastes another, there one addresses another, there one hears another, there one thinks of another, there one touches another, there one knows another.

children.text: yatra tv asya sarvam ātmaivābhūt tat kena kaṃ paśyet tat kena kaṃ jighret tat kena kaṃ rasayet tat kena kam abhivadet tat kena kaṃ śṛṇuyāt tat kena kaṃ manvīta tat kena kaṃ spṛśet tat kena kaṃ vijānīyāt
children.translated_text: But where, for this one, everything has become the self alone, then by what would one see whom? By what would one smell whom? By what would one taste whom? By what would one address whom? By what would one hear whom? By what would one think of whom? By what would one touch whom? By what would one know whom?

children.text: yenedaṃ sarvaṃ vijānāti taṃ kena vijānīyāt
children.translated_text: By what would one know that through which one knows all this?
This is that self: "not this, not this."
It is ungraspable, for it is not grasped.
It is undecaying, for it does not decay.
It is unattached, for it does not become attached.
It is unfettered; it does not suffer and is not injured.

children.text: vijñātāram are kena vijānīyād ity uktānuśāsanāsi maitreyi
children.translated_text: By what, dear one, would one know the knower? Thus, <s>Maitreyī</s>, you have been instructed.

children.text: etāvad are khalv amṛtatvam iti hoktvā yājñavalkyo vijahāra ||
children.translated_text: Having said, "This much indeed, dear one, is immortality," <s>Yājñavalkya</s> departed.
Now the lineage:
<s>Pautimāṣya</s> from <s>Gaupavana</s>.
<s>Gaupavana</s> from <s>Pautimāṣya</s>.
<s>Pautimāṣya</s> from <s>Gaupavana</s>.
<s>Gaupavana</s> from <s>Kauśika</s>.
<s>Kauśika</s> from <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>.
<s>Kauṇḍinya</s> from <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>.
<s>Śāṇḍilya</s> from <s>Kauśika</s> and from <s>Gautama</s>.
<s>Gautama</s>;
from <s>Agniveśya</s>.
<s>Agniveśya</s> from <s>Gārgya</s>.
<s>Gārgya</s> from <s>Gārgya</s>.
<s>Gārgya</s> from <s>Gautama</s>.
<s>Gautama</s> from <s>Saitava</s>.
<s>Saitava</s> from <s>Pārāśaryāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Pārāśaryāyaṇa</s> from <s>Gārgyāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Gārgyāyaṇa</s> from <s>Uddālakāyana</s>.
<s>Uddālakāyana</s> from <s>Jābālāyana</s>.
<s>Jābālāyana</s> from <s>Mādhyandināyana</s>.
<s>Mādhyandināyana</s> from <s>Saukarāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Saukarāyaṇa</s> from <s>Kāṣāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Kāṣāyaṇa</s> from <s>Sāyakāyana</s>.
<s>Sāyakāyana</s> from <s>Kauśikāyani</s>.
<s>Kauśikāyani</s>;
from <s>Ghṛtakauśika</s>.
<s>Ghṛtakauśika</s> from <s>Pārāśarya</s>.
<s>Pārāśarya</s> from <s>Pārāśarya</s>.
<s>Pārāśarya</s> from <s>Jātukarṇya</s>.
<s>Jātukarṇya</s> from <s>Āsurāyaṇa</s> and from <s>Yaska</s>.
<s>Āsurāyaṇa</s> from <s>Traivaṇi</s>.
<s>Traivaṇi</s> from <s>Aupajandhani</s>.
<s>Aupajandhani</s> from <s>Āsuri</s>.
<s>Āsuri</s> from <s>Bhāradvāja</s>.
<s>Bhāradvāja</s> from <s>Ātreya</s>.
<s>Ātreya</s> from <s>Māṇṭi</s>.
<s>Māṇṭi</s> from <s>Gautama</s>.
<s>Gautama</s> from <s>Gautama</s>.
<s>Gautama</s> from <s>Vātsya</s>.
<s>Vātsya</s> from <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>.
<s>Śāṇḍilya</s> from <s>Kaiśorya Kāpya</s>.
<s>Kaiśorya Kāpya</s> from <s>Kumāraharita</s>.
<s>Kumāraharita</s> from <s>Gālava</s>.
<s>Gālava</s> from <s>Vidarbhīkauṇḍinya</s>.
<s>Vidarbhīkauṇḍinya</s> from <s>Vatsanapāt Bābhrava</s>.
<s>Vatsanapāt Bābhrava</s> from <s>Panthā Saubhara</s>.
<s>Panthā Saubhara</s> from <s>Ayāsya Āṅgirasa</s>.
<s>Ayāsya Āṅgirasa</s> from <s>Ābhuti Tvāṣṭra</s>.
<s>Ābhuti Tvāṣṭra</s> from <s>Viśvarūpa Tvāṣṭra</s>.
<s>Viśvarūpa Tvāṣṭra</s> from the two <s>Aśvins</s>.
The two <s>Aśvins</s> from <s>Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa</s>.
<s>Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa</s> from <s>Atharvan Daiva</s>.
<s>Atharvan Daiva</s> from <s>Mṛtyu Prādhvaṃsana</s>.
<s>Mṛtyu Prādhvaṃsana</s> from <s>Prādhvaṃsana</s>.
<s>Prādhvaṃsana</s> from <s>Ekarṣi</s>.
<s>Ekarṣi</s> from <s>Viprajitti</s>.
<s>Viprajitti</s> from <s>Vyaṣṭi</s>.
<s>Vyaṣṭi</s> from <s>Sanāru</s>.
<s>Sanāru</s> from <s>Sanātana</s>.
<s>Sanātana</s> from <s>Sanaga</s>.
<s>Sanaga</s> from <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
<s>Parameṣṭhin</s> from <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s>, the self-existent.
Homage to <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: pūrṇam adaḥ pūrṇam idaṃ pūrṇāt pūrṇam udacyate
children.translated_text: That is fullness; this is fullness. From fullness, fullness comes forth.
Taking fullness from fullness, fullness alone remains.
Space is <s>Brahman</s>.
Space is ancient.
The wind is space.
So indeed said the son of <s>Kauravyāyaṇī</s>.
The Brahmins know: this is the Veda.
By this one knows what is to be known.

children.text: trayāḥ prājāpatyāḥ prajāpatau pitari brahmacaryam ūṣuḥ
children.translated_text: The three kinds of offspring of <s>Prajāpati</s> lived as brahmacarins with their father <s>Prajāpati</s>:
the gods, human beings, and asuras.

children.text: uṣitvā brahmacaryaṃ devā ūcur bravītu no bhavān iti
children.translated_text: After they had lived as brahmacarins, the gods said, "May the venerable one instruct us."

children.text: tebhyo haitad akṣaram uvāca da iti
children.translated_text: To them he uttered this very syllable: "da."
"Have you understood?"
They said, "We have understood."
"You told us, 'Control yourselves,' did you not?"
"Om," he said. "You have understood."

children.text: atha hainaṃ manuṣyā ūcur bravītu no bhavān iti
children.translated_text: Then the human beings said to him, "May the venerable one instruct us."

children.text: tebhyo haitad evākṣaram uvāca da iti
children.translated_text: To them he uttered that very same syllable: "da."
"Have you understood?"
They said, "We have understood."
"You told us, 'Give,' did you not?"
"Om," he said. "You have understood."

children.text: atha hainam asurā ūcur bravītu no bhavān iti
children.translated_text: Then the asuras said to him, "May the venerable one instruct us."

children.text: tebhyo haitad evākṣaram uvāca da iti
children.translated_text: To them he uttered that very same syllable: "da."
"Have you understood?"
They said, "We have understood."
"You told us, 'Be compassionate,' did you not?"
"Om," he said. "You have understood."

children.text: tad etad evaiṣā daivī vāg anuvadati stanayitnur da da da iti
children.translated_text: This very thing is repeated by that divine voice, thunder, saying "da, da, da."
That means: control yourselves, give, be compassionate.

children.text: tad etat trayaṃ śikṣed damam dānam dayām iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should learn these three: self-control, giving, and compassion.
This <s>Prajāpati</s> is what the heart is.
This is <s>brahman</s>.
This is all.
This word hṛdayam, 'heart,' has three syllables.
Hṛ is one syllable.

children.text: abhiharantyasmai svāścānye ca ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: His own people and others bring offerings to him who knows thus.
Da is one syllable.

children.text: dadatyasmai svāścānye ca ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: His own people and others give to him who knows thus.
Yam is one syllable.

children.text: eti svargaṃ lokaṃ ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus goes to the heavenly world.

children.text: tad vai tad etad eva tad āsa
children.translated_text: That, indeed, was just this very thing.
It was truth alone.

children.text: sa yo haitaṃ mahad yakṣaṃ prathamajaṃ veda satyaṃ brahmeti jayatīmāṃllokān jita in nvasāv asat ya evam etan mahad yakṣaṃ prathamajaṃ veda satyaṃ brahmeti
children.translated_text: Whoever knows this great, first-born wonder as truth, as <s>brahman</s>, conquers these worlds; surely he is not conquered, he who knows this great, first-born wonder as truth, as <s>brahman</s>.
For <s>brahman</s> is truth indeed.
In the beginning, this was water alone.
Those waters created truth.
Truth is <s>brahman</s>.
<s>Brahman</s> created <s>Prajāpati</s>.
<s>Prajāpati</s> created the gods.
Those gods worship truth alone.

children.text: tad etat tryakṣaraṃ sa ti yam iti sa ity ekam akṣaram
children.translated_text: This word satyam, 'truth,' has three syllables: sa, ti, and yam. Sa is one syllable.
Ti is one syllable.
Yam is one syllable.
The first and last syllables are truth; in the middle is untruth.

children.text: tad etad anṛtam ubhayataḥ satyena parigṛhītam
children.translated_text: This untruth is enclosed on both sides by truth.
It becomes more truly truth.
Untruth does not harm one who knows thus.

children.text: tad yat tat satyam asau sa ādityaḥ
children.translated_text: That which is truth is that Sun there.

children.text: ya eṣa etasmin maṇḍale puruṣo yaścāyaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣan puruṣas tāvetāvanyonyasmin pratiṣṭhitau
children.translated_text: The person who is in that disk and the person who is here in the right eye: these two are established in one another.

children.text: raśmibhir eṣo 'smin pratiṣṭhitaḥ prāṇair ayam amuṣmin
children.translated_text: By rays that one is established in this one; by the vital breaths this one is established in that one.

children.text: sa yadotkramiṣyan bhavati śuddham evaitan maṇḍalaṃ paśyati
children.translated_text: When he is about to depart, he sees that disk as pure indeed.
Those rays do not come back to him.

children.text: ya eṣa etasmin maṇḍale puruṣas tasya bhūr iti śiraḥ
children.translated_text: For the person who is in that disk, bhūr is his head.
There is one head; this is one syllable.
Bhuva is his arms.
There are two arms; these are two syllables.
Svar is his supports.
There are two supports; these are two syllables.
His secret name is ahar, 'day.'

children.text: hanti pāpmānaṃ jahāti ca ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He smites evil and abandons it, who knows thus.

children.text: yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣan puruṣas tasya bhūr iti śiraḥ
children.translated_text: For the person who is here in the right eye, bhūr is his head.
There is one head; this is one syllable.
Bhuva is his arms.
There are two arms; these are two syllables.
Svar is his supports.
There are two supports; these are two syllables.
His secret name is aham, 'I.'

children.text: hanti pāpmānaṃ jahāti ca ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He smites evil and abandons it, who knows thus.
This person consists of mind and has light as his reality.

children.text: tasminn antar hṛdaye yathā vrīhir vā yavo vā
children.translated_text: He is there within the heart, like a grain of rice or barley.

children.text: sa eṣa sarvasyeśānaḥ sarvasyādhipatiḥ sarvam idaṃ praśāsti yad idaṃ kiṃca ||
children.translated_text: He is the ruler of all, the lord of all; he governs all this, whatever there is here.
They say, "Lightning is <s>brahman</s>."
Because of illumination, it is lightning.

children.text: vidyaty enaṃ pāpmano ya evaṃ veda vidyud brahmeti
children.translated_text: Lightning cuts him away from evil, who knows thus: "Lightning is <s>brahman</s>."
For lightning indeed is <s>brahman</s>.
One should worship speech as a cow.
She has four teats.
They are the svāhā-call, the vaṣaṭ-call, the hanta-call, and the svadhā-call.
The gods live upon two of her teats:
the svāhā-call and the vaṣaṭ-call.
Human beings live upon the hanta-call.
The ancestors live upon the svadhā-call.
Her breath is the bull, and mind is the calf.

children.text: ayam agnir vaiśvānaro yo 'yam antaḥ puruṣe
children.translated_text: This is the fire <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, which is here inside a person,
by which this food is cooked,
the food that is eaten here.
This is its sound,
which one hears when one covers the ears.

children.text: sa yadotkramiṣyan bhavati nainaṃ ghoṣaṃ śṛṇoti ||
children.translated_text: When he is about to depart, he does not hear this sound.

children.text: yadā vai puruṣo 'smāllokāt praiti sa vāyum āgacchati
children.translated_text: When a person goes forth from this world, he reaches the wind.

children.text: tasmai sa tatra vijihīte yathā rathacakrasya kham
children.translated_text: There it opens itself for him like the hole of a chariot wheel.
Through that he steps upward.
He reaches the Sun.
There it opens itself for him.
It is like the hole of a lambara.
Through that he steps upward.
He reaches the Moon.
There it opens itself for him.
It is like the hole of a drum.
Through that he steps upward.
He reaches a world free from sorrow and free from cold.
In it he dwells for everlasting years.

children.text: etad vai paramaṃ tapo yad vyāhitas tapyate
children.translated_text: This indeed is the highest austerity: when one who is ill suffers.

children.text: paramaṃ haiva lokaṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He who knows thus wins the highest world indeed.

children.text: etad vai paramaṃ tapo yaṃ pretam araṇyaṃ haranti
children.translated_text: This indeed is the highest austerity: when they carry a dead person to the wilderness.

children.text: paramaṃ haiva lokaṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He who knows thus wins the highest world indeed.

children.text: etad vai paramaṃ tapo yaṃ pretam agnāv abhyādadhati
children.translated_text: This indeed is the highest austerity: when they place a dead person upon the fire.

children.text: paramaṃ haiva lokaṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He indeed wins the highest world who knows thus.
Some say, "Food is <s>brahman</s>."
That is not so.
For food decays without <s>prāṇa</s> (breath).
Some say, "<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>brahman</s>."
That is not so.
For <s>prāṇa</s> dries up without food.

children.text: ete ha tv eva devate ekadhābhūyaṃ bhūtvā paramatāṃ gacchataḥ
children.translated_text: But these two deities, having become one, attain supremacy.
Then <s>Prātṛda</s> said to his father:

children.text: kiṃ svid evaivaṃ viduṣe sādhu kuryāṃ kim evāsmā asādhu kuryām iti
children.translated_text: "What good, indeed, should I do for one who knows thus? What harm, indeed, should I do to him?"

children.text: sa ha smāha pāṇinā mā prātṛda
children.translated_text: He said, with his hand, "No, <s>Prātṛda</s>."

children.text: kas tvenayor ekadhābhūyaṃ bhūtvā paramatāṃ gacchatīti
children.translated_text: "Which of these two, having become one, attains supremacy?"
To him he then said this: "vi."
Food indeed is "vi."
For in food all these beings are entered and established.
"ram," he said.
<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is "ram."
For in <s>prāṇa</s> all these beings delight.

children.text: sarvāṇi ha vā asmin bhūtāni viśanti
children.translated_text: All beings indeed enter into him,

children.text: sarvāṇi bhūtāni ramante ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: and all beings delight in him who knows thus.
The <s>uktha</s> (recitation).
<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>uktha</s>.
For <s>prāṇa</s> raises up all this.
A heroic son rises up from him who knows the <s>uktha</s>.

children.text: ukthasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He wins union and dwelling in the same world with the <s>uktha</s> who knows thus.
The <s>yajus</s> (sacrificial formula).
<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>yajus</s>.
For in <s>prāṇa</s> all these beings are yoked together.
All beings are yoked for his preeminence.

children.text: yajuṣaḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He wins union and dwelling in the same world with the <s>yajus</s> who knows thus.
The <s>sāman</s> (chant).
<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>sāman</s>.
For in <s>prāṇa</s> all these beings come together harmoniously.

children.text: samyañci hāsmai sarvāṇi bhūtāni śraiṣṭhyāya kalpante
children.translated_text: All beings become harmonious for his preeminence.

children.text: sāmnaḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He wins union and dwelling in the same world with the <s>sāman</s> who knows thus.
<s>Kṣatra</s> (ruling power).
<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is <s>kṣatra</s>.
For <s>prāṇa</s> indeed is <s>kṣatra</s>.
<s>Prāṇa</s> protects him from being wounded.
He attains manifest <s>kṣatra</s>, a protection.

children.text: kṣatrasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He wins union and dwelling in the same world with <s>kṣatra</s> who knows thus.
"Earth, atmosphere, and sky" are eight syllables.

children.text: aṣṭākṣaraṃ ha vā ekaṃ gāyatryai padam
children.translated_text: One foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> indeed has eight syllables.
This, indeed, is that foot of hers.

children.text: sa yāvad eṣu triṣu lokeṣu tāvaddha jayati yo 'syā etad evaṃ padaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: As far as these three worlds extend, so much does he win who knows this foot of hers thus.
"The ṛc verses, the yajus formulas, and the sāman chants" are eight syllables.

children.text: aṣṭākṣaraṃ ha vā ekaṃ gāyatryai padam
children.translated_text: One foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> indeed has eight syllables.
This, indeed, is that foot of hers.

children.text: sa yāvatīyaṃ trayī vidyā tāvaddha jayati yo 'syā etad evaṃ padaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: As far as this threefold knowledge extends, so much does he win who knows this foot of hers thus.
"<s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and <s>vyāna</s>" are eight syllables.

children.text: aṣṭākṣaraṃ ha vā ekaṃ gāyatryai padam
children.translated_text: One foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> indeed has eight syllables.
This, indeed, is that foot of hers.

children.text: sa yāvad idaṃ prāṇi tāvaddha jayati yo 'syā etad evaṃ padaṃ veda
children.translated_text: As far as this living world extends, so much does he win who knows this foot of hers thus.

children.text: athāsyā etad eva turīyaṃ darśataṃ padaṃ parorajā ya eṣa tapati
children.translated_text: Now this fourth, visible foot of hers, beyond the realm of dust, is that one which shines yonder.
For what is fourth is called <s>turīya</s> (the fourth).

children.text: darśataṃ padam iti dadṛśa iva hy eṣaḥ
children.translated_text: It is called the visible foot because this one is, as it were, seen.

children.text: parorajā iti sarvam u hyevaiṣa raja upary upari tapati
children.translated_text: It is called beyond the realm of dust because this one shines above and beyond all this realm.

children.text: evaṃ haiva śriyā yaśasā tapati yo 'syā etad evaṃ padaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: In just this way he shines with prosperity and fame who knows this foot of hers thus.

children.text: saiṣā gāyatryetasmiṃsturīye darśate pade parorajasi pratiṣṭhitā
children.translated_text: This <s>Gāyatrī</s> is established in that fourth, visible foot, in what is beyond the realm of dust.
That, indeed, is established in truth.
The eye indeed is truth.
For the eye indeed is truth.

children.text: tasmād yad idānīṃ dvau vivadamānāveyātam aham adarśam aham aśrauṣam iti
children.translated_text: Therefore, when two men who are disputing come now, one saying, "I saw it," and the other, "I heard it,"

children.text: ya evaṃ brūyād aham adarśam iti
children.translated_text: we would trust the one who said, "I saw it."
To him indeed we would give credence.

children.text: tad vai tat satyaṃ bale pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: That truth, indeed, is established in strength.
<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is strength.
That is established in <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: tasmād āhur balaṃ satyād ogīya iti
children.translated_text: Therefore they say, "Strength is more powerful than truth."
Thus indeed this <s>Gāyatrī</s> is established with reference to the self.
She indeed protected the <s>gayas</s> there.
The <s>prāṇas</s> indeed are the <s>gayas</s>.
Therefore she protected the <s>prāṇas</s> there.
Because she protected the <s>gayas</s>, therefore her name is <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: sa yām evāmūṃ sāvitrīm anvāhaiṣaiva sā
children.translated_text: That <s>Sāvitrī</s> which one recites, she is this very one.

children.text: sa yasmā anvāha tasya prāṇāṃs trāyate ||
children.translated_text: She protects the <s>prāṇas</s> of the one for whom he recites it.

children.text: tāṃ haitām eke sāvitrīm anuṣṭubham anvāhuḥ
children.translated_text: Some recite this <s>Sāvitrī</s> as an <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>.
Speech is the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>.
They think, "We are reciting this speech."
One should not do so.
One should recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> alone as the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.

children.text: yadi ha vā apy evaṃvid bahv iva pratigṛhṇāti na haiva tad gāyatryā ekaṃ cana padaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: Even if one who knows thus receives what seems to be much, it does not equal even one foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: sa ya imāṃstrīṃllokān pūrṇān pratigṛhṇīyāt so 'syā etat prathamaṃ padam āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: If someone were to receive these three worlds filled full, he would obtain this first foot of hers.

children.text: atha yāvatīyaṃ trayī vidyā yas tāvat pratigṛhṇīyāt so 'syā etad dvitīyaṃ padam āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: And if someone were to receive as much as this threefold knowledge extends, he would obtain this second foot of hers.

children.text: atha yāvad idaṃ prāṇi yas tāvat pratigṛhṇīyāt so 'syā etat tṛtīyaṃ padam āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: And if someone were to receive as much as this living world extends, he would obtain this third foot of hers.
