children.text: athāsyā etad eva turīyaṃ darśataṃ padaṃ parorajā ya eṣa tapati
children.translated_text: But this fourth, visible foot of hers, beyond the realm of dust, is that one which shines yonder.
It is not obtainable by anyone at all.
How, then, could one receive so much?
The approach to her in worship is this:

children.text: gāyatry asy ekapadī dvipadī tripadī catuṣpadi
children.translated_text: "<s>Gāyatrī</s>, you are one-footed, two-footed, three-footed, four-footed.
You are footless.
For you are not reached.

children.text: namas te turīyāya darśatāya padāya parorajase
children.translated_text: Homage to your fourth, visible foot beyond the realm of dust.
May that one not attain this."

children.text: yaṃ dviṣyād asāv asmai kāmo mā samardhīti vā
children.translated_text: Or, regarding one whom he hates, he may say, "May this desire not prosper for him."

children.text: na haivāsmai sa kāmaḥ samṛdhyate yasmā evam upatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: That desire does not prosper for the one against whom he approaches her in worship thus.
Or he may say, "I have attained that."

children.text: etaddha vai tajjanako vaideho buḍilam āśvatarāśvim uvāca yan nu ho tad gāyatrīvid abrūthāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Janaka Vaideha</s> said this to <s>Buḍila Āśvatarāśvi</s>: "Since, then, you used to say, 'I am a knower of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>,'
how is it that you carry burdens like an elephant?"

children.text: mukhaṃ hy asyāḥ samrāṇ na vidāṃcakareti hovāca
children.translated_text: "Because, Your Majesty, he did not understand her mouth," he said.
For her, fire itself is the mouth.

children.text: yadi ha vā api bahv ivāgnāv abhyādadhati sarvam eva tat saṃdahati
children.translated_text: If, indeed, they place even a great deal into a fire, it burns all of that up.

children.text: evaṃ haivaivaṃvid yady api bahv iva pāpaṃ kurute sarvam eva tat saṃpsāya śuddhaḥ pūto 'jaro 'mṛtaḥ sambhavati ||
children.translated_text: In just the same way, one who knows thus, even if he commits what seems like a great deal of evil, consumes all of it and becomes clean, purified, undecaying, and immortal.
The face of truth is covered by a golden vessel.

children.text: tat tvam pūṣann apāvṛṇu satyadharmāya dṛṣṭaye
children.translated_text: Uncover it, <s>Pūṣan</s>, so that one whose <s>dharma</s> is truth may see.

children.text: pūṣann ekarṣe yama sūrya prājāpatya vyūha raśmīn samūha tejaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pūṣan</s>, sole seer, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, child of <s>Prajāpati</s>, spread out your rays; gather up your radiance.

children.text: yat te rūpaṃ kalyāṇatamam tat te paśyāmi yo 'sāvasau puruṣaḥ so 'ham asmi
children.translated_text: That form of yours which is most auspicious, that form of yours I behold. The person who is yonder, he am I.

children.text: vāyur anilam amṛtam athedaṃ bhasmāntaṃ śarīram
children.translated_text: Let the breath go to the immortal wind; then this body ends in ashes.

children.text: oṃ krato smara kṛtaṃ smara krato smara kṛtaṃ smara
children.translated_text: Oṃ. O resolve, remember; remember what has been done. O resolve, remember; remember what has been done.

children.text: agne naya supathā rāye 'smān viśvāni deva vayunāni vidvān
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, lead us by the good path to prosperity, O god, knowing all the ways.

children.text: yuyodhy asmajjuhurāṇam eno bhūyiṣṭhāṃ te namauktiṃ vidhema ||
children.translated_text: Remove from us the crooked sin; to you we shall offer the fullest utterance of homage.

children.text: yo ha vai jyeṣṭhaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ ca veda jyeṣṭhaśca śreṣṭhaśca svānāṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: He who truly knows the eldest and the best becomes the eldest and the best among his own people.
<s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed the eldest and the best.
He becomes the eldest and the best among his own people,
and also among those among whom he wishes to become so,
he who knows thus.

children.text: yo ha vai vasiṣṭhāṃ veda vasiṣṭhaḥ svānāṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: He who truly knows the vasiṣṭha becomes vasiṣṭha among his own people.
Speech indeed is vasiṣṭha.
He becomes vasiṣṭha among his own people,
and also among those among whom he wishes to become so,
he who knows thus.

children.text: yo ha vai pratiṣṭhāṃ veda pratitiṣṭhati same
children.translated_text: He who truly knows the foundation stands firm on level ground.
He stands firm in difficult places.
The eye indeed is the foundation.

children.text: cakṣuṣā hi same ca durge ca pratitiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: For by the eye one stands firm both on level ground and in difficult places.
He stands firm on level ground; he stands firm in difficult places,
he who knows thus.

children.text: yo ha vai saṃpadaṃ veda saṃ hāsmai padyate yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate
children.translated_text: He who truly knows attainment has fulfilled for him whatever desire he desires.
The ear indeed is attainment.
For in the ear all these Vedas have come together.

children.text: saṃ hāsmai padyate yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate
children.translated_text: Whatever desire he desires is fulfilled for him,
he who knows thus.

children.text: yo ha vā āyatanaṃ vedāyatanaṃ svānāṃ bhavaty āyatanaṃ janānām
children.translated_text: He who truly knows the abode becomes an abode for his own people, an abode for others.
The mind indeed is the abode.
He becomes an abode for his own people, an abode for others,
he who knows thus.

children.text: yo ha vai prajātiṃ veda prajāyate ha prajayā paśubhiḥ
children.translated_text: He who truly knows generation is born forth with offspring and cattle.
Semen indeed is generation.
He is born forth with offspring and cattle,
he who knows thus.

children.text: te heme prāṇā ahaṃśreyase vivadamānā brahma jagmuḥ
children.translated_text: Then these vital powers, disputing over who was superior, went to <s>brahman</s>.
They said, 'Who among us is vasiṣṭha?'

children.text: taddhovāca yasmin va utkrānta idaṃ śarīraṃ pāpiyo manyate sa vo vasiṣṭha iti ||
children.translated_text: It said, 'The one upon whose departure this body is thought to be worse, he is your vasiṣṭha.'
Speech departed.

children.text: sā saṃvatsaraṃ proṣyāgatyovāca katham aśakata mad ṛte jīvitum iti
children.translated_text: After staying away for a year, she returned and said, 'How were you able to live without me?'

children.text: te hocuḥ yathākalā avadanto vācā prāṇantaḥ prāṇena paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa vidvāṃso manasā prajāyamānā retasaivam ajīviṣmeti
children.translated_text: They said, 'As mute people, not speaking with speech, but breathing with <s>prāṇa</s>, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, knowing with the mind, and procreating with semen, so we lived.'
Speech entered back in.
The eye departed.

children.text: tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣyāgatyovāca katham aśakata mad ṛte jīvitum iti
children.translated_text: After staying away for a year, it returned and said, 'How were you able to live without me?'

children.text: te hocuḥ yathāndhā apaśyantaś cakṣuṣā prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa vidvāṃso manasā prajāyamānā retasaivam ajīviṣmeti
children.translated_text: They said, 'As blind people, not seeing with the eye, but breathing with <s>prāṇa</s>, speaking with speech, hearing with the ear, knowing with the mind, and procreating with semen, so we lived.'
The eye entered back in.
The ear departed.

children.text: tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣyāgatyovāca katham aśakata mad ṛte jīvitum iti
children.translated_text: After staying away for a year, it returned and said, 'How were you able to live without me?'

children.text: te hocuḥ yathā badhirā aśṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā vidvāṃso manasā prajāyamānā retasaivam ajīviṣmeti
children.translated_text: They said, 'As deaf people, not hearing with the ear, but breathing with <s>prāṇa</s>, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, knowing with the mind, and procreating with semen, so we lived.'
The ear entered back in.
The mind departed.

children.text: tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣyāgatyovāca katham aśakata mad ṛte jīvitum iti
children.translated_text: After staying away for a year, it returned and said, 'How were you able to live without me?'

children.text: te hocuḥ yathā mugdhā avidvāṃso manasā prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa prajāyamānā retasaivam ajīviṣmeti
children.translated_text: They said, 'As bewildered people, not knowing with the mind, but breathing with <s>prāṇa</s>, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, and procreating with semen, so we lived.'
The mind entered back in.
Semen departed.

children.text: tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣyāgatyovāca katham aśakata mad ṛte jīvitum iti
children.translated_text: After staying away for a year, it returned and said, 'How were you able to live without me?'

children.text: te hocuḥ yathā klībā aprajāyamānā retasā prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa vidvāṃso manasaivam ajīviṣmeti
children.translated_text: They said, 'As impotent people, not procreating with semen, but breathing with <s>prāṇa</s>, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, and knowing with the mind, so we lived.'
Semen entered back in.

children.text: atha ha prāṇa utkramiṣyan yathā mahāsuhayaḥ saindhavaḥ paḍvīśaśaṅkhūnt saṃvṛhed evaṃ haivemān prāṇānt saṃvavarha
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>prāṇa</s> was about to depart, just as a great Sindh horse might pull up the tethering pegs, so indeed it pulled together these vital powers.
They said, 'Revered one, do not depart.

children.text: na vai śakṣyāmas tvad ṛte jīvitum iti
children.translated_text: We shall not be able to live without you.'
'Then make an offering to me,' it said.
'So be it,' they said.

children.text: sā ha vāg uvāca yad vā ahaṃ vasiṣṭhāsmi tvaṃ tad vasiṣṭho 'sīti
children.translated_text: Speech said, 'Since I am vasiṣṭha, you are therefore vasiṣṭha.'

children.text: yad vā ahaṃ pratiṣṭhāsmi tvaṃ tat pratiṣṭho 'sīti cakṣuḥ
children.translated_text: The eye said, 'Since I am the foundation, you are therefore the foundation.'

children.text: yad vā ahaṃ saṃpad asmi tvaṃ tat saṃpad asīti śrotram
children.translated_text: The ear said, 'Since I am attainment, you are therefore attainment.'

children.text: yad vā aham āyatanam asmi tvaṃ tad āyatanam asīti manaḥ
children.translated_text: The mind said, 'Since I am the abode, you are therefore the abode.'

children.text: yad vā ahaṃ prajātir asmi tvaṃ tat prajātir asīti retaḥ
children.translated_text: Semen said, 'Since I am generation, you are therefore generation.'

children.text: tasyo me kim annaṃ kiṃ vāsa iti
children.translated_text: 'What, then, is food for it, and what is its garment?'

children.text: yad idaṃ kiṃcā śvabhya ā kṛmibhya ā kīṭapataṅgebhyas tat te 'nnam
children.translated_text: 'Whatever there is, from dogs to worms, to insects and moths, that is your food.'
Water is its garment.

children.text: na ha vā asyānannaṃ jagdhaṃ bhavati nānannaṃ pratigṛhītaṃ ya evam etad anasyānnaṃ veda
children.translated_text: For one who knows thus this food of the eater, food eaten by him is not uneaten, nor is non-food received by him.

children.text: tad vidvāṃsaḥ śrotriyā aśiṣyanta ācāmanty aśitvācāmanti
children.translated_text: Knowing this, learned śrotriyas sip water before eating and sip water after eating.

children.text: etam eva tad annam anagnaṃ kurvanto manyante ||
children.translated_text: They think that thereby they make this very food not naked.

children.text: śvetaketur vā āruṇeyaḥ pañcālānāṃ pariṣadam ājagāma
children.translated_text: Now <s>Śvetaketu Āruṇeya</s> came to the assembly of the <s>Pañcālas</s>.
He came to <s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s> while he was being attended.
Looking up at him, he addressed him: "Boy?"
He replied, "Sir?"
"Have you been instructed by your father?"
He said, "Yes."

children.text: vettha yathemāḥ prajāḥ prayatyo vipratipadyantā3 iti
children.translated_text: "Do you know how these creatures, when they depart, go their separate ways?"
He said, "No."

children.text: vettho yathemaṃ lokaṃ punar āpadyantā3 iti
children.translated_text: "Do you know how they return again to this world?"
He said again, "No."

children.text: vettho yathāsau loka evaṃ bahubhiḥ punaḥ punaḥ prayadbhir na saṃpūryatā3 iti
children.translated_text: "Do you know why that world is not filled up, though many go to it again and again?"
He said again, "No."

children.text: vettho yatithyām āhutyāṃ hutāyām āpaḥ puruṣavāco bhūtvā samutthāya vadantī3 iti
children.translated_text: "Do you know at which oblation, when it has been offered, waters rise up, become human-voiced, and speak?"
He said again, "No."

children.text: vettho devayānasya vā pathaḥ pratipadaṃ pitṛyāṇasya vā
children.translated_text: "Do you know the approach to the path of the devayāna (path of the gods) or of the pitṛyāṇa (path of the ancestors),

children.text: yat kṛtvā devayānaṃ vā panthānaṃ pratipadyante pitṛyāṇaṃ vā
children.translated_text: that is, by doing what people enter upon the path of the gods or the path of the ancestors?

children.text: api hi na ṛṣer vacaḥ śrutaṃ dve sṛtī aśṛṇavaṃ pitṝṇām ahaṃ devānām uta martyānām
children.translated_text: For has not the saying of the seer been heard: 'I have heard of two courses, of the ancestors and of the gods, and also of mortals.

children.text: tābhyām idaṃ viśvam ejat sameti yad antarā pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ceti
children.translated_text: By those two all this moving world comes together, whatever is between father and mother?'

children.text: nāham ata ekaṃ cana vedeti hovāca ||
children.translated_text: He said, "I do not know even one of these."
Then he invited him to stay.
Disregarding the lodging, the boy ran away.
He came to his father.

children.text: taṃ hovāca iti vāva kila no bhavān purānuśiṣṭān avoca iti
children.translated_text: He said to him, "Did Your Reverence not previously say that we had been instructed?"
"How so, intelligent one?"
"A kinsman of the royal class asked me five questions,
and I did not know even one of them."
"What were they?"
He recited the opening words of them as follows.

children.text: sa hovāca tathā nas tvaṃ tata jānīthā yathā yad ahaṃ kiṃca veda sarvam ahaṃ tat tubham avocam
children.translated_text: He said, "Dear boy, you know us in this way: whatever I know at all, I have told all of that to you.
But go there.
Having approached him, we shall live as students in brahmacarya (discipline of sacred study)."
"Your Reverence himself should go," he said.

children.text: sa ājagāma gautamo yatra pravāhaṇasya jaivaler āsa
children.translated_text: So <s>Gautama</s> came to where <s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s> was.
For him he had a seat brought and water fetched.
Then he made an arghya (honor-offering) for him.

children.text: taṃ hovāca varaṃ bhagavate gautamāya dadma iti ||
children.translated_text: He said to him, "We give a boon to the revered <s>Gautama</s>."

children.text: sa hovāca pratijñato ma eṣa varaḥ
children.translated_text: He said, "This boon has been promised to me.

children.text: yāṃ tu kumārasyānte vācam abhāṣathās tāṃ me brūhīti ||
children.translated_text: Tell me the speech that you spoke in the presence of the boy."

children.text: sa hovāca daiveṣu vai gautama tad vareṣu
children.translated_text: He said, "That is among divine boons, <s>Gautama</s>.
Ask for human things."

children.text: sa hovāca vijñāyate hāstihiraṇyasyāpāttaṃ goaśvānāṃ dāsīnāṃ pravārāṇāṃ paridhānasya
children.translated_text: He said, "There is clearly acquisition of elephants and gold, of cattle and horses, of female servants, cloaks, and garments.

children.text: mā no bhavān bahor anantasyāparyantasyābhyavadānyo bhūd iti
children.translated_text: May Your Reverence not be ungenerous toward us concerning what is great, endless, and boundless."
"You seek by the proper approach, <s>Gautama</s>," he said.
"I approach Your Reverence as a pupil," he said.
Formerly, indeed, people used to approach merely by speech.
So, having declared his approach, he stayed.

children.text: sa hovāca tathā nas tvam gautama māparādhās tava ca pitāmahāḥ
children.translated_text: He said, "In that case, <s>Gautama</s>, do not fault us, nor let your forefathers fault us,

children.text: yatheyaṃ vidyetaḥ pūrvaṃ na kasmiṃścana brāhmaṇa uvāsa
children.translated_text: because before this this knowledge had not dwelt in any brāhmaṇa.
But I shall tell it to you.

children.text: ko hi tvaivaṃ bruvantam arhati pratyākhyātum iti ||
children.translated_text: For who could refuse one who speaks as you do?"
"That world, <s>Gautama</s>, is indeed a fire.
Its fuel is the sun itself.
The rays are the smoke.
Day is the flame.
The directions are the coals.
The intermediate directions are the sparks.

children.text: tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ śraddhāṃ juhvati
children.translated_text: In this fire the gods offer śraddhā (faith).
From that oblation King <s>Soma</s> arises.
Parjanya (the rain-cloud), <s>Gautama</s>, is indeed a fire.
Its fuel is the year itself.
The clouds are the smoke.
Lightning is the flame.
The thunderbolt is the coals.
The thunderclaps are the sparks.

children.text: tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ somaṃ rājānaṃ juhvati
children.translated_text: In this fire the gods offer King <s>Soma</s>.
From that oblation rain arises.
This world, <s>Gautama</s>, is indeed a fire.
Its fuel is the earth itself.
Fire is the smoke.
Night is the flame.
The moon is the coals.
The stars are the sparks.

children.text: tasminn etasminn agnau devā vṛṣṭiṃ juhvati
children.translated_text: In this fire the gods offer rain.
From that oblation food arises.
A man, <s>Gautama</s>, is indeed a fire.
His opened mouth is the fuel.
The breath is the smoke.
Speech is the flame.
The eye is the coals.
The ear is the sparks.

children.text: tasminn etasminn agnau devā annaṃ juhvati
children.translated_text: In this fire the gods offer food.
From that oblation semen arises.
A woman, <s>Gautama</s>, is indeed a fire.
Her womb-place is the fuel.
The hairs are the smoke.
The yoni (generative organ) is the flame.
What he does inside are the coals.
The pleasures are the sparks.

children.text: tasminn etasminn agnau devā reto juhvati
children.translated_text: In this fire the gods offer semen.
From that oblation a person arises.
He lives as long as he lives.
Then, when he dies,
they carry him to the fire.
For him fire itself becomes the fire.
Fuel is the fuel.
Smoke is the smoke.
Flame is the flame.
Coals are the coals.
Sparks are the sparks.

children.text: tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ puruṣaṃ juhvati
children.translated_text: In this fire the gods offer the person.
From that oblation a person of radiant color arises.

children.text: te ya evam etad vidur ye cāmī araṇye śraddhāṃ satyam upāsate te 'rcir abhisaṃbhavanti
children.translated_text: Those who know this, and those there in the forest who worship śraddhā (faith) and truth, go to the flame.
From the flame they go to day.
From day they go to the brightening fortnight.

children.text: āpūryamāṇapakṣād yān ṣaṇ māsān udaṅṅ āditya eti
children.translated_text: from the waxing fortnight to the six months during which the sun goes north;
from the months to the <s>devaloka</s> (world of the gods);
from the world of the gods to the sun;
from the sun to lightning.

children.text: tān vaidyutān puruṣo mānasa etya brahmalokān gamayati
children.translated_text: A mind-born person comes to those who have reached lightning and leads them to the worlds of <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: te teṣu brahmalokeṣu parāḥ parāvato vasanti
children.translated_text: In those worlds of <s>brahman</s> they dwell in supreme, farthest regions.
For them there is no return.

children.text: atha ye yajñena dānena tapasā lokāñjayanti te dhūmam abhisaṃbhavanti
children.translated_text: Now those who win worlds by sacrifice, giving, and austerity pass into smoke;
from smoke to night;
from night to the waning fortnight;

children.text: apakṣīyamāṇapakṣād yān ṣaṇ māsān dakṣiṇāditya eti
children.translated_text: from the waning fortnight to the six months during which the sun goes south;
from the months to the <s>pitṛloka</s> (world of the ancestors);
from the world of the ancestors to the moon.
Having reached the moon, they become food.

children.text: tāṃs tatra devā yathā somaṃ rājānam āpyāyasvāpakṣīyasvety evam enāṃstatra bhakṣayanti
children.translated_text: There the gods consume them, just as they consume King <s>Soma</s>, saying, 'Swell up; diminish,' and so they consume these there.

children.text: teṣāṃ yadā tat paryavaity athemam evākāśam abhiniṣpadyante
children.translated_text: When that comes to an end for them, then they pass forth into this very space;
from space to wind;
from wind to rain;
from rain to the earth.
Having reached the earth, they become food.

children.text: te punaḥ puruṣāgnau hūyante tato yoṣāgnau jāyante
children.translated_text: They are again offered in the fire of man; from there they are born in the fire of woman.
Rising again toward the worlds, they revolve onward in just this way.

children.text: atha ya etau panthānau na vidus te kīṭāḥ pataṅgā yad idaṃ dandaśūkam ||
children.translated_text: But those who do not know these two paths become worms, insects, and whatever biting creatures there are here.

children.text: sa yaḥ kāmayeta mahat prāpnuyām ity udagayana āpūryamāṇapakṣasya puṇyāhe dvādaśāham upasadvratī bhūtvaudumbare kaṃse camase vā sarvauṣadhaṃ phalānīti saṃbhṛtya parisamuhya parilipyāgnim upasamādhāya paristīryāvṛtājyaṃ saṃskṛtya puṃsā nakṣatreṇa manthaṃ saṃnīya juhoti
children.translated_text: Now, if a man should desire, 'May I attain greatness,' during the northern course, on an auspicious day of the waxing fortnight, after becoming one who observes the <s>upasad</s> vow for twelve days, having collected all herbs and fruits in an udumbara bowl or cup, having swept and smeared the place, established the fire, spread the sacred grass, prepared the clarified butter in the prescribed way, and mixed the <s>mantha</s> under a male constellation, he offers.

children.text: yāvanto devās tvayi jātavedas tiryañco ghnanti puruṣasya kāmān
children.translated_text: 'As many gods as are in you, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, who crosswise strike down a man's desires,

children.text: tebhyo 'haṃ bhāgadheyaṃ juhomi te mā tṛptāḥ sarvaiḥ kāmais tarpayantu svāhā
children.translated_text: to them I offer a share. Satisfied, may they satisfy me with all desires. Svāhā.'
'You who lie crosswise, saying, I am the upholder,

children.text: tāṃ tvā ghṛtasya dhārayā yaje saṃrādhanīm ahaṃ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: you I worship with a stream of ghee, as the one who brings success. Svāhā.'

children.text: jyeṣṭhāya svāhā śreṣṭhāya svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To the eldest, svāhā; to the best, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: prāṇāya svāhā vasiṣṭhāyai svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To <s>prāṇa</s>, svāhā; to the most excellent, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: vāce svāhā pratiṣṭhāyai svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To speech, svāhā; to foundation, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: cakṣuṣe svāhā saṃpade svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To the eye, svāhā; to prosperity, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: śrotrāya svāhāyatanāya svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To the ear, svāhā; to the abode, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: manase svāhā prajātyai svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To the mind, svāhā; to generation, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: retase svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati ||
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To semen, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: agnaye svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: somāya svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To <s>Soma</s>, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: bhūḥ svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, '<s>Bhūḥ</s>, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: bhuvaḥ svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, '<s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: svaḥ svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, '<s>Svaḥ</s>, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, '<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: brahmaṇe svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To <s>brahman</s>, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: kṣatrāya svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To <s>kṣatra</s> (royal power), svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: bhūtāya svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To what has been, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: bhaviṣyate svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To what will be, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: viśvāya svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To the universe, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: sarvāya svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To all, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: prajāpataye svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati ||
children.translated_text: Having offered into the fire, 'To <s>Prajāpati</s>, svāhā,' he pours the remaining flow into the <s>mantha</s>.
Then he touches it: 'You are whirling;
you are blazing;
you are full;
you are firmly set;
you are one assembly;
you are the <s>hiṃkāra</s> uttered;
you are the <s>hiṃkāra</s> being uttered;
you are the <s>udgītha</s> chant;
you are the <s>udgītha</s> being sung;
you are the summons heard;
you are the response to the summons;
you are kindled in the moist place;
you are expansive power;
you are sovereign power;
you are food;
you are light;
you are the conclusion;
you are the absorber.'
Then he raises it: 'We have praised you; magnify us.
For he is king, ruler, overlord.
May he make me king, ruler, overlord.'
Then he sips it.
'That excellent splendor of <s>Savitṛ</s>,

children.text: madhu vātā ṛtāyate madhu kṣaranti sindhavaḥ
children.translated_text: the winds blow honey for the one who follows <s>ṛta</s>; the rivers pour honey.
May the plants be honey-sweet for us.
<s>Bhūḥ</s>, svāhā.
We meditate on the radiance of the god.

children.text: madhu naktam utoṣaso madhumat pārthivaṃ rajaḥ
children.translated_text: Honey-sweet be night and dawn; honey-sweet the earthly realm.
May heaven, our father, be honey-sweet to us.
<s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, svāhā.
May he impel our thoughts.

children.text: madhumān no vanaspatir madhumān astu sūryaḥ
children.translated_text: May the forest tree be honey-sweet to us; may the sun be honey-sweet.
May the cows be honey-sweet for us.
<s>Svaḥ</s>, svāhā.
He recites the whole <s>Sāvitrī</s>,

children.text: sarvāś ca madhumatīr aham evedaṃ sarvaṃ bhūyāsaṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāheti antata ācamya pāṇī prakṣālya jaghanenāgniṃ prākśirāḥ saṃviśati
children.translated_text: and all the honey-verses. Saying at the end, 'May I myself become all this: <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>, svāhā,' he sips, washes his hands, and lies down behind the fire with his head toward the east.
In the morning he approaches the sun.
'You are the one lotus of the directions.
May I become the one lotus among human beings.'

children.text: yathetam etya jaghanenāgnim āsīno vaṃśaṃ japati ||
children.translated_text: Having returned in the same way, seated behind the fire, he recites the lineage.

children.text: taṃ haitam uddālaka āruṇir vājasaneyāya yājñavalkyāyāntevāsina uktvovāca api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcejjāyerañchākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s>, having taught this to his student <s>Vājasaneya Yājñavalkya</s>, said: 'Even if one were to sprinkle this on a dry stump, branches would be born and leaves would sprout.'

children.text: etam u haiva vājasaneyo yājñavalkyo madhukāya paiṅgyāyāntevāsina uktvovāca api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcejjāyerañchākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ||
children.translated_text: This indeed <s>Vājasaneya Yājñavalkya</s>, having taught to his student <s>Madhuka Paiṅgya</s>, said: 'Even if one were to sprinkle this on a dry stump, branches would be born and leaves would sprout.'

children.text: etam u haiva madhukaḥ paiṅgyaś cūlāya bhāgavittaye 'ntevāsina uktvovāca api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcejjāyerañchākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ||
children.translated_text: This indeed <s>Madhuka Paiṅgya</s>, having taught to his student <s>Cūla Bhāgavitti</s>, said: 'Even if one were to sprinkle this on a dry stump, branches would be born and leaves would sprout.'

children.text: etam u haiva cūlo bhāgavittir jānakaya āyaḥsthūṇāyāntevāsina uktvovāca api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcejjāyerañchākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ||
children.translated_text: This indeed <s>Cūla Bhāgavitti</s>, having taught to his student <s>Jānaki Āyaḥsthūṇa</s>, said: 'Even if one were to sprinkle this on a dry stump, branches would be born and leaves would sprout.'

children.text: etam u haiva jānakir āyaḥsthūṇaḥ satyakāmāya jābālāyāntevāsina uktvovāca api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcejjāyerañchākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ||
children.translated_text: This indeed <s>Jānaki Āyaḥsthūṇa</s>, having taught to his student <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>, said: 'Even if one were to sprinkle this on a dry stump, branches would be born and leaves would sprout.'

children.text: etam u haiva satyakāmo jābālo 'ntevāsibhya uktvovācāpi ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcejjāyerañchākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti
children.translated_text: This indeed <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>, having taught to his students, said: 'Even if one were to sprinkle this on a dry stump, branches would be born and leaves would sprout.'

children.text: tam etaṃ nāputrāya vānantevāsine vā brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: One should not tell this to anyone who is not a son or not a student.
There are four things made of udumbara wood.

children.text: audumbaraḥ sruva audumbaraś camasa audumbara idhma audumbaryā upamanthanyau
children.translated_text: The offering ladle is of udumbara wood, the cup is of udumbara wood, the fuel is of udumbara wood, and the two churning sticks are of udumbara wood.
There are ten cultivated grains.

children.text: vrīhiyavās tilamāṣā aṇupriyaṃgavo godhūmāś ca masūrāś ca khalvāś ca khalakulāś ca
children.translated_text: They are rice and barley, sesame and māṣa beans, aṇu and priyaṅgu, wheat and lentils, and khalva and khalakula.

children.text: tān piṣṭān dadhani madhuni ghṛta upasiñcati
children.translated_text: Having ground them, he sprinkles them into curds, honey, and ghee.
He offers from the clarified butter.
Of these beings, earth indeed is the essence.
Of earth, water is the essence.
Of waters, plants are the essence.
Of plants, flowers are the essence.
Of flowers, fruits are the essence.
Of fruits, the human being is the essence.
Of the human being, semen is the essence.

children.text: sa ha prajāpatir īkṣāṃcakre hantāsmai pratiṣṭhāṃ kalpayānīti sa striyaṃ sasṛje
children.translated_text: Then <s>Prajāpati</s> reflected, 'Come, let me prepare a support for this.' He created woman.
Having created her, he approached her from below.
Therefore one should approach a woman from below.

children.text: sa etaṃ prāñcaṃ grāvāṇam ātmana eva samudapārayat
children.translated_text: He caused this forward-facing pressing stone to rise up from his own self.
With it he emitted into her.
Her sexual place is the altar.
Her hairs are the sacrificial grass; her skin is the two pressing boards.
The two testicles are the kindled fires in the middle.

children.text: sa yāvān ha vai vājapeyena yajamānasya loko bhavati tāvān asya loko bhavati
children.translated_text: As great indeed as the world of the sacrificer becomes through the Vājapeya, so great does his world become.

children.text: ya evaṃ vidvān adhopahāsaṃ caraty āsāṃ strīṇāṃ sukṛtaṃ vṛṅkte
children.translated_text: The one who, knowing thus, practices intercourse from below wins the good deeds of these women.

children.text: atha ya idam avidvān adhopahāsaṃ caraty āsya striyaḥ sukṛtaṃ vṛñjate ||
children.translated_text: But the women win the good deeds of the one who practices intercourse from below without knowing this.

children.text: etaddha sma vai tad vidvān uddālaka āruṇir āha
children.translated_text: <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s>, knowing this, used to say precisely this.

children.text: etaddha sma vai tad vidvān nāko maudgalya āha
children.translated_text: <s>Nāka Maudgalya</s>, knowing this, used to say precisely this.

children.text: etaddha sma vai tad vidvān kumārahārita āha bahavo maryā brāhmanāyanā nirindriyā visukṛto 'smāllokāt prayanti ya idam avidvāṃso 'dhopahāsaṃ carantīti
children.translated_text: <s>Kumārahārita</s>, knowing this, used to say precisely this: 'Many mortal men born in brāhmaṇa families depart from this world without potency and without good deeds, namely those who practice this intercourse without knowing this.'

children.text: bahu vā idaṃ suptasya vā jāgrato vā retaḥ skandati ||
children.translated_text: Often, whether one is asleep or awake, semen spills forth.

children.text: tad abhimṛśed anu vā mantrayeta yan me 'dya retaḥ pṛthivīm askāntsīd yad oṣadhīr apy asarad yad apaḥ
children.translated_text: He should touch it and recite over it: 'What semen of mine has today spilled onto the earth, what has flowed to the plants, what to the waters,
that semen I take back here.

children.text: punar mām aitu indriyaṃ punas tejaḥ punar bhagaḥ
children.translated_text: May potency return to me, may splendor return, may fortune return.
May <s>Agni</s> and the sacred hearths be set again in their proper places.'

children.text: ityanāmikāṅguṣṭhābhyām ādāyāntareṇa stanau vā bhruvau vā nimṛjyāt ||
children.translated_text: Thus, taking it with the ring finger and thumb, he should rub it between the breasts or between the eyebrows.

children.text: atha yady udaka ātmānaṃ paśyet tad abhimantrayeta mayi teja indriyaṃ yaśo draviṇaṃ sukṛtam iti
children.translated_text: Then if he should see himself in water, he should recite over it: 'May splendor, potency, fame, wealth, and good deed be in me.'

children.text: śrīr ha vā eṣā strīṇāṃ yan malodvāsāḥ
children.translated_text: This indeed is the prosperity of women, that their garment is stained.
Therefore, approaching a woman with a stained garment, a woman endowed with fame, he should address her.

children.text: sā ced asmai na dadyāt kāmam enām avakrīṇīyāt
children.translated_text: If she does not grant herself to him, he may buy her off according to his desire.

children.text: sā ced asmai naiva dadyāt kāmam enāṃ yaṣṭyā vā pāṇinā vopahatyātikrāmet
children.translated_text: If she still does not grant herself to him, he may, according to his desire, strike her with a stick or with his hand and overcome her.

children.text: indriyena te yaśasā yaśa ādada iti
children.translated_text: He says, 'With potency and fame I take away your fame.'
She becomes without fame.

children.text: sā ced asmai dadyād indriyeṇa te yaśasā yaśa ādadhāmīti
children.translated_text: If she grants herself to him, he says, 'With potency and fame I place fame in you.'
They both become possessed of fame.

children.text: sa yām icchet kāmayeta meti tasyām arthaṃ niṣṭhāya mukhena mukhaṃ saṃdhāyopastham asyā abhimṛśya japet
children.translated_text: As for the woman whom he wishes, 'May she desire me,' after accomplishing his purpose with her, joining mouth to mouth, and touching her sexual place, he should murmur:
'From limb after limb you arise; from the heart you are born.

children.text: sa tvam aṅgakaṣāyo 'si digdhaviddhām iva mādayemām amūṃ mayīti ||
children.translated_text: You are the sap of the limbs; like one smeared and pierced, make this woman, so-and-so, mad with passion for me.'

children.text: atha yām icchen na garbhaṃ dadhīteti tasyām arthaṃ niṣṭhāya mukhena mukhaṃ saṃdhāyābhiprāṇyāpānyāt
children.translated_text: Then, as for the woman whom he wishes, 'May she not conceive,' after accomplishing his purpose with her and joining mouth to mouth, he should first breathe out and then breathe in.

children.text: indriyeṇa te retasā reta ādada iti
children.translated_text: He says, 'With your potency, with your seed, I take away the seed.'
She becomes without seed.

children.text: atha yām icched dadhīteti tasyām arthaṃ niṣṭhāya mukhena mukhaṃ saṃdhāyāpānyābhiprāṇyāt
children.translated_text: Then, as for the woman whom he wishes, 'May she conceive,' after accomplishing his purpose with her and joining mouth to mouth, he should first breathe in and then breathe out.
He says, 'With potency and seed I place seed in you.'
She does become pregnant.

children.text: atha yasya jāyāyai jāraḥ syāt taṃ ced dviṣyād āmapātre 'gnim upasamādhāya pratilomaṃ śarabarhiḥ stīrtvā tasminn etāḥ śarabhṛṣṭīḥ pratilomāḥ sarpiṣāktā juhuyāt
children.translated_text: Then, if a man's wife has a lover and he should hate him, he should place a fire in an unbaked vessel, spread reed grass in reverse order, and in it offer these reed darts, reversed and smeared with ghee.
He says, 'You have offered in my kindled fire.
I take away your <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, O so-and-so.'
You have offered in my kindled fire.
I take your sons and cattle, O so-and-so.
You have offered in my kindled fire.
I take your sacrifices and good works, O so-and-so.
You have offered in my kindled fire.
I take your hopes and prospects, O so-and-so.

children.text: sa vā eṣa nirindriyo visukṛto 'smāllokāt praiti yam evaṃvid brāhmaṇaḥ śapati
children.translated_text: The man whom a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who knows thus curses departs from this world bereft of powers and deprived of good works.
Therefore one should not seek dalliance with the wife of a <s>śrotriya</s> who knows thus.
For indeed one who knows thus becomes superior.

children.text: atha yasya jāyām ārtavaṃ vindet tryahaṃ kaṃse na pibet
children.translated_text: Now, when a man's wife finds her menstrual period, for three days she should not drink from a bronze vessel.
She should wear an unworn garment.
A low-born man or low-born woman should not touch her.
At the end of three nights, having bathed, she should pound rice grains.

children.text: sa ya icchet putro me śuklo jāyeta vedam anubruvīta sarvam āyur iyād iti kṣīraudanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām
children.translated_text: If he should desire, 'May a fair son be born to me; may he recite one <s>Veda</s>; may he live out his full lifespan,' then they should cook rice with milk, mixed with ghee, and both should eat it.
They will be able to beget such a one.

children.text: atha ya icchet putro me kapilaḥ piṅgalo jāyeta dvau vedāvanubruvīta sarvam āyur iyād iti dadhyodanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām
children.translated_text: Now if he should desire, 'May a tawny, reddish-brown son be born to me; may he recite two <s>Vedas</s>; may he live out his full lifespan,' then they should cook rice with curds, mixed with ghee, and both should eat it.
They will be able to beget such a one.

children.text: atha ya icchet putro me śyāmo lohitākṣo jāyeta trīn vedān anubruvīta sarvam āyur iyād iti udaudanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām
children.translated_text: Now if he should desire, 'May a dark son with red eyes be born to me; may he recite three <s>Vedas</s>; may he live out his full lifespan,' then they should cook rice with water, mixed with ghee, and both should eat it.
They will be able to beget such a one.

children.text: atha ya icched duhitā me paṇḍitā jāyeta sarvam āyur iyād iti tilaudanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām
children.translated_text: Now if he should desire, 'May a learned daughter be born to me; may she live out her full lifespan,' then they should cook rice with sesame, mixed with ghee, and both should eat it.
They will be able to beget such a one.

children.text: atha ya icchet putro me paṇḍito vigītaḥ samitiṃgamaḥ śuśrūṣitāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣitā jāyeta sarvān vedān anubruvīta sarvam āyur iyād iti māṃsaudanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām
children.translated_text: Now if he should desire, 'May a learned son be born to me, celebrated, going to assemblies, speaking speech that people wish to hear; may he recite all the <s>Vedas</s>; may he live out his full lifespan,' then they should cook rice with meat, mixed with ghee, and both should eat it.
They will be able to beget such a one.
With meat of an ox or of a bull.

children.text: athābhiprātar eva sthālīpākāvṛtājyaṃ ceṣṭitvā sthālīpākasyopaghātaṃ juhoty agnaye svāhānumataye svāhā devāya savitre satyaprasavāya svāheti
children.translated_text: Then, early in the morning, having prepared ghee according to the procedure of the pot-cooked offering, he offers a portion of the pot-cooked food: 'To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā; to <s>Anumati</s>, svāhā; to the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, whose impulse is true, svāhā.'
Having offered, he takes it out and eats.
After eating, he gives it to the other one.

children.text: prakṣālya pāṇī udapātraṃ pūrayitvā tenaināṃ trir abhyukṣati
children.translated_text: Having washed the hands and filled a water vessel, with it he sprinkles her three times.
'Rise from here, O <s>Viśvāvasu</s>; seek another woman, one already mature.
Unite the wife together with her husband.'

children.text: athainām abhipadyate amo 'ham asmi sā tvam
children.translated_text: Then he approaches her: 'I am <s>ama</s>; you are <s>sā</s>.
You are <s>sā</s>; I am <s>ama</s>.
I am the <s>Sāman</s>; you are the <s>Ṛc</s>.
I am heaven; you are earth.

children.text: tāv ehi saṃrabhāvahai saha reto dadhāvahai
children.translated_text: Come, let us two embrace; together let us deposit seed.
For wealth, for a male, for a son.'

children.text: athāsyā ūrū vihāpayati vijihīthāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī iti
children.translated_text: Then he causes her thighs to spread, saying, 'Let heaven and earth open apart.'

children.text: tasyām arthaṃ niṣṭhāya mukhena mukhaṃ saṃdhāya trir enām anulomām anumārṣṭi
children.translated_text: Having fixed his purpose in her, joining mouth with mouth, he strokes her three times along the grain.

children.text: viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatu tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi piṃśatu
children.translated_text: 'May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb; may <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> shape the forms.

children.text: āsiñcatu prajāpatir dhātā garbhaṃ dadhātu te
children.translated_text: May <s>Prajāpati</s> pour in; may <s>Dhātṛ</s> place an embryo in you.

children.text: garbhaṃ dhehi sinīvāli garbhaṃ dhehi pṛthuṣṭuke
children.translated_text: Place the embryo, O <s>Sinīvālī</s>; place the embryo, O <s>Pṛthuṣṭukā</s>.

children.text: garbhaṃ te aśvinau devāv ādhattāṃ puṣkarasrajau ||
children.translated_text: May the two divine <s>Aśvins</s>, lotus-garlanded, set the embryo in you.
The golden fire-sticks with which the <s>Aśvins</s> churned forth,

children.text: taṃ te garbhaṃ havāmahe daśame māsi sūtaye
children.translated_text: that embryo of yours we invoke for birth in the tenth month.

children.text: yathāgnigarbhā pṛthivī yathā dyaur aindreṇa garbhiṇī
children.translated_text: As the earth is pregnant with fire, as heaven is pregnant through <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: vāyur diśāṃ yathā garbha evaṃ garbhaṃ dadhāmi te 'sāviti ||
children.translated_text: as wind is the embryo of the directions, so I place an embryo in you, O so-and-so.'
When she is about to give birth, he sprinkles her with waters.
'As the wind stirs a lotus pond on every side,

children.text: evā te garbha ejatu sahāvaitu jarāyuṇā
children.translated_text: so may your embryo stir; may it come down together with the afterbirth.
This pen of <s>Indra</s> has been made, with bolt and enclosure.

children.text: tam indra nirjahi garbheṇa sāvarāṃ saheti ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Indra</s>, drive that out, together with the child and its covering.'

children.text: jāte 'gnim upasamādhāyāṅka ādhāya kaṃse pṛṣadājyaṃ saṃnīya pṛṣadājyasyopaghātaṃ juhoti
children.translated_text: When the child is born, having set up the fire, placed him on his lap, and poured <s>pṛṣadājya</s> (curds mixed with ghee) into a bronze vessel, he offers a portion of the <s>pṛṣadājya</s>.
'May I prosper here a thousandfold, growing in my own house.

children.text: asyopasandyāṃ mā chaitsīt prajayā ca paśubhiś ca svāhā
children.translated_text: May this one's continuity not be cut off, with offspring and with cattle, svāhā.

children.text: mayi prāṇāṃs tvayi manasā juhomi svāhā
children.translated_text: In me I offer the breaths; in you, with the mind, svāhā.

children.text: yat karmaṇātyarīricam yad vā nyūnam ihākaram
children.translated_text: Whatever I have overdone by the rite, or whatever deficiency I have made here,

children.text: agniṣṭat sviṣṭakṛd vidvān sviṣṭaṃ suhutaṃ karotu naḥ svāheti ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Agni</s>, the knowing <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, make it well-performed and well-offered for us, svāhā.'

children.text: athāsya dakṣiṇaṃ karṇam abhinidhāya vāg vāg iti triḥ
children.translated_text: Then, placing himself near his right ear, he says three times, 'Speech, speech.'

children.text: atha dadhi madhu ghṛtaṃ saṃnīyānantarhitena jātarūpeṇa prāśayati
children.translated_text: Then, mixing curds, honey, and ghee, he feeds him by means of unalloyed gold.

children.text: bhūs te dadhāmi bhuvas te dadhāmi svas te dadhāmi bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ sarvaṃ tvayi dadhāmīti ||
children.translated_text: 'I place <s>bhūḥ</s> in you; I place <s>bhuvaḥ</s> in you; I place <s>svaḥ</s> in you; I place <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>, the whole, in you.'
Then he gives him a name: 'You are <s>Veda</s>.'

children.text: tad asyaitad guhyam eva nāma bhavati ||
children.translated_text: This becomes his secret name.

children.text: athainaṃ mātre pradāya stanaṃ prayacchati yas te stanaḥ śaśayo yo mayobhūr yo ratnadhā vasuvid yaḥ sudatraḥ
children.translated_text: Then, giving him to the mother, he offers the breast: 'That breast of yours, which lies ready, which brings delight, which bestows treasure, finds wealth, and is generous,

children.text: yena viśvā puṣyasi vāryāṇi sarasvati tam iha dhātave kar iti ||
children.translated_text: with which you nourish all desirable things, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, make that here for nursing.'

children.text: athāsya mātaram abhimantrayate ilāsi maitrāvaruṇī vīre vīram ajījanat
children.translated_text: Then he addresses his mother with a mantra: 'You are <s>Ilā</s>, daughter of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>; from a hero you have borne a hero.

children.text: sā tvaṃ vīravatī bhava yāsmān vīravato 'karad iti
children.translated_text: May you be rich in heroes, you who have made us rich in heroes.'

children.text: taṃ vā etam āhuḥ atipitā batābhūḥ
children.translated_text: Of such a son they say, 'Ah, you have surpassed your father!
Ah, you have surpassed your grandfather!

children.text: paramāṃ bata kāṣṭhāṃ prāpa śriyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena
children.translated_text: Ah, he has reached the highest limit in prosperity, fame, and brahmanic radiance,'

children.text: ya evaṃvido brāhmaṇasya putro jāyata iti ||
children.translated_text: when a son is born to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who knows thus.
Now the lineage.
<s>Pautimāṣīputra</s> from <s>Kātyāyanīputra</s>.
<s>Kātyāyanīputra</s> from <s>Gautamīputra</s>.
<s>Gautamīputra</s> from <s>Bhāradvājīputra</s>.
<s>Bhāradvājīputra</s> from <s>Pārāśarīputra</s>.
<s>Pārāśarīputra</s> from <s>Aupasvastīputra</s>.
<s>Aupasvastīputra</s> from <s>Pārāśarīputra</s>.
<s>Pārāśarīputra</s> from <s>Kātyāyanīputra</s>.
<s>Kātyāyanīputra</s> from <s>Kauśikīputra</s>.
<s>Kauśikīputra</s> from both <s>Ālambīputra</s> and <s>Vaiyāghrapadīputra</s>.
<s>Vaiyāghrapadīputra</s> from both <s>Kāṇvīputra</s> and <s>Kāpīputra</s>.
<s>Kāpīputra</s>.
From <s>Ātreyīputra</s>.
<s>Ātreyīputra</s> from <s>Gautamīputra</s>.
<s>Gautamīputra</s> from <s>Bhāradvājīputra</s>.
<s>Bhāradvājīputra</s> from <s>Pārāśarīputra</s>.
<s>Pārāśarīputra</s> from <s>Vātsīputra</s>.
<s>Vātsīputra</s> from <s>Pārāśarīputra</s>.
<s>Pārāśarīputra</s> from <s>Vārkāruṇīputra</s>.
<s>Vārkāruṇīputra</s> from <s>Vārkāruṇīputra</s>.
<s>Vārkāruṇīputra</s> from <s>Ārtabhāgīputra</s>.
<s>Ārtabhāgīputra</s> from <s>Śauṅgīputra</s>.
<s>Śauṅgīputra</s> from <s>Sāṃkṛtīputra</s>.
<s>Sāṃkṛtīputra</s> from <s>Ālambāyanīputra</s>.
<s>Ālambāyanīputra</s> from <s>Ālambīputra</s>.
<s>Ālambīputra</s> from <s>Jāyantīputra</s>.
<s>Jāyantīputra</s> from <s>Māṇḍūkāyanīputra</s>.
<s>Māṇḍūkāyanīputra</s> from <s>Māṇḍūkīputra</s>.
<s>Māṇḍūkīputra</s> from <s>Śāṇḍilīputra</s>.
<s>Śāṇḍilīputra</s> from <s>Rāthītarīputra</s>.
<s>Rāthītarīputra</s> from <s>Bhālukīputra</s>.
<s>Bhālukīputra</s> from the two <s>Krauñcikīputras</s>.
The two <s>Krauñcikīputras</s> from <s>Vaidabhṛtīputra</s>.
<s>Vaidabhṛtīputra</s> from <s>Kārśakeyīputra</s>.
<s>Kārśakeyīputra</s> from <s>Prācīnayogīputra</s>.
<s>Prācīnayogīputra</s> from <s>Sāñjīvīputra</s>.
<s>Sāñjīvīputra</s> from <s>Prāśnīputra</s>, the pupil of <s>Āsuri</s>.
<s>Prāśnīputra</s> from <s>Āsurāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Āsurāyaṇa</s> from <s>Āsuri</s>.
<s>Āsuri</s>.
From <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> from <s>Uddālaka</s>.
<s>Uddālaka</s> from <s>Aruṇa</s>.
<s>Aruṇa</s> from <s>Upaveśi</s>.
<s>Upaveśi</s> from <s>Kuśri</s>.
<s>Kuśri</s> from <s>Vājaśravas</s>.
<s>Vājaśravas</s> from <s>Jīhvāvant Bādhyoga</s>.
<s>Jīhvāvant Bādhyoga</s> from <s>Asita Vārṣagaṇa</s>.
<s>Asita Vārṣagaṇa</s> from <s>Harita Kaśyapa</s>.
<s>Harita Kaśyapa</s> from <s>Śilpa Kaśyapa</s>.
<s>Śilpa Kaśyapa</s> from <s>Kaśyapa Naidhruvi</s>.
<s>Kaśyapa Naidhruvi</s> from <s>Vāc</s> (Speech).
<s>Vāc</s> from <s>Ambhiṇī</s>.
<s>Ambhiṇī</s> from <s>Āditya</s>.
From <s>Āditya</s> these white <s>yajus</s> formulas are taught by <s>Vājasaneya Yājñavalkya</s>.
The same up to <s>Sāñjīvīputra</s>.
<s>Sāñjīvīputra</s> from <s>Māṇḍūkāyani</s>.
<s>Māṇḍūkāyani</s> from <s>Māṇḍavya</s>.
<s>Māṇḍavya</s> from <s>Kautsa</s>.
<s>Kautsa</s> from <s>Māhitthi</s>.
<s>Māhitthi</s> from <s>Vāmakakṣāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Vāmakakṣāyaṇa</s> from <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>.
<s>Śāṇḍilya</s> from <s>Vātsya</s>.
<s>Vātsya</s> from <s>Kuśri</s>.
<s>Kuśri</s> from <s>Yajñavacas Rājastambāyana</s>.
<s>Yajñavacas Rājastambāyana</s> from <s>Tura Kāvaṣeya</s>.
<s>Tura Kāvaṣeya</s> from <s>Prajāpati</s>.
<s>Prajāpati</s> from <s>Brahman</s>.
<s>Brahman</s>, the self-existent.
Homage to <s>Brahman</s>.
